Mahādeva said:
Listen attentively, O goddess, to the efficacy that destroys sin,
the primordial sacred field, O great goddess, which destroys all sin.
In the vicinity of glorious Meru, there is a peak adorned with jewels,
an abode of many wonders, crowded with numerous trees,
variegated with strange minerals, having platforms of pure crystal,
rich in the beauty of varied hues, resounding with hosts of seers,
frequented by deer and great elephants, filled with herds of elephants,
dense with clouds of spray rising from cascading waterfall waters,
variegated with carpets of blossoms from clusters of trees shaken by the wind,
its entire forest perfumed with the excellent fragrance of musk,
a place of pleasure in bower-cottages, a refuge of Siddhas and Vidyādharas,
resounding with the sweet melody of skilled Kinnara hosts.
In that exceedingly delightful forest, which adorns the whole region,
[stands] the palace named Vairāja belonging to Brahmā, the Supreme Lord.
There, resounding with the sweet sounds of singing by celestial maidens,
adorned with garlands of floral clusters draped from pārijāta trees,
echoing with the loud music struck up on many instruments,
resounding with diverse songs and instruments accompanied by tempo and rhythm,
supported by millions of pillars, adorned with spotless mirrors,
accompanied by manifold great spectacles endowed with tempo and rhythm,
adorned with the play and splendor of dance arrangements by apsarases,
is the assembly hall named Kāntimatī, bestowing delight upon the gods,
thronged with gatherings of seers, frequented by groups of sages,
resounding with the sound of the Veda chanted by twice-born [brahmins], conferring bliss.
Seated in it was the lord of speech, devoted to the worship of Śaṃkara,
the divine seer Sanatkumāra, the mind-born son of Brahmā.
Rising from among the sages, the sage Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana,
Vyāsa, son of Parāśara, having bowed down according to rule,
with hands folded in reverence, infused with devotion to Bhava,
with supreme joy, his body hair bristling and his face cheerful, inquired
about the māhātmya of Mahākāla, which destroys the delusion of living beings:
Vyāsa said:

O Lord, let the māhātmya of the sacred field of Mahākāla be told!
Why is it called a secret forest, a seat [of power], and also a barren land?

6.1.m: And because it is the abode of the mothers, for that reason it is called a seat (pīṭha).
Those who die are not born again; therefore it is remembered as a barren ground (ūṣara).
This is a secret, ever dear to the great-souled Śambhu as his sacred field.
Because a cremation ground is pleasing to spirits and exceedingly dear [to him],
the forest of Mahākāla, as well as Avimuktika,
Ekāmraka, Bhadrakāla, and Karavīravana,
Kolāgiri, as well as Kāśī, Prayāga, and Amareśvara,
and Bharatha, Kedāra, and the divine Rudramahālaya—
these are the divine cremation grounds ever dear to Rudra.
The Lord sports continuously in these sacred fields of perfections.
On earth Naimiṣa is an excellent sacred ford, and Puṣkara is the best of sacred fords;
Kurukṣetra is praised throughout even the three worlds.
Vārāṇasī is considered ten times more meritorious than Kurukṣetra;
ten times greater than that, O Vyāsa, is the excellent forest of Mahākāla.
Among all the sacred fords on this earth such as Prabhāsa,
Prabhāsa is an excellent sacred ford, the primordial sacred field of the bearer of the Pināka.
Śrīśaila is an excellent sacred ford, as is Devadāruvana;
even more excellent than that, O Vyāsa, meritorious Vārāṇasī is held to be.
Ten times greater than that is declared [to be this place], because it is the best of all sacred fords:
the Mahākālavana, secret, a field of perfected beings, and likewise a saline waste.
Others are somewhat secret, or cremation grounds, or saline wastes; // 5.1.1.40
but the Mahākālavana is celebrated for possessing all [these], O sage:
a cremation ground, a saline field, a seat of power, and indeed a forest. // 41
These five are not found together except in the city of Mahākāla. // 42

6.1.m:
Sanatkumāra said:
Formerly, when the single ocean had arrived and mobile and immobile things were destroyed,
there was no fire, no wind, no sun, no earth, no directions, no sky; // 1
no lunar mansions, no light, no heaven, no moon, and likewise no planets;
no gods, asuras, or gandharvas, no piśācas, serpents, or rākṣasas; // 2
neither lakes nor mountains, neither rivers nor oceans.
Everything was enveloped in darkness; nothing could be discerned. // 3
Then Mahākāla alone, for the sake of bestowing grace upon the worlds,
the Lord stood beholding all places throughout the quarters of the sky. // 4
For the sake of creation, that Mahākāla took Desire present in his hand;
upon the index finger of his right hand, he churned it without drying up. // 5
Becoming an embryo, a bubble, swollen by that momentum,
there arose a golden egg, exceedingly firm and perfectly spherical. // 6
Struck by his hand, it split into two great halves:
the lower portion is remembered as the earth; the upper as heaven endowed with stars. // 7
In the middle there then arose Brahmā, five-faced and four-armed.
Maheśvara, having approved of him, immediately directed him: // 8
"Perform diverse creation, O mighty-armed one, by my grace!"
Having spoken thus, the god vanished somewhere; Brahmā did not depart. // 9
Though urged to create, Brahmā meditated upon the god;
and while being contemplated by Brahmā for the sake of knowledge, the lord Bhava, // 5.1.2.10
beheld through the austerity of Brahmā, bestowed the Veda with its six limbs.
Even having obtained the Veda, he was unable for a long time to perform creation. // 11
He stood again in austerity to worship Bhava.
When he did not see the god, he then praised him with devotion: // 12
Brahmā said:
"Homage to Śiva, whose mind is pure sattva, whose blazing splendor transcends the three guṇas,
the maker of the six-limbed Veda and of me, the eye for perceiving the supreme nature! // 13
Homage to you who partake of rajas in the act of creation, who preside over sattva in the preservation of the universe,
who are magnified by tamas as the cause of destruction, to Śiva, the bestower of the bliss of liberation! // 14
Homage indeed to Śiva, who is beyond the primordial nature of all beings, whose form is the Supreme Self,
the producer of the intellect, ego, and mind of humans, the maintainer, whose form is the twenty-sixth principle! // 15
By whose forms as the elements, water, fire, ether, wind, moon, sun, and self this universe is pervaded—
homage to him, past, future, and present! // 16
Whatever splendors are here, whatever worlds, beings, future things, and causes
arise in creation and dissolve at destruction into whose Self, to him I bow!" // 17
Sanatkumāra said:
When Brahmā was thus praising him, O Vyāsa, the supreme Lord
spoke while remaining invisible: "O Brahmā, ask for a boon!" // 18
In his mind he chose Bhava as his son, out of pride.
Knowing what was in his mind, the Supreme Lord spoke to him: // 19
"Since you desire me in your mind as a son, O four-faced one,
therefore, for a certain reason, I shall cut off your head. // 5.1.2.20
Since that which should not be asked was asked, an amśā of mine, Nīlalohita,
will become Rudra your son, and he will destroy your splendor. // 21
Moreover, since I have been remembered with devotion by you with the feeling of being a father,
and since you made an inquiry into me as possessing the form of the supreme Brahman, // 22
therefore your name will be renowned in this world as 'Brahmā';
by that also you possess grandfathership, and hence you are indeed the Grandfather." // 23
Having thus received a curse and a boon, he undertook the creation of sons.
As he offered oblations into the fire born of his own splendor, sweat came forth upon him. // 24
As he wiped his forehead with a hand holding sacrificial twigs,
a single drop of blood fell from his sweat into the fire. // 25
That indeed became Nīlalohita, and he was Rudra by the command of Bhava.
Thereupon, having approached, the son emerged from his presence, // 26
five-faced, ten-armed, bearing a trident, bow, sword, and spear,
with fifteen eyes, fierce, having a snake as a sacred thread, // 27
bearing matted hair with the moon, wearing a garment of lion-skin.
Seeing him thus born, Brahmā then gave him a name: // 28
"You are named Nīlalohita, Bhava, Rudra, and the wielder of the Pināka."
Then creation proceeded from the creator, the Grandfather of the worlds. // 29
At first he generated seven mind-born [sons], Sanaka and others, then others:
Marīci, Dakṣa, and others, and Manu and others, the creators of offspring. // 5.1.2.30
Having made eight classes of gods, animals of five kinds,
and humans of one kind, he thus brought forth creation. // 31
The creation, beginning with the gods, having arisen, set aside even Brahmā,
and having bowed, they worshipped only Nīlalohita. // 32
Then Brahmā said to Rudra: "I have been rendered unworshipped by you;
you are worthy of worship by your own splendor, therefore go to the Himālaya." // 33
Nīlalohita said to him: "Indeed, I was not honored by you."
Then that Rudra departed to where the Lord Bhava was. // 34
Then Brahmā became foolish, puffed up with rajas;
he scorched the creation with his splendor, thinking: "It was made by me! // 35
There is no god equal to me, by whom creation has been expanded,
with gods, asuras, and gandharvas, filled with domestic animals, birds, and wild beasts." // 36

6.1.m:
Thus deluded, that five-faced Virañci became arrogant.
His eastern face, having a pleasant sound, was the promoter of the Sāmaveda; // 37
his second face was the promoter of the Ṛgveda;
Another [face] bore the Yajurveda, and the fourth was named Atharva[veda].
And along with their auxiliary and secondary branches, histories, / secret doctrines, and summaries,
he recites the Vedas with his fifth, upper-facing mouth.
Because of the splendor of that mouth of wondrous radiance, all the gods and asuras
did not shine, like a lamp at sunrise.
Even with their sons, they became agitated and bewildered in mind,
unable to approach, nor to look upon it for long, nor to retreat from that splendor.
Considering themselves as if overwhelmed, free from hatred,
all those gods deliberated for their own welfare:
“Let us go for refuge to the god [Śiva], stripped of radiance as we are by the brahma-splendor;
yet we do not know the place where he abides.
We shall see that terrible one here through devotion, not by any other means.”

6.1.m:
Having thus deliberated, those gods, with joined palms,
then composed a hymn of praise to the Great Lord with the highest excellence of tone:
The gods said:
“Homage to you, Lord of the gods of gods! O Maheśvara, homage, homage!
Fools that we are, we do not comprehend your supreme, matchless greatness,
by union with which you are the supreme Brahman, eternal among beings,
the foundation of all beings, the cause in the creation of all.
And you bear the moon, the sun, and fire abiding within your eyes.
Merely by chanting your name creatures are freed from misfortune.
Characterized by earth, water, fire, moon, sun, space, and wind
are your forms, O Mahādeva, and by them this [all] is entirely pervaded.
The world, being spun around by you through the states of rajas, sattva, and tamas,
does not recognize you, O Lord of all, since you assume all forms.
The delusion that deludes the rulers of the gods, beginning with Brahmā,
you create, unbearable, at each recurring cycle of the ages.”
Sanatkumāra said:
Having granted visible darśana out of compassion for the gods,

with a gracious countenance and bowed down to by the gods,
dwelling together with the gods, the Great Lord,
thus being praised by celestial seers, ancestors, and humans,
remaining invisible, said this: “O gods, speak as you desire!”
The gods said:
“O Sthāṇu, we pray always for your direct darśana.
May a boon also be granted to us by you out of compassion.
Whatever great energy, splendor, and valor we had,
all that has been swallowed by Brahmā through the splendor of his fifth mouth.
All our radiances have perished; O Lord, through your grace,
O Maheśvara, act in such a way that it is restored as before.”
Sanatkumāra said:
Having appeared visibly, Śarva then indeed set forth;
he went to that place where he [Brahmā] was, the embodiment of passion and egoism.
The gods, praising the Lord of gods, surrounded him and sat down.
Brahmā, enveloped in darkness, did not recognize that the god had arrived.
Delighting the world with the splendor of tens of millions of suns,

6.1.m:
the Self of all, the creator of all, the sustainer of all was then seen.
Rudra, overpowering with his splendor the Grandfather
who was seated in the whole circle of the gods, stood before him, intoxicated with that [splendor].
And Brahmā’s mouth, overwhelmed by Rudra's splendor, did not shine,
just like the moon, though shedding bright rays at night, [does not shine] at sunrise.
Then, seeing his son, the eternal god Rudra, proud,
he greeted him with just his hand and spoke these smiling words;
Virūpākṣa replied to that Brahmā, as if laughing.
Since, enveloped in his own splendor, he did not know the supreme god,
therefore the Lord bearing the crescent moon let out a loud roar of laughter.
While all the gods were watching and listening, he uttered words.
Having confounded the Grandfather with that sound of boisterous laughter,
he, a mass of splendor resembling the moon, whose eyes are the moon, sun, and fire,
[severed] the fifth head of Brahmā with the tip of the nail of his left thumb.
severed it as a man would [sever] the core of a plantain tree with his fingernails.
And the Grandfather did not realize that his face was being cut off. // 66

6.1.m:
Stupefied therefore by the fiery splendor of Rudra, he did not bow down.
His severed head then rested thereafter in Rudra's hand. // 67
Together with the gods he saw the terrible [head], blazing exceedingly with fright.
Held by the fingernails at the end of Maheśvara's hand, the face shone // 68
like a second moon standing in the midst of the planetary circle.
Lifting it up with that skull, the moon-crested god danced, // 69
like Mount Kailāsa with the sun resting upon its summit.
Then, when the face was severed, the gods, delighted and thriving,
praised the god of gods, the bull-bannered bearer of the skull, with various hymns. // 5.1.2.70
The gods said:
Praise always to the skull-bearer, to Mahākāla, the conch-possessor, // 71
who is endowed with sovereignty and knowledge, the bestower of all enjoyments,
praise to the destroyer of arrogance, and to the one who comprises all gods! // 72
You are the maker of the dissolution of Time, and therefore indeed you are Mahākāla.
You pacify the sorrow of devotees, bringing an end to suffering; therefore you are pleasing. // 73
You also quickly bestow peace upon devotees; therefore you are remembered as Śaṃkara.

6.1.m:
Since you have cut off the head of Brahmā and also bear the skull, // 74
for that reason, O God, you are Kapālin; indeed you have been praised, be gracious to us!
Thus praised, Śaṃkara, his mind serene, raised up the gods; // 75
that Lord, an ocean of compassion, vanished right there.
Whose matted hair is illuminated by the rays of the crescent moon, where the celestial Gaṅgā melts into ripples of water to be gathered,
holding the white skull in a wreath at Rudra's side, he who conquered Brahmā, powerful and endowed with vast splendor, triumphs! // 76
Thus ends the second chapter, titled 'The Description of the Severing of the Head of Brahmā,' in the Avantīkṣetramāhātmya of the Fifth Avantīkhaṇḍa, in the Skandapurāṇa comprising eighty-one thousand verses. // 2
Sanatkumāra said:

6.1.s: chinne vaktre tato brahmā krodhena tamasā vṛtaḥ ..

6.1.m: Then, when the face was severed, Brahmā, enveloped by anger and darkness,
took the sweat produced on his forehead and struck it upon the ground. // 1
From that sweat was born an ear-ringed hero with a bow, a great quiver,
and a thousand coats of armor, and he said: "What shall I do?" // 2
Brahmā said to him, pointing out Rudra with power:
"Let this wicked-minded one be slain so that he is not born again!" // 3
Having heard Brahmā's command, raising his bow behind him,
he set out after the Great Lord, holding arrows, filled with great fury. // 4
Seeing that fierce man, Bhava was astonished and went on,
holding divine arrows and a bow in his hand, advancing with swift strides. // 5
"He is exceedingly strong and should not be killed by me; he will become a friend of Viṣṇu.

6.1.s: anugrāhyo hyahaṃ tena sakhyārthaṃ tapasi sthitaḥ .. 6 ..
6.1.d: अनुग्राह्यो ह्यहं तेन सख्यार्थं तपसि स्थितः .. 6 ..
6.1.m: Indeed he should be favored by me, for he is engaged in austerity for friendship." // 6
Reflecting thus, the Lord also went to the hermitage of Viṣṇu,
having then bewildered that man, O brahmin, with the sound of a "huṃ!" // 7

6.1.s: prapātya ca tadā hṛṣṭaḥ krīḍāṃ kurvañjagatsthitau ..

6.1.m: And striking him down, delighted, sporting in the maintenance of the universe,
[he went] where the illustrious and majestic Nārāyaṇa was practicing austerity, // 8
invisible to all beings, the soul of the universe, the creator of the universe, the all-pervading Lord.
Arriving there, the three-eyed god saw Madhusūdana // 9
standing on one big toe upon the ground, engaged in supreme, unperturbed austerity,
wondrous, enveloped by the radiance of a thousand suns at the end of an era, // 5.1.3.10
the ancient Supreme Person, endowed with the support of merits.

6.1.s: dṛṣṭvā nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ bhikṣāṃ dehītyuvāca ha .. 11 ..
6.1.d: दृष्ट्वा नारायणं देवं भिक्षां देहीत्युवाच ह .. 11 ..
6.1.m: Seeing the god Nārāyaṇa, he said, "Give alms!" // 11
displaying the skull in front, ferocious and blazing like fire.
Beholding Rudra with the skull in his hand, Viṣṇu thought: // 12
"Who else could be a worthy beggar for the giving of alms right now?"
Resolving, "He is worthy," he offered his right arm. // 13
Knowing his inner thought, the moon-crested god pierced it with his trident.
Then a stream of blood flowed from the arm of the Lord; // 14
having the form of molten gold, pure like a flame of fire,
it fell into the skull, received by Śambhu. // 15
Straight, swift, and rapid, like a ray of the sun in the sky,
fifty yojanas long and ten yojanas in width, // 16
it flowed from Hari's arm for a thousand divine years.

6.1.s: kiyaṃtaṃ kālamīśo hi bhikṣāṃ jagrāha bhāvitaḥ .. 17 ..
6.1.d: कियंतं कालमीशो हि भिक्षां जग्राह भावितः .. 17 ..
6.1.m: Indeed, for some time the Lord, concentrated in thought, received the alms. // 17
given by Nārāyaṇa into the worthy vessel, the excellent vessel.

6.1.s: tato nārāyaṇaḥ prāha haraṃ paramidaṃ vacaḥ .. 18 ..
6.1.d: ततो नारायणः प्राह हरं परमिदं वचः .. 18 ..
6.1.m: Then Nārāyaṇa addressed these supreme words to Hara:

6.1.s: saṃpūrṇaṃ tava pātraṃ hi tato vai parameśvaraḥ ..

6.1.m: "Indeed, your vessel is full." Then the Supreme Lord,
Hara, hearing the speech of Hari that sounded like a raincloud,
whose eyes are the moon, sun, and fire, adorned with the crescent moon on his crest,
cast his gaze into the skull and looked at Janārdana with his three eyes.
Stirring with his finger, he said: "The skull is overflowing."
Hearing this speech, Hari withdrew the stream of blood.
Then from the side of Hari, the Lord with his own finger

6.1.s: divyaṃ varṣasahasraṃ ca dṛṣṭipātaṃ mamaṃtha vai .. 22 ..
6.1.d: दिव्यं वर्षसहस्रं च दृष्टिपातं ममंथ वै .. 22 ..
6.1.m: churned that blood with the cast of his gaze for a divine thousand years.

6.1.s: mathyamāne tato rakte kalalaṃ budbudaṃ kramāt ..
6.1.d: मथ्यमाने ततो रक्ते कललं बुद्बुदं क्रमात् ..
6.1.m: As the blood was churned, there arose in succession an embryo and a bubble,
and after that there appeared one wearing a diadem and holding a bow,
having a thousand arms and red eyes, repeatedly touching the bowstring,
with a quiver at his neck, shoulders like a bull, and wearing archer's finger-guards.
A man resembling Arjuna shone forth in the skull.

6.1.s: taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhagavānviṣṇuḥ prāha rudramidaṃ vacaḥ .. 25 ..
6.1.d: तं दृष्ट्वा भगवान्विष्णुः प्राह रुद्रमिदं वचः .. 25 ..
6.1.m: Seeing him, the blessed Viṣṇu addressed these words to Rudra:
"O Blessed One, who is this man who has manifested in the skull?"
Hearing Hari's question, the Lord said to him: "Listen, O Hari!
This man is named Nara, the foremost among knowers of supreme weapons.
Since he was addressed by you as 'Nara', he shall therefore be Nara.
Both Nara and Nārāyaṇa shall become renowned in the age,
in battle, in the tasks of the gods, and in the protection of the worlds.
O Nārāyaṇa, this Nara will be your friend;
he will be a great sage companion for you when you are alone in battle and in austerity.
His brilliance will exist in the world to test experiential knowledge.
This divine fifth head of Brahmā possesses supreme splendour;

6.1.s: tejasā brahmaṇo dīpto bhujasya tava śoṇitāt ..
6.1.d: तेजसा ब्रह्मणो दीप्तो भुजस्य तव शोणितात् ..
6.1.m: illuminated by the splendour of Brahmā, from the blood of your arm,
and from the casting of my gaze—since these three splendours are combined,
born from their union, he will cause distress to enemies.
Those who will be invincible and difficult to conquer for you and others,
and terrifying to Śakra and the foes of the immortals—he will terrify precisely them."
When Śambhu had spoken thus, amazed by his splendour,
Hari also, right there, praised Hara and Keśava:

6.1.s: namo hara hare tubhyaṃ namaḥ śaṃkara viṣṇave .. 34 ..
6.1.d: नमो हर हरे तुभ्यं नमः शंकर विष्णवे .. 34 ..
6.1.m: "Salutations to you, O Hara, O Hari! Salutations to Śaṃkara, to Viṣṇu!
Salutations to you who hold the trident in hand! Salutations to you who hold the sword in hand!
Homage, homage to you, the pure one! O Hṛṣīkeśa, salutations be to you!
Salutations be to the Lord of speech! Homage, homage to Śrīdhara!"

6.1.s: evaṃ stuvantaṃ taṃ bhaktyā kṛtāṃjali puṭaṃ naram.. 36 ..
6.1.d: एवं स्तुवन्तं तं भक्त्या कृतांजलि पुटं नरम्.. 36 ..
6.1.m: To that Nara who was thus praising with devotion, his hands joined in reverence,
quickly taking both his hands which were joined in reverence in that same manner,
and lifting him out of the skull, [Hara] spoke these words again:

6.1.s: ya eva puruṣo raudro brahmaṇaḥ svedasaṃ bhavaḥ ..
6.1.d: य एव पुरुषो रौद्रो ब्रह्मणः स्वेदसं भवः ..
6.1.m: "That terrible being born of Brahmā's sweat,
who fell into a sleep of delusion at the sound of my hum roar—
awaken him quickly!" Having spoken thus, Hara vanished.

6.1.s: nārāyaṇasya pratyakṣaṃ bodhayitvā drutaṃ hi tam.. 39 ..
6.1.d: नारायणस्य प्रत्यक्षं बोधयित्वा द्रुतं हि तम्.. 39 ..
6.1.m: Having quickly awakened him before Nārāyaṇa's eyes

6.1.s: vāmapādena hatvā ca samuttasthau naro ruṣā ..
6.1.d: वामपादेन हत्वा च समुत्तस्थौ नरो रुषा ..
6.1.m: and struck him with his left foot, Nara stood up in anger.
A great battle took place between the two, the one born of sweat and the one born of blood,
making the entire earth resound with the twang of their drawn bows.
One piece of armour remained for the sweat-born one, and likewise two arms for the blood-born one.

6.1.s: evaṃ samena vai yuddhaṃ divyaṃ jātaṃ tu bhūtale ..
6.1.d: एवं समेन वै युद्धं दिव्यं जातं तु भूतले ..
6.1.m: Thus an equally matched divine battle took place on earth.
A thousand years less three, O good twice-born,
passed while the two, the sweat-born and the blood-born, were fighting, O sage.
The two-armed blood-born one, seeing the sweat-born one with only one piece of armour,
pierced that supreme man of Brahmā with the force of his arrows.
Madhusūdana, agitated, said this to Brahmā:
"O Brahmā, the exalted one belonging to you has been struck down by my Nara."
Hearing that, Brahmā, perturbed, spoke to Madhusūdana:
"O Hari, if my Nara is vanquished, in another birth..."
By him, gratified, Hari said: "It shall be so."

6.1.s: kṛtvā tayo raṇamapi nivārya tāvuvāca ha ..
6.1.d: कृत्वा तयो रणमपि निवार्य तावुवाच ह ..
6.1.m: Putting an end to their battle and stopping the two, he indeed said:
"Then in another birth, my Nara will be [born] in Kali [Yuga]."

6.1.s: tato mahāraṇe jāte tatrāhaṃ yojayāmi tam ..
6.1.d: ततो महारणे जाते तत्राहं योजयामि तम् ..
6.1.m: "Then, when a great battle arises, I shall appoint him there."
Then, having summoned Maheśvara and the Lord of Gods (Indra), Viṣṇu
said to them: "These two men, O Rudras, must be protected according to your power.
Born from sweat and born from blood, they are portions of yourself upon the earth.
Having become your own portions, they are to be directed by you upon the surface of the earth at the end of Dvāpara."
Then the Lord of Gods (Indra) spoke these sorrowful words to Viṣṇu:
"O Lord, in this manvantara, back when it was the Tretāyuga,
by your great form here, desiring the welfare of the son of the Sun,
the mighty-armed one named Vālin was struck down for the sake of Sugrīva.

6.1.s: tena duḥkhena tapto'haṃ nāhaṃ gṛhṇāmi te naram ..
6.1.d: तेन दुःखेन तप्तोऽहं नाहं गृह्णामि ते नरम् ..
6.1.m: Afflicted by that grief, I will not accept your man."
To the Lord of Gods who was refusing and stating another reason,
Viṣṇu said: "O Maghavan, to remove the burden of the earth,
I too shall take an incarnation in the mortal world, O mighty lord."
Then Śakra became delighted indeed by those words of Viṣṇu.
Having accepted the man, rejoiced, [he said]: "May your word be true!"

6.1.s: ityuktvā tu ravīndrau sa preṣayitvā ca tau punaḥ ..
6.1.d: इत्युक्त्वा तु रवीन्द्रौ स प्रेषयित्वा च तौ पुनः ..
6.1.m: Having said this, and having dismissed the sun and the moon,
the lotus-eyed one (Viṣṇu) went to Brahmā in the abode of Brahmā [and said]:
"O Brahmā, a detestable deed was done by you desiring to kill the Lord,
in that you, O lord of the gods of gods, addressed a man in anger.
For the purification of this sin, perform a supreme expiation.
Taking the triad of fires, O Brahmā, worship the agnihotra.
Let one indeed be the Gārhapatya, the second the Āhavanīya,
and the third the Dakṣiṇāgni; arrange them in three fire-pits.
Gratify yourself in the circular one, me in the one shaped like a bow,
and god Hara in the four-cornered one, with the names of the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman.

6.1.m:
Wishing to know that treasure of fiery splendor, the lord of all, Prajāpati [praised him]
with esoteric hymns from the Nirukta spoken in the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman.
Brahmā said:
Homage to you of sevenfold splendor, the supreme Self of the supreme;
homage to the counter-ear of wonders, to the treasury of splendor.
[Homage to you] who are the seed of cosmic existences, the deluder of delusion,
the darkness at the cycle of the yugas, and unbearable time after time.
O upward-faced one, homage to you, whose nature is sattva, whose nature is the earth;
from whose blazing flames water arises, O lord of water-born [lotuses], O mover in water;
whose eyes are like the blooming petals of a lotus, O water-god, O fire!
O you of dark beauty, you whose path is black [smoke], you who grant the path to heaven;
you whose practice is the sacrificial offering, whose form is the sacrifice, homage, homage to you!
O gold-wombed one, residing within the śamī tree, victory to you, eternal god!
O dispeller of darkness, great swallower, lover of one's own, destroyer of darkness,
O blazing radiant lord of the gods, O Citrabhānu, homage to you!
O fierce Vaiśvānara fire, upward-flaming purifier, all-pervading, / O Vibhāvasu, illustrious one, black-pathed one, homage, homage to you!

6.1.m:
Sanatkumāra said:
Thus praised at that time, that fire spoke these words to Brahmā:
“I am pleased with you, O Brahmā; your intended work will succeed.”
Thus addressed, Brahmā then bowed and spoke again:
“I desire to know, O lord, who you indeed are, O blessed one.”
He then said to Brahmā: “You are the Puruṣa, the Prajāpati.
My supreme form is unknowable; therefore, look upon me with [vision] fit for it.”
Then, through divine [vision], he saw the eternal blessed one,
the all-knowing creator of order, the Īśvara beyond existence and non-existence,
fire, sky, earth, the visible and invisible supreme abode,
the past, present, and future, the universe mobile and immobile.
The god continually creates, since the Lord consumes everything.
Then Prajāpati, with a hymn of great becoming and future glory,
praised the original god, ancient, unborn, and imperishable.
Then, having seen the god of intensely red color, Prajāpati,
who had arms and feet on every side, and faces and heads of fire on every side,

the guide of the manifest and unmanifest, bowing down with his own head, [said:]
“Look [upon me]; homage to you, whose self is the origin of the universe!
Earth, wind, space, and whatever else is the three worlds,
the lord of the worlds and non-worlds, and the universe mobile and immobile,
the creation of elements, the creation of beings, and likewise the creation of states of being—”
beholding of his own accord with his eye the one whose self consists of Brahmā's splendor,
[he saw] whatever collection of things exists, all that is immobile and mobile.
Thus praised at that time, that beginningless blessed Lord,
then the Lord (Īśa) said to Brahmā: “You have seen [reality] just as it is.
Now create all creatures, you who are full of modesty.
I am the maker; you are the imitator in causing the maintenance of the worlds.
Carry out this destiny that was created by me in the past.”
Thus addressed by the god of gods, Brahmā spoke these words:

Then Brahmā spoke to that fire at the end of the yuga,
touching it with his right and left hands as though soothing it with his speech:
“Bhṛgu and Aṅgiras shall be my sons, without a doubt;
in my very lineage here, having renowned deeds, you two shall be born.
Dividing the fire into two through him, the sacrifice of creation will take place.
May you two remain there on earth, devoted to giving.”
The two fires, brought together by Brahmā, were urged by Brahmā;
therefore, they should be produced in this manner by churning, according to ritual injunction.
Hence their union is recited there in the aśvattha tree within the womb of the śamī tree.
The Bhārgava and Āṅgirasa fires are spoken of as twofold and divine;

Thus, O Vyāsa, was this Nara born in a former birth;
thus did the fifth head of Brahmā come to be.
Whoever comprehends this incomparable emanation of fiery splendour, O god,
calm, self-controlled, and with senses conquered, attains the realm of Brahmā.
The person of pure intellect who, filled with faith, constantly listens to this origin of the fire which reveals the majesty of Paśupati, / and who, O Vyāsa, recites it with devotion before brahmins and deities, immersed in the thought of Bhava, is honoured exceedingly by the gods in the city of Śiva.
Thus ends the fourth chapter, entitled 'The Description of the Origin of Vaiśvānara', in the Avantīkṣetramāhātmya of the fifth Avantyakhaṇḍa in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand verses.

6.1.m: Vyāsa said: / "That archer named Nara who was born from the skull, / why did he now arise in this way at the creation by Viśvakarman? / How was he produced intentionally by lord Rudra, / or by the Blessed One Viṣṇu, or by Brahmā, according to different dispositions? / By whom and from what was he produced among Śaṃkara, Acyuta, and Brahmā? / As for Brahmā who is Hiraṇyagarbha, who was born four-faced, / how did that wonderful fifth face of his also appear? / How did that blessed Brahmā stand, fixing his mind on Rudra, / by whom, foolish-minded, Nara was sent to kill Hara?" / Sanatkumāra said: / "These two alone, Maheśvara and Hari, abide in existence; / nothing is unknown to those two great-souled ones, whether achieved or unachieved. / That which was the fifth face of noble Brahmā, / that was his mental fire, borne indeed by that head. / The Nara who was spoken of as belonging to Brahmā was also his mental fire; / Mahādeva held him, placing him between his fingers. / Having seen his origin before, Nara was thus great; / therefore the skull arose rubbed upon the finger. / Having struck him with an arrow in battle, Brahmā's passion was removed; / the pure sattva was bewildered by rajas, since the Lord acts at will." / Vyāsa said: / "How was the fire produced, the womb held by Sarva (Śiva)? / Tell that in detail, O Blessed One worshipped by sages!" / Sanatkumāra said: / "In the beginning he emitted the Unmanifest and other principles, and then the cosmic egg was born; / Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, was born with the radiance of the color of gold. / That self-manifest one, having performed great austerity for a hundred divine years, / standing in austerity, uttered the sacred texts: 'Bhūr, bhuvaḥ, svar.' / From the connection of the sacred texts with the mind, the fire was later born; / when that fire fell downward, burning the earth..."

6.1.m:
With both hands, that fire was placed above the earth by Brahmā. / Then with the right hand the fire is led onto the altar. // 15
Formerly its flame fell downward; when it was held with flame upward / and turned face up, because it was formed reciprocally by Brahmā, // 16
blazing upward with flames, crackling with sparks of every sound, / it then spoke fiercely to the golden-hued Brahmā: // 17
"Why, O Lord, have I been prevented from devouring the earth? / I am overwhelmed with hunger; let food be given to me!" // 18
Addressed in this way, Brahmā offered his own body-hairs to the fire. / But the lean fire devoured all the body-hairs of Brahmā, // 19
and said, "I have no satisfaction, nor any ease in my body." / Then Brahmā offered his skin, and the fire devoured the skin. // 20
Then the fire indeed said to him, "I have no satisfaction." / Cutting away [his flesh] with the skin, Prajāpati offered his own flesh. // 21
And it said, "I have no satisfaction, nor any ease in my body." / Then Brahmā offered his bones; hungry, it devoured them. // 22
Then a body devoid of elements was made for the fire by the Creator. / Seeing Brahmā then bodiless, it said to him: // 23
"Ah, O Brahmā, I have no satisfaction, nor any ease in my body!" / Enraged, Brahmā split that fire into two with the sound huṃ. // 24
Both weeping fires spoke to Prajāpati for the sake of food. / Again with the sound huṃ Brahmā divided each one into two. // 25
Three of them wept, and one wept uncovered. / Struck by enraged Brahmā, O Vyāsa, with the very sound huṃ, // 26
and as the fire wailed excessively, Brahmā, filled with compassion again, / said: "Devour the bodily elements of those overcome by lust." // 27
That time belonged to that lust; that livelihood was ordained. / Seeing the A-kāra fire situated within his mind, he who is born from the mind— // 28
the Huṃ-kāra fire blazed up, and it said, "What is this?"

Brahmā said to it, "You too resort to a livelihood as you desire, // 29
among the gods, or outside, or in the hermitages of the sages." / Addressed thus by him, it immediately found this livelihood pleasing. // 30
"I myself will grant it in this way," he spoke again and again. / Since this second fire arose from the sound huṃ, // 31
wherever the sound huṃ is uttered with pride or insult, / that is your livelihood by my command, for the appeasement of your hunger. // 32
Summoning the I-kāra fire, Brahmā spoke these words: / "May this livelihood be yours, O Fire: you shall burn the eaten food." // 33
Summoning the U-kāra fire, Brahmā spoke these words: / "Whatever deep meditation upon the earth is weighty, O Lord, resort to that. // 34
And I will arrange an abode and food for you." / Addressed thus by him, that fire which is the mass of stones on the earth— // 35
since fire was declared by him to be in the mountain and the fortress, O great sage Vyāsa— / that U-kāra fire is also the submarine fire in the ocean. // 36
That one too, divided and summoned by Brahmā wishing for an abode, [heard him]: / "You are the eye of the whole world," Brahmā spoke these words. // 37
"Therefore reveal refined speech to the twice-born. / For divine and virtuous [speech destroys] sins, but unrefined speech destroys longevity. // 38
Therefore, refined speech is to be known as virtuous for the twice-born. / And speech is the mother of the twice-born; she is established in the mouth. // 39
Due to the arrangement of false syllables, unrefined speech brings misfortune; / it destroys the speaker; therefore, the fire [resides where] a twice-born person continually purifies it. // 40
Calling again upon the A-kāra fire that had no eyes, / Prajāpati spoke the Vedic speech of speech, but its eyes were closed. // 41
The fire said to Brahmā, "I am the mouth of speech! / Grant me an abode, supreme and best among all splendours." // 42
Brahmā said to it, "Since you desire a place of splendour, / therefore yours shall be the luminous abode of the sun. // 43

therefore, endued with that splendour, one might somehow look upon it without winking." // 44
Then the Grandfather spoke to the distinct I-kāra fire, / which had approached gazing upon Brahmā with a gentle look: // 45
"Because you came here swiftly with a gentle look, O being of great strength, / therefore I shall give you an abode pleasing to all beings. // 46
Cool of nature and cold-rayed, you shall become the moon, / exceeding all splendours, divine, gentle, supremely radiant. // 47
Stationed in trees, you will surpass all splendours with your brilliance." / Having spoken thus and dismissed it, he then summoned the U-kāra fire: // 48
"Come here, come!" Saying this, taking it up, he placed it upon his head. / Stationed there, it becomes this fifth, upward face. // 49
That U-kāra fire was established with such a form; / therefore one should point out fire and the sun as one. // 50
The supreme form of the fire of existence spoke this to Brahmā: / "Grant me too a splendid place, just as [you have done] for yourself." // 51
Brahmā said to it, "Which place pleases you, O Fire?" / The fire replied to him, "Declare a supreme place for me." // 52
"There is no fitting place for you, therefore it will be thus: / if you desire to dwell here, you will indeed abide here. // 53
The perpetual conduct in the world is the cause of the world's maintenance. / For the sake of existence, abide here with your own strength and valour. // 54
Because here, endowed with beauty by the splendour of great flames, / you will obtain unequalled radiance among all creatures; / for this first dharma is not due to desire deluded by illusion." // 55
When this was said by Brahmā, that fire blazed up a thousandfold. / Then, surrounded by endless flames of varied colours and forms, // 56
A-kāra, I-kāra, and U-kāra—Brahmā then beheld it. / That fire did not attain pacification; it increased even more. // 57
Everything was pervaded by the fire of existence, across, above, and below.

Sanatkumāra said:
Brahmā, offering the agnihotra oblation with wild herbs, fruits, and leaves,
and with auspicious kuśa grass and kindling sticks, as had been previously spoken by Hari,
and the seers Nara and Nārāyaṇa, having reached the hermitage of Badarī,
practised fierce austerity for the benefit of all living beings.
The lord of gods, holding a skull in his hand, wandering about this earth,
reached Kuśasthalī and entered that excellent forest,
strewn with various trees and creepers, adorned with diverse flowers,
filled with the calls of various birds, and teeming with diverse deer,
scented by the pleasant wind bearing the fragrance of masses of tree-blossoms,
as though well-worshipped with fruits and flowers laid out intentionally,
and rich with ripe and unripe fruits bearing various scents and tastes,
charming on all sides with fruits richly endowed with golden beauty.
The winds tossed outside withered leaves, grass, and the like,
as well as the dried wood and fruits that had fallen, doing a favour [to the forest].
Bearing the fragrance of clusters of various flowers,

6.1.m: the cool wind blew upon that region of the earth where he entered,
adorned with countless trees bearing leafy crests, / with green, glossy, flawless leaves and hollows free from cracks;
and trees endowed with tops adorned with countless leaves,
free from disease, lovely to look upon, well-rounded, and here and there tall,
perfection shone on all sides, as if in the households of brahmins.
Trees covered with beautiful shoots stirred by the breeze,
like men surrounded by their own noble and faultless kin,
with tops shaken by the wind, made contact with one another;
their crests of branches gently touched one another from nearby due to the wind.
Here and there the nāga trees, with flowers whose filaments were covered with rows of bees,
shone like white eyes with dark pupils.
Here and there karṇikāra trees with tops laden with flowers
shone like noble couples pair by pair at a wedding.
With the lavish display of their fine flowers, the rows of sinduvāra trees
shone like worshiped forest deities incarnate in bodily form. (17)
Here and there, jasmine creepers, bright with their ornaments of beautiful blossoms,
shone forth in every direction like rising crescent moons. (18)
Rich with the exceptional beauty of coral, shining yūthikā creepers
stood up in full bloom, as if fanning the flowering branches. (19)
Here and there in the forest clearings blossomed śāla and arjuna trees,
looking like noble men clad in washed garments of silk. (20)
And the trees, entwined without restraint by flowering creepers,
shone forth like dearly loved husbands embraced by their women. (21)
Mango trees and tilaka trees, with their flower clusters as hands
yielded by the wind, seemed to present offerings to virtuous guests. (22)
And with the interwoven shoots of tilaka and aśoka trees,
they seemed like friends united in heart touching hand to hand. (23)
Bending low with fruit and flowers, like gentle and noble men,
the trees seemed to offer each other fruits and flowers. (24)
Trees, gladdened when embraced by the wind with the waters of rice-fields,

As if with the swiftness of blooms, they advanced for their own adornment,
like men donning equal armor in rivalry. (26)
Upon treetops trembling and bent down under the weight of floral splendor,
intoxicated birds danced, adorned with handsome crests. (27)
Bees resting on heavenly creepers tossed by the wind,
danced along with the vines like men with their beloveds. (28)
Trees covered here and there with flowering jasmine creepers
shone like the autumn sky studded with diverse constellations of stars. (29)
And upon the tops of the trees, flowering mādhavī creepers
shone like ornamental crests fashioned with deliberate artistry. (30)
Green and having the luster of gold, the fruiting and flowering trees
seemed to display friendship, like men in the assembly of the virtuous. (31)
Teeming with floral filaments, their hollows filled with filaments,
with honeybees intoxicated by filaments, they were clear like myna birds. (32)
Resembling śirīṣa blossoms, parrots in pairs here and there
uttered variegated sounds, like honored brahmins [chanting]. (33)
Accompanied by their mates, peacocks with wondrous plumage
stood deep within the woods, as if residing in solitude. (34)
Flocks of birds, warbling in various wonderful tones, sang aloud;
indeed, they made the delightful forest yet more delightful. (35)
Teeming with diverse herds of beasts, constantly filled with rejoicing birds,
that forest equaled Nandana, gladdening the mind and the eyes. (36)
The Lord with a skull in his hand, Śaṃkara,
beheld that supreme forest resembling Nandana with a gentle gaze. (37)

The peaks of mountains shattered in their thousands.

Trembling, crashed down and were destroyed on the surface of the earth.
Pigeon-gray clouds and countless dense masses appearing again,
Veiling the luminous planets, made the sun disappear.
By the tremendous roar of it, [creatures] were made stunned, blind, and deaf;
All the three worlds, with both moving and unmoving beings, were confounded.
The bodies and minds of all the gods and asuras
Trembled helplessly, and they wondered, "What is this?"
Taking courage, all of them gathered, led by Indra,
Reached the world of Brahmā, and spoke this to Brahmā:
"O Lord, what is the cause of this manifestation of portents,
By which the three worlds have been shaken, joined with the workings of Time?
Has the end of the kalpa arrived, with the oceans bursting their bounds?
Have the four elephants of the quarters and the immovable [mountains] become shaken?
Why is the earth submerged by the waters of the seven oceans?
There is no destruction of everything, O Lord, nor any reason for it.

Having reached the most sacred field, where the great lord remained,

Then, having seen what was set down by you, all those of great splendor departed.

At that terrible sound, the Dānava, a thorn to the gods,

Unable to endure it, afflicted with wrath, wicked-souled and invincible to the gods,

Surrounded by crores of terrible Daityas with raised weapons,

“O leaders of the gaṇas, the deceitful Daitya, a thorn even to the three worlds,
comes swiftly; therefore, slay him!”
All the gaṇa leaders took refuge in the approach of the skull.

roaring with a great shout, rushing about, mighty-armed,
pierced him with volleys of darts, with swords, and likewise with clubs.
Befuddling him with a net of arrows, they then felled him to the earth.

6.1.m:
Sanatkumāra said:
“Now, therefore, I shall declare the sacred ford renowned throughout the three worlds,
self-manifest, belonging to Maheśa, known as Kuṭumbikeśvara.
He is freed from all sins, even those committed in seven lifetimes,
who, pure, beholds the god after performing a śrāddha according to the rule.
Surpassing all the worlds, he goes to the world of Śiva.
Moreover, whoever offers all vegetables and various bulbs
upon its bank, he attains the supreme state.
Composed in mind on the first or the eighth day of the bright fortnight of Pauṣa,
by a single fast alone he obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.
And on the full-moon day of Āśvina, the pure man who beholds
the tying of the turban of Maheśa, freed from sin, shall go to heaven.
Having fasted on the fifth day in the bright half in the month of Caitra,
he offers to the god camphor, saffron, musk with sandalwood,
and an oblation of milk-rice with ghee,
and, O best of brahmins, feeds a brahmin together with his wife, presenting [gifts] according to means;
he attains the world of Rudra for as long as fourteen Indras endure.”
Thus ends the tenth chapter, entitled “Description of the Māhātmya of Kuṭumbikeśvara”, in the Avantīkṣetramāhātmya of the fifth Avantyakhaṇḍa in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].

6.1.m:
Sanatkumāra said:
"Now in the north I shall describe the excellent Markaṭeśvara;
there is a famous sacred ford there that bestows all desires. / 1
Having bathed in that sacred ford, a man obtains the fruit of a hundred cows.
For the pacification of poxes, and for the sake of children, / 2
one should crush lentils there, having measured them with a standard measure:
'By the power of Śītalā, may the children be free from disease!' / 3
The people who behold Śītalā, who removes evil, with devotion—
no sin is theirs, O best of the twice-born, nor poverty, / 4
nor do they have any fear of disease or affliction by the planets." / 5
Thus ends the twelfth chapter, titled 'Description of the Śītalā Māhātmya', in the Avantīkṣetramāhātmya in the Avantīkhaṇḍa, in the Skandamahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

6.1.m:
Sanatkumāra said:
"Having bathed at Svargadvāra and beheld the god Bhairava,
one should perform a śrāddha right there dedicated to the ancestors with devotion. / 1
That man, O Vyāsa, delivers his ancestors together with himself;
he who goes through Svargadvāra attains the supreme abode of Rudra. / 2
In front of Bhairava, to the east, stands the goddess Ambikā;
beholding her, a man or a woman is freed from all sins. / 3
On the Mahānavamī day, a person who offers a sacrifice of a goat,
or a buffalo, wine, meat, and an auspicious garland made of bilva leaves,
presenting them with devotion to the Goddess, shall attain all success. / 4
Having bathed there with devotion and performed worship to Maheśvara,
he goes through Svargadvāra to the abode of Rudra, O twice-born." / 5
Thus ends the thirteenth chapter, titled 'Description of the Svargadvāra Māhātmya', in the Avantīkṣetramāhātmya of the fifth Avantīkhaṇḍa, in the Skandamahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
Sanatkumāra said:
"Having bathed in the four oceans, one should view the auspicious Rājasthala,
by the mere darśana of which a man becomes endowed with a son.
There are four oceans: Salt, Milk, Curds, and Sugarcane-juice.
Near that god they were established by Sudyumna."
Vyāsa said:

6.1.s: rājasthala samīpe tu samudrāḥ kena hetunā ..
6.1.d: राजस्थल समीपे तु समुद्राः केन हेतुना ..
6.1.m: "For what reason were the oceans near Rājasthala,
established by Sudyumna? Tell me, O best of sages!
Jambudvīpa extends to a hundred thousand yojanas, very beautiful;
at its boundary this ocean named 'Salt' is situated.
In Śākadvīpa, measuring two hundred thousand [yojanas], the Ocean of Milk is situated;
the Ocean of Curds is situated in Kuśadvīpa, measuring four hundred thousand [yojanas];
in Śālmala the Ocean of Sugarcane-juice is situated, measuring eight hundred thousand [yojanas].
Those four oceans have been described on the orb of the earth;
how then did they come together in one place near Rājasthala?"
Sanatkumāra said:
"In a past kalpa, there was a very righteous king named Sudyumna.

6.1.s: tasya patnī varārohā nāmnā khyātā sudarśanā .. 7 ..

6.1.m: His wife, of lovely limbs, was known by the name Sudarśanā.

6.1.s: muniṃ dālbhyaṃ ca sā dṛṣṭvā papraccha sutakāmyayā ..

6.1.m: Seeing the sage Dālbhya, she asked him, desiring a son:
'O Lord, by what gift, ritual ablution, or ritual practice,
can a son endowed with all auspicious marks be obtained by me?
Explain this to me as it truly is, with details, O brahmin seer!'"
Dālbhya said:
"Formerly, O daughter, those excellent oceans were created by one desiring sons,
by the self-manifest god Brahmā, the creator of the worlds.

6.1.s: teṣu rājñā kṛte snāne tava putro bhaviṣyati ..

6.1.m: When a ritual ablution is performed in them by the king, you will have a son.
Therefore, O daughter, urge your beloved husband to worship Śaṃkara."
Following the very words of Dālbhya and by means of wondrous narrative,
she quickly sent her husband to worship Śaṃkara.
Having gone to Gandhamādana, he propitiated Śaṃkara.
Satisfied, Śaṃkara, whose eyes are the moon, sun, and fire, said:

6.1.s: avaṃtīṃ gaccha rājedra putraṃ prāpsyasi śobhanam..
6.1.d: अवंतीं गच्छ राजेद्र पुत्रं प्राप्स्यसि शोभनम्..
6.1.m: "Go to Avantī, O king of kings; you will obtain an excellent son.
By my command, the oceans will proceed to Kuśasthalī.
On the site shaped like Meru, O king, near Śaṃkara,
you will see the oceans gathered together there, O best of men.
Requested by you, they will remain there forever by a portion of their essence."
Having spoken thus, the all-pervading Mahādeva vanished.
Sudyumna came to Kuśasthalī together with his wife.
Having arrived at Kuśasthalī, he beheld the oceans.
Seeing them near Rājasthala, he bowed down to them.

6.1.m: Hear the meritorious fruit of him who performs a pilgrimage to them.
Having performed a ritual ablution in the exceedingly holy ocean called the Salt [Ocean],
he should then, intent on devotion, perform a śrāddha for the ancestors, O Vyāsa,
and worship Mahādeva, the lord of Pārvatī, who resides in that sacred place.
He should then give maṇḍaka cakes to a brahmin who has mastered the Vedas.
A copper vessel should be made and filled with salt,
and it should be given, along with gold, to a brahmin who has mastered the Vedas.
Furnished with seven kinds of grains, made of bamboo, wrapped with cloth,
accompanied by a priestly fee and fruits, he should carefully offer a guest-water offering.

Whoever performs the pilgrimage in this manner near Rājasthala

Sanatkumāra said:
Hear, O Vyāsa, of the great sacred ford by name Śaṃkaravāpikā.
The excellent sacred ford was created by the god while at play.
The water for washing the skull was thrown down by the God of gods;
because it was placed into a stepwell, it is therefore [called] Śaṃkaravāpikā.

6.1.s: arkāṣṭamyāṃ naraḥ snātvā diśāsu vidiśāsu ca ..

6.1.m: A man, having bathed on the eighth lunar day coinciding with a Sunday, in the cardinal and intermediate directions,
in order beginning with the east, up to and likewise within the center of the stepwell,
should give new water jars filled with sacrificial food, O Vyāsa,
and vegetables and roots to brahmins. Hear the meritorious fruit of that:
Whatever worlds exist in the next world and in this one, endowed with every condition,
to each of those he goes, and he enjoys supreme sovereignty.
Those men who, filled with deep devotion, will praise this māhātmya,
are worshipped even in the world of Rudra. Perpetual homage to them as well!
Sanatkumāra said:
Then, indeed, the lord of the gods, bearer of the Pināka, having the bull for his emblem,
becoming composed, praised the God of gods, the Sun.
The lord of the day arrived, pleased, and spoke to Śaṃkara:

6.1.m: “Choose a boon, O Lord of beings; I am a grantor of boons, I grant [it] to you.” / [Śaṃkara] said to him: “If you grant boons, grant what is asked of me:
Stay here with a portion [of yourself] for the benefit of all embodied beings.”
The sun descended there upon hearing the words of Māheśvara.
Then, by the command of the supreme God of gods, Śaṃkara of great power,
the sun of great splendor attained renown there
by the name Śaṃkarāditya, causing grace to the worlds.
The gods, Daityas, and Gandharvas, together with the Kinnaras, were astonished:

and the Sun, dwelling there, is also present within the sacred ford!”
Then, all those best of gods, headed by Brahmā, pleased,
worshipped the lord of the gods, Āditya, and likewise Śaṃkara.
And those gods, taking bodily form, descended, and having established

Sanatkumāra said:
Now I shall describe another supreme sacred ford among sacred fords,
a supreme sacred ford established under its own name, O best of sages. (1)
Once upon a time, O Vyāsa, in order to wash the skull-bowl,
taking water from [his] head with the skull-bowl, Maheśvara (2)
washed [it] and threw [it] onto the ground. There, an unexcelled sacred ford—
the holy river named Gandhavatī, renowned across the three worlds, [arose]. (3)
Instantly, in a single moment, it became filled with the blood of Brahmā.

6.1.m: Ritual ablution in it is always praised; it was spoken by the God himself: (4)

6.1.m:
Sanatkumāra said:
Having bathed at Daśāśvamedhika and seen the god Maheśvara,
a man attains the fruit of ten horse sacrifices. (1)
By Manu the lord of men, and by King Yayāti,
by Raghu and Uśanas, and by the great seer Lomaśa, (2)
by Atri, by Bhṛgu, O Vyāsa, by wise Dattātreya,
by holy Purūravas, by Nahuṣa, and by Nala, (3)
by bathing here, the fruit of ten horse sacrifices was obtained.
When the end of Dvāpara arrived, likewise by King Bāṣkali (4)
the fruit of ten horse sacrifices was obtained, O best of brahmins.
Likewise, the black-colored liṅga was constantly worshipped with devotion. (5)
Having seen and touched that god, one obtains the previously stated fruit.
In the month of Caitra on the bright eighth [day], having worshipped the god with devotion, (6)
one should give to a brahmin a handsome horse endowed with virtues.
As many as are counted as its hairs, O twice-born one, (7)
for that many thousands of years he is honored in the world of Śiva.
Falling from the world of Śiva, he becomes a universal sovereign on earth. (8)
Thus ends the seventeenth chapter, named 'Description of the Glory of Daśāśvamedha,' in the Avantīkṣetramāhātmya of the fifth Avantyakhaṇḍa, in the Skandapurāṇa comprising eighty-one thousand verses. (17)

6.1.m: O Vyāsa, he obtains ten million times that fruit, there is no doubt of this.
Whatever is offered at Koṭitīrtha with the ancestors in mind,
all that becomes multiplied ten million fold, there is no doubt of this.
The man who, having bathed at Koṭitīrtha, meditates upon the supreme imperishable,
is freed from all sins, just as a serpent [is freed] from its slough.

6.1.s: prātarutthāya yo vipra tatra snānaṃ karoti vai ..9..
6.1.d: प्रातरुत्थाय यो विप्र तत्र स्नानं करोति वै ..9..
6.1.m: O brahmin, he who rises early in the morning and indeed performs a ritual ablution there,
and beholds the god Mahākāla, obtains the fruit of a thousand cows.
A man who has bathed at Koṭitīrtha, having fasted for seven nights and become pure,
that mortal obtains the fruit of a thousand Cāndrāyaṇa penances.
He who keeps a vigil there indeed enjoys endless fruit.
Having performed worship with perfumes and flowers, preceded by a great ceremonial bath,

6.1.s: ya evaṃ nayate rātriṃ sopavāso jiteṃdriyaḥ .. 12 ..
6.1.d: य एवं नयते रात्रिं सोपवासो जितेंद्रियः .. 12 ..
6.1.m: he who thus spends the night fasting, with restrained senses,
attains the fulfillment of all desires, which is difficult even for gods to obtain.
One should worship the god there on the full moon of Kārttika or of Vaiśākha,
with perfumes, flowers of the season, and very beautiful garments.
Camphor, saffron, sandalwood, and aloe—

6.1.s: samabhāgāni kṛtvā tu śilāpṛṣṭhe ca peṣayet ..
6.1.d: समभागानि कृत्वा तु शिलापृष्ठे च पेषयेत् ..
6.1.m: having made equal portions [of these], one should grind them upon a stone slab.
Having anointed Mahākāla, one will become an attendant of Rudra.

6.1.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvaṃtyakhaṇḍe'vantīkṣetramāhātmye rudrasaromāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma dvāviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. .. 22 .. .. cha ..
6.1.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवंत्यखण्डेऽवन्तीक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये रुद्रसरोमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम द्वाविंशोऽध्यायः .. .. 22 .. .. छ ..
6.1.m: Thus ends the twenty-second chapter, entitled “Description of the Māhātmya of Rudrasaras,” in the Avantīkṣetramāhātmya of the fifth Avantyakhaṇḍa in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, the compendium of eighty-one thousand [verses].
Sanatkumāra said:
Now I shall carefully explain the pilgrimage of Mahākāla,
auspicious, bringing welfare, holy, and bestowing holy worlds.

6.1.s: snātvā sarasi rudrasya dṛṣṭvā koṭeśvaraṃ śivam..
6.1.d: स्नात्वा सरसि रुद्रस्य दृष्ट्वा कोटेश्वरं शिवम्..
6.1.m: Having bathed in the lake of Rudra and beheld Śiva Koṭeśvara,
and having bowed, one should then go to the eternal Mahākāla.
Having worshipped the Lord of the thirty [gods] with perfumes, flowers, and salutations,
and prostrated oneself, one should then go to the god Kapālamocana.
Right there the Lord of the god of gods set down the skull upon the ground.
The moment the skull was placed down, an excellent liṅga appeared there.
Named Kapālamocana, destroying all sins.
There indeed one should perform a ceremonial bath with a hundred palas of clarified butter,
Or with a quarter of that half [a quarter of fifty, twelve and a half], or a quarter [of that], free from stinginess regarding wealth.

6.1.s: kāle pūrṇe sa viprendra śivaloke mahīyate .. 6 ..
6.1.d: काले पूर्णे स विप्रेन्द्र शिवलोके महीयते .. 6 ..
6.1.m: When his time is completed, O best of brahmins, he is exalted in the world of Śiva.
Having bowed down, one should then go to the supreme Kapileśvara;
By the darśana of this god, one is freed from the murder of a brahmin.
Then, concentrated in mind, one should go to the god Hanumatkeśvara;
Incomparable sovereignty arises from the darśana of him, O Vyāsa.
Then one should go to the eternal Great God named Paippala,
By the mere darśana of whom liberation is attained, O best of twice-born.
Endowed with devotion and faith, one should then go to Svapneśvara;
And by the darśana of this god, bad dreams are destroyed.
Then one should go to the Great God Īśāna, facing in all directions,
By the mere darśana of whom one becomes the lord of the universe itself.
Having conquered anger and subdued the senses, one should then go to Someśvara;
From blemishes such as leprosy one is freed by the darśana of him.
O Vyāsa, concentrated in mind, one should then go to Vaiśvānareśvara;

6.1.s: tasya vṛddhiḥ sadā loke jāyate tasya darśanāt .. 13 ..
6.1.d: तस्य वृद्धिः सदा लोके जायते तस्य दर्शनात् .. 13 ..
6.1.m: His prosperity constantly increases in the world from the darśana of him.

6.1.s: bījapūrakahastaṃ tu laku līśaṃ tato vrajet ..
6.1.d: बीजपूरकहस्तं तु लकु लीशं ततो व्रजेत् ..
6.1.m: Then one should go to Lakulīśa, who holds a citron fruit in his hand;
The state of Rudra arises from the darśana of him; of this there is no doubt.
Then one should go to the supreme Great God Gadyāṇeśvara,
By the mere darśana of whom all perfections arise.
Constantly prayed to by the gods and worshipped for the sake of success,
Therefore, this lord of obstacles is celebrated as Abhyarthiteśvara.
Then one should go to the eternal, advanced-in-age Mahākāla;
There is neither disease nor old age and affliction from the darśana [of him]; of this there is no doubt.
Then one should go to Vighnanāśa, the lord of living beings, of supreme might.
One should perform his ritual ablution with a hundred pitchers, collected in mind and with devotion.

6.1.s: tasya caiva kṛte snāne labhyaṃte sarvasiddhayaḥ ..
6.1.d: तस्य चैव कृते स्नाने लभ्यंते सर्वसिद्धयः ..
6.1.m: And when his ritual ablution is performed, all perfections are obtained;
And heaven also is always attained from his darśana, O Vyāsa.

6.1.s: tanayaṃ tamanūllaṃghya daṃḍa pāṇiṃ tato vrajet ..
6.1.d: तनयं तमनूल्लंघ्य दंड पाणिं ततो व्रजेत् ..
6.1.m: Not bypassing that son, one should then go to Daṇḍapāṇi,
By the mere darśana of whom Yama's realm is not seen.
Endowed with devotion and faith, one should then go to Puṣpadanta,
By the mere darśana of whom one is freed from all sins.
And concentrated in mind, one should then go to Guhya Mahākāla,
By the mere darśana of whom one is released from secret sins.
Then, absorbed in meditation, one should go to the supreme Durvāseśvara,
By the mere darśana of whom a man accomplishes his purpose.
Holding one's breath near Durvāsas,
And having gone to Gaurī, the great Durgā, one should release the breath immediately after.
There the exhalation is to be released after worshipping her in every way.
Then one should go to Kāleśvara, the god of gods, the great lord,
By the mere darśana of whom one does not see the world of Yama.
And then one should go to Vidhīśa, the god of gods, the great lord,
By the mere darśana of whom deafness does not arise.

6.1.s: kīrtayedātmano nāma sthānaṃ gotraṃ ca tasya vai .. 27 ..
6.1.d: कीर्तयेदात्मनो नाम स्थानं गोत्रं च तस्य वै .. 27 ..
6.1.m: One should declare one's own name, place, and lineage to him indeed.

6.1.s: na kīrtayedyadā nāma sā yātrā viphalī bhavet ..
6.1.d: न कीर्तयेद्यदा नाम सा यात्रा विफली भवेत् ..
6.1.m: If one does not declare the name, that pilgrimage becomes fruitless.
Then, O Vyāsa, having sat down before the god, collected in mind,
Filled with devotion, having bowed down repeatedly, one should say:
"This pilgrimage has been offered by me through your grace, O Great Lord!
Rescue me, O Lord of the universe, from the dreadful ocean of worldly existence!"
He who circumambulates Mahākāla according to this rule,
By him the earth with its seven continents has been circumambulated.
The fruit that one obtains by giving a hundred thousand cows to a hundred thousand brahmins,
That fruit [is attained] by circumambulating the god of gods once.
Endowed with supreme devotion, one should circumambulate Mahākāla;
At every step is the fruit of a sacrifice—thus Śaṃkara told me.
Sixty thousand crores and sixty hundred crores [of deities]—
Are worshipped here through the worship of Yātreśvara.
Whoever performs the pilgrimage in this manner, intent upon meditation on Śiva,
[and] should give a gift of a thousand [coins]; hear the meritorious fruit for him:
he is freed from the sin committed in seven births; there is no doubt about this.

6.1.s: evaṃ yātrāṃ samāpyātha gatvā nijagṛhaṃ naraḥ ..
6.1.d: एवं यात्रां समाप्याथ गत्वा निजगृहं नरः ..
6.1.m: Having thus completed the pilgrimage and then gone to his own home, a man
should feed twenty-six excellent brahmins, corresponding to the number of pilgrimage deities,
who are devotees of Śiva, intent on meditating upon Śiva.
Having given a sacrificial fee along with garments, and having received their permission, he should dismiss them.
Following the sequence of the pilgrimage, he should accompany each one to the door.
Afterwards, to the teacher of dharma, equipped with all utensils,
he should give a milch cow, free from deceit regarding wealth.
Then, O Vyāsa, he should eat himself, accompanied by all his servants.
He should also feed the miserable, the helpless, the poor, the blind, the crippled, and others.
What fruit is declared for this, that I will tell; listen to me:
Having delivered a hundred lineages of both mother and father, steadfast,
he rejoices in the world of Śiva for thousands of crores of kalpas.

6.1.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe'vantīkṣetramāhātmye mahākāleśvarayātrāmāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma trayoviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 23 .. .. cha ..
6.1.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डेऽवन्तीक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये महाकालेश्वरयात्रामाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम त्रयोविंशोऽध्यायः .. 23 .. .. छ ..
6.1.m: Thus ends the twenty-third chapter, named 'Description of the Glory of the Pilgrimage to Mahākāleśvara', in the glorification of the sacred field of Avantī, in the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
Sanatkumāra said:
He who worships the god named Vālmīkeśvara,
becoming silent and intent on meditation, attains the state of a poet.
Vyāsa said:
How did he arise here, and who is this Lord Vālmīkeśvara,
by the mere darśana of whom the state of a poet arises?
Sanatkumāra said:
Formerly, O Vyāsa, there was a brahmin named Sumati, born in the lineage of Bhṛgu.
His wife Kauśikī was endowed with beauty and youth.
A son was born to him indeed, named Agniśarman.

6.1.s: sa pitrā procyamāno'pi vedābhyāsaṃ na manyate .. 4 ..
6.1.d: स पित्रा प्रोच्यमानोऽपि वेदाभ्यासं न मन्यते .. 4 ..
6.1.m: Even though instructed by his father, he did not care for the study of the Vedas.
Then, after a long time, a drought occurred.
Having fallen into misfortune during it, he then took refuge in the southern region.
Then that brahmin Sumati, along with his wife and likewise his son,
reached a foreign forest and, having constructed a hermitage, dwelt there.
Agniśarman fell into company with Ābhīra bandits.

6.1.s: āgacchati pathā tena yastaṃ haṃti sa pāpakṛt.. 7 ..
6.1.d: आगच्छति पथा तेन यस्तं हंति स पापकृत्.. 7 ..
6.1.m: Whoever came by that path, that evil-doer would kill him.

6.1.s: smṛtirnaṣṭā gatā vedā gataṃ gotraṃ gatā śrutiḥ ..
6.1.d: स्मृतिर्नष्टा गता वेदा गतं गोत्रं गता श्रुतिः ..
6.1.m: The Smṛti was lost to him, the Vedas were gone, the lineage was gone, and the Śruti was gone.
Then, at a certain time, in the course of a pilgrimage to sacred fords,
the Seven Seers, of noble vows, arrived along that path.
Then Agniśarman, seeing them, wishing to kill them, said this:
"Take off these garments, and likewise your umbrellas and shoes!

6.1.s: hantavyā hi mayā yūyaṃ gantāro yama sādane .. 5.1.24.10 ..
6.1.d: हन्तव्या हि मया यूयं गन्तारो यम सादने .. 5.1.24.10 ..
6.1.m: For you are to be killed by me, and will go to the abode of Yama."
Hearing that speech of his, Atri spoke these words:

6.1.s: asmatpīḍanajaṃ pāpaṃ kathaṃ te hṛdi vartate ..
6.1.d: अस्मत्पीडनजं पापं कथं ते हृदि वर्तते ..
6.1.m: "How does the sin born of tormenting us abide in your heart?
We are ascetics, striving on a pilgrimage to sacred fords."
Agniśarman said:

6.1.s: mamāsti mātātha pitā suto bhāryā garīyasī ..
6.1.d: ममास्ति माताथ पिता सुतो भार्या गरीयसी ..
6.1.m: "I have a mother, a father, a son, and an elderly wife.

6.1.s: poṣayāmi sadā tāṃstu etanme hṛdi saṃsthitam .. 12 ..
6.1.d: पोषयामि सदा तांस्तु एतन्मे हृदि संस्थितम् .. 12 ..
6.1.m: I always maintain them; this is what is fixed in my heart."
Atri said:
"Go quickly and ask your father and others concerning what has been earned by your own action:
'If sin is committed for your sake, tell me, whose is it?'

6.1.s: yadi te kathayaṃti sma mā mṛṣā prāṇino vadhīḥ .. 14 ..
6.1.d: यदि ते कथयंति स्म मा मृषा प्राणिनो वधीः .. 14 ..
6.1.m: If they tell you [it is theirs, then slay us]; do not kill living beings in vain!"
Agniśarman said:

6.1.s: na kadācinmayā te tu saṃpṛṣṭā īdṛśaṃ vacaḥ..
6.1.d: न कदाचिन्मया ते तु संपृष्टा ईदृशं वचः..
6.1.m: "Never indeed have they been asked such words by me.
By your words, an awakening arises in me today.
Having gone, I shall ask them all: 'Whose disposition is what?'
You must stay right here until my return."
Having said this to them, he went quickly and spoke to his father:
"By the obstruction of dharma and by the tormenting of living beings,
a very great sin is seen; tell me, whose is it?"
The father and likewise the mother said: "There is no demerit of us two here.

6.1.s: tvaṃ jānāsi yatkuruṣe kṛtaṃ bhāvyaṃ punastvayā ..
6.1.d: त्वं जानासि यत्कुरुषे कृतं भाव्यं पुनस्त्वया ..
6.1.m: You know what you do; what was done must be experienced by you again."
Hearing their words, he spoke these words to his wife.

6.1.s: tayāpyuktaṃ na me pāpaṃ pāpametattavaiva hi ..
6.1.d: तयाप्युक्तं न मे पापं पापमेतत्तवैव हि ..
6.1.m: She too said: "The sin is not mine; this sin is yours alone."
He spoke those words to his son, and he replied, “I am [just] a child.”

6.1.s: tajjñātvā hṛdayaṃ teṣāṃ ceṣṭitaṃ caiva tattvataḥ ..
6.1.d: तज्ज्ञात्वा हृदयं तेषां चेष्टितं चैव तत्त्वतः ..
6.1.m: Having understood their inner mind and their conduct truly as it was,
thinking, “I am ruined; the practitioners of austerity are my refuge,”

6.1.s: kṣiptvātha laguḍaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ yena vai jaṃtavo hatāḥ..
6.1.d: क्षिप्त्वाथ लगुडं कृष्णं येन वै जंतवो हताः..
6.1.m: then throwing down the black club with which creatures had been slain,
dishevelling his hair, he quickly stood before the seers.
Bowing down by falling like a rod, he then spoke these words:

6.1.s: na me mātā na ca pitā na bhāryā na ca me sutaḥ .. 23 ..
6.1.d: न मे माता न च पिता न भार्या न च मे सुतः .. 23 ..
6.1.m: “I have no mother, nor father, nor wife, nor son.
Abandoned by all of them, I have taken refuge with you.
You ought to deliver me from hell by giving good instruction.”
Seeing him speaking thus, the seers then said to Atri:
“From your words, awakening has come to him.
He should be shown favour by you; let him become your disciple, O sage.”
Saying “So be it,” he then said to him: “Perform meditation upon Agni.
Through this practice of meditation and recitation of the great mantra,
though a killer of people who committed many insurmountable and terrible sins,

6.1.s: saṃsthito vṛkṣa mūle tvaṃ parā siddhiṃ gamiṣyasi .. 27 ..
6.1.d: संस्थितो वृक्ष मूले त्वं परा सिद्धिं गमिष्यसि .. 27 ..
6.1.m: staying at the root of a tree, you shall attain the highest perfection.”

6.1.s: ityuktvā te yayuḥ sarve saṃkāmaṃ so'pi tatra vai ..
6.1.d: इत्युक्त्वा ते ययुः सर्वे संकामं सोऽपि तत्र वै ..
6.1.m: Having said this, they all departed as they wished; and he too remained right there.
Absorbed in that meditation, he became a yogin for thirteen years.
Over him, motionless, an ant-hill arose there.
Returning by that path, the sages heard there,
filled with wonder, the sound uttered by him inside the ant-hill.
Then, having dug up the ant-hill, [finding him] whose thick limbs had become like wood,
the sages, seeing him, raised him up, who was endowed with prudence.
Then that brahmin paid homage to all those foremost sages.
Having bowed down, he said to those whose splendour blazed through austerity:
“Through your grace, auspicious knowledge has been attained by me today.
Wretched and sunk in the mire of sin, I have been rescued by all of you.”
To him those most righteous ones spoke this sentence:
“O son, since you remained in this ant-hill with single-minded focus,

6.1.s: vālmīkiriti te nāma bhuvi khyātaṃ bhavi ṣyati .. 34 ..
6.1.d: वाल्मीकिरिति ते नाम भुवि ख्यातं भवि ष्यति .. 34 ..
6.1.m: your name shall become renowned on earth as Vālmīki.”

6.1.s: ityuktvā munayo jagmuḥ svāṃ diśāṃ tapasānvitāḥ ..
6.1.d: इत्युक्त्वा मुनयो जग्मुः स्वां दिशां तपसान्विताः ..
6.1.m: Having said this, the seers endowed with austerity went each in his own direction.
When the foremost sages had departed, Vālmīki, best of those who practise austerity,
then came to Kuśasthalī and worshipped Maheśvara.
Having attained the power of poetic composition from him, he composed a charming poem,
which they call the Rāmāyaṇa, the very foremost narrative.
From that time forth, the Lord of gods, named Vālmīkeśvara,
became renowned in Avantī, O Vyāsa, as the granter of poetic power to men.
Thus has been recounted to you the supreme liṅga Vālmīkeśvara,
by merely beholding which the gift of poetry arises.

6.1.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvaṃtyakhaṇḍe'vaṃtīkṣetramāhātmya vālmīkeśvaramāhātmya varṇanaṃ nāma caturviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 24 ..cha ..
6.1.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवंत्यखण्डेऽवंतीक्षेत्रमाहात्म्य वाल्मीकेश्वरमाहात्म्य वर्णनं नाम चतुर्विंशोऽध्यायः .. 24 ..छ ..
6.1.m: Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter, entitled “Description of the Māhātmya of Vālmīkeśvara” in the Avantīkṣetramāhātmya of the fifth Avantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand [verses].

6.1.m: Sanatkumāra said: / Having fully worshipped Śukreśvara with white flowers and ointments, / and then bowing down with devotion, one is honoured in the realm of Rudra. // 1 // / A man, having seen Bhīmeśvara and worshipped him with effort and devotion, / incurs no fear in battle, at night, in water, or in fire, O Vyāsa. // 2 // / Having bathed Gargeśvara with sesame oil / and worshipped him with bilva leaves, a person shall obtain an increase in righteousness. // 3 // / Having fasted on the fourteenth lunar day, [and] having bathed [him] with sesame water containing a prastha of sesame seeds / and worshipped him with sesame seeds, he shall attain constant happiness. // 4 // / A man who gives a thousand cows, having cultivated special devotion, / freed from the bond of worldly existence, goes to the realm of Rudra. // 5 // / Having worshipped Kāmeśvara with ointments such as saffron, / he goes to heaven on an aerial chariot that moves at will; there is no doubt. // 6 // / Having bowed down to Cūḍāmaṇi on the bright ninth lunar day of Kārttika, / a man does not enter an animal womb; he becomes one whose mind is set on dharma. // 7 // / Having worshipped Caṇḍīśvara while fasting on the dark eighth lunar day, / one is not affected even by the grief arising from stepping over leftover offerings. // 8 // / Having approached all these auspicious sacred fords of Maheśvara, / a person of purified mind and cultivated self on earth goes to the delightful realm of Śambhu. // 9 // / Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter, entitled “Description of the Māhātmya of the Sacred Fords of Śukreśvara, Bhīmeśvara, Gargeśvara, Kāmeśvara, Cūḍāmaṇīśvara, Caṇḍīśvara, and Others” in the Avantīkṣetramāhātmya of the fifth Avantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand [verses].

Thus no end to the skull-bowls was reached, O best of sages.
Recognizing him as Rudra Kapardin, they went to him for refuge.
Then, pleased by their devotion, Maheśvara granted them his darśana.
Then the blessed lord with a skull-bowl in his hand spoke to me:
“Choose a boon, O Brahmā, whatever is in your heart.
There is nothing I cannot give you; I shall grant everything in truth.
This superior place of Brahmā is given by me, O four-faced one.
Settle the four varṇas here as you desire.”
To the supreme lord Īśāna, the giver of boons, who spoke thus,
I said in the assembly, “So be it,” and chose no other boon.
The name Ujjayinī was established for Kuśasthalī.
Thereupon the pool Mandākinī was made there by me.
When a ritual ablution is performed there, O brahmins, one is completely freed from all sins.
In it, one should place four auspicious vessels of wealth in the cardinal directions.

one should present them on the full moon of Kārttika or Māgha to brahmins learned in the four Vedas:
the first for the Ṛgveda, the southern for the Yajurveda,
the western for the Sāmaveda, and likewise the northern for the Atharvan.
[Saying] thus with reference to the Vedas: “May the Grandfather be pleased with me.”
Listen attentively to the merit produced when this is done:
Whatever merit is found in all sacred fords is found in the Mandākinī.
Ritual ablution becomes multiplied a thousandfold; chanting is multiplied a hundred thousand times.
Gift-giving in the Mandākinī is to be known as multiplied ten millionfold, without doubt.
When the month of Kārttika arrives, one should perform the gift of a cow there:
a cow made of ghee on the full moon of Kārttika, and one made of sesame on the full moon of Māgha;
and by offering a water-cow on the full moon of Vaiśākha, one is freed from sins.
Whatever sin is committed in speech, in mind, or born of action,
all that evil is destroyed by the mere sight of the Mandākinī.
No sacred ford equal to the Mandākinī is seen on earth,
by the mere sight of which one rejoices in the world of Brahmā.

He who performs a ritual ablution in the Mandākinī and offers a śrāddha
on the new moon or on the full moon rejoices in the world of the ancestors.
The man who constantly beholds the Grandfather with devotion
is endowed with [the merit of] a thousand horse sacrifices and a hundred rājasūyas;
there is no doubt about this, this is the truth, O you whose wealth is austerity.
Then, when a manvantara had passed and the Vaivasvata [age] arrived once more,
Maheśvara, in that very guise of a madman, with his erect linga,
entered Brahmā’s sacrificial session and was seen by those best of twice-born.
Those brahmins cursed him, and others reviled him;
others struck his phallus with dust, and the twice-born cursed him.
Others, arrogant in their strength, struck him with clods of earth and clubs;
some seized the crown of his matted hair and others pulled him.
They asked about the practice of his vow: “By whom was this vow shown?
Women are present right here! How could this be done by you?

Being thus beaten there by the brahmins, Śaṃkara,
the supreme lord, smiled and spoke to all the brahmins:
“Why do you strike me, a madman who has lost his wits?
You are all compassionate, established in a disposition of friendliness.”
To the god Hara who was speaking thus, wearing the appearance of a rogue,
those twice-born, deluded by that god’s māyā,
struck Kapardin again with their hands and feet.
Being beaten by those brahmins, he was overcome with intense anger.
Then they were cursed by the god: “You shall be destitute of the Vedas,
with your topknots tied up, carrying clubs, living off other men's wives,
devoted to gambling and prostitutes, bereft of fathers and mothers.
Neither the father’s wealth nor his learning shall descend to the son.
