And those brahmins who showed compassion to me when I was being beaten—
theirs shall truly be wealth, sons, female and male servants and so forth,
and noble-born wives, by my boon.
Having thus given a curse and a boon, the Lord disappeared.
Then, when the god had departed, the twice-born, realizing that he was the all-pervading Śaṃkara,
went with great effort to the Mahākālavana searching [for him].
Having bathed in the pool of Rudra, they recited the Śatarudrīya;
at the conclusion of their recitation, the god spoke to them with a bodiless voice:
“No falsehood has been uttered by me; where is happiness even in wilful acts?
Nevertheless, O brahmins, I will grant you grace once more.
Those brahmins who are peaceful, self-controlled, and devoted to me—
their lineage shall not be cut off, nor their wealth, nor their offspring.

Having spoken this much, the Lord of gods, the Sovereign of the universe, became silent.
Having thus received both curse and boon from Maheśvara, the God of gods,
they all came together to where the god, the Grandfather [Brahmā], was.
Then, pleasing Virañci with recitations, they stood before him;
pleased, Brahmā said to them: “Choose a boon from me as well.”
At those words of Brahmā, all the best of the twice-born were pleased:
“O brahmins, what boon should be requested, now that the Grandfather is thoroughly pleased?”
Some brahmins there said: “Let us choose the Vedas!”
Then others [said]: “Let wealth and grain be chosen without hesitation!”
Others said: “What is the use of wealth to us, now that the Grandfather is pleased?
Agnihotra fires, the Vedas, and the various scriptures,
peaceful and wealthy people—let these be ours by the granting of the boon!”
As the brahmins were thus disputing there, anger entered them;

then they prepared to fight with one another for the sake of the boon.
Some fought with weapons; some there were aggressors;
some brahmins remained neutral; some took refuge in silence.
Seeing the brahmins fighting in this manner, the Lord said:
“Because ill-counselled brahmins stood outside the hall,
therefore, O brahmins, down to the roots, in the troop of those advancing to fight—
the troop that was neutral shall be bereft of livelihood;
the Vedas shall belong to that [troop] which remained in silence;
the third troop, armed with weapons, which stood wishing to fight,
shall always be devoted to other men's wives, to courtesans, to gambling, and to theft;
that fourfold brahmin [class] shall be devoid of livelihood.”
Having spoken thus, Brahmā went to the supreme abode of Virāj.

for them nothing shall be difficult to attain in my world.
At Kolāmukha, Kurukṣetra, Naimiṣa, and the Puṣkaras,
at Vārāṇasī, Prabhāsa, and likewise at Badarikāśrama,
at Gaṅgādvāra, Prayāga, and the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean,
at Rudrakoṭi, Virūpākṣa, and likewise in the forest of Mitra—
whatever siddhi requiring twelve years in these sacred fords and sacred fields
is obtained by mortals in this world, that is obtained here in a single month,
in Ujjayinī, without doubt, if the mind is fixed on celibacy.
The best among sacred fords and the supreme among sacred fields,
this has always been delightful to me, O best of sages!
Such is the māhātmya of the Mandākinī, the excellent origin of the sacred field.
What else do you desire to hear again, O best of the twice-born?”
Sanatkumāra said:
Having heard that speech of such a kind from Brahmā, O Vyāsa,
Then the sages, headed by Vasiṣṭha, entered into supreme meditation;
and having meditated for a long time, set their minds on dwelling there.

6.1.m:
With their sacrificial fires and with their wives, they went to the region of Avantī.
Having seen the forest of Mahākāla and the great river Śiprā,
the cremation ground, the saline waste, and also the river Gandhavatī,
and having touched the waters of Koṭitīrtha, they indeed took up their abode there.
Remembering that utterance of Brahmā, a desire [to stay] then arose in them.
And Vasiṣṭha, urged by Arundhatī regarding departure,
spoke, O best of sages, to that noble wife of his:
“Mahākāla is here, the river Śiprā, and an exceedingly pure path of destiny;
O large-eyed one, to whom would residence in Ujjayinī not be pleasing?
A man who performs a ritual ablution in the great river, which is indeed hard to attain,
and bows down to Mahākāla, need not grieve over death.
Even an insect or a moth, having died [here], becomes an attendant of Rudra.
Where such liberation is heard of, how could it be abandoned by me?”
Having spoken thus, the foremost of sages at once took up his dwelling right there;

Vyāsa said: / Sacred abodes have been proclaimed by you, O sage. / Tell me now the extent of the forest of Mahākāla. // 1
Sanatkumāra said: / Just as I heard it in ancient times as Brahmā himself spoke it, / that I shall declare to you; listen as I tell it. // 2
To the extent of a single yojana, adorned on all four sides / with golden arched gateways hung with strings of pearls, // 3
the gates shine there, with stationed golden pitchers, / with gates facing white lotuses, adorned with many gems. // 4
And stationed by Maheśvara, the mighty guardians of the gates / shine at those gates, bestowing grace upon the worlds. // 5
Piṅgaleśa stands in the east, the sun appearing in youthful form, / facing the sacred ford, fair-complexioned, heavy, followed by hosts of attendants. // 6
In the south also stands the great yogin Kāyāvarohaṇeśvara; / the lord of wealth stands at the western gate facing the sacred field, // 7
assigned by Maheśa, stationed in the western quarter; / and having taken his place in the northern direction stands Uttareśvara, // 8
the accomplisher of all deeds, commanded by Śaṃkara. / Those very righteous mortals who dwell here within the sacred field, // 9
upon dying, go to the city of Rudra in aerial chariots that fulfill all desires. / On the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, or during the conjunction of the sun and the moon, // 10
having bowed to the five Īśānas in reverse and direct order, / fasting for a single day, meditating on Maheśvara, // 11
one is freed from all sins, even those accumulated over many births. / And thus, O brahmin, he who undertakes the pilgrimage to the five Īśānas // 12
goes to the realm of Rudra in this very body of his. / Now listen as I declare another pilgrimage to the five Īśānas, destructive of all sins, // 13
so that it may be performed with ease. / Having bathed in the morning in the Rudrasaras on the eleventh day, concentrated in mind, // 14

6.1.m:
having performed the śrāddha and bowed to Mahākāla and the lord Īśāna, / having then gone to Piṅgaleśa and bathed, he should perform the śrāddha. // 15
Then approaching the god Piṅgaleśvara, who is the lord of Gaṇas, / having worshipped him with perfumes, flowers, and incense, he should depart. // 16
Having reached Mahākāleśvara, bathed again and with senses conquered, / he should worship the eternal, self-manifest lord of the gods of gods. // 17
He should spend the night in the northeast after taking an evening meal, / meditating on Maheśāna, resting his body upon the ground. // 18
On the twelfth day, having bathed in the morning, the man should perform everything as before; / having gone to Kāyāvarohaṇa, he should worship as at Piṅgaleśvara. // 19
Then, in the same way on the thirteenth day, he should worship Bilveśa in the west; / on the fourteenth day likewise he should worship Uttareśvara in the north. // 20
On the new moon day, pure and bathed, he should worship Mahākāleśvara / with perfumes, flowers, incenses, and various offerings of food. // 21
Having performed singing, dancing, and the like, bowing down he should beg forgiveness; / and having performed the pilgrimage mentioned before, he should then go to his own home. // 22
He should feed five brahmins devoted to the worship of Śiva; / having bowed down to those twice-born residing at Mahākāla, who are the forms of deities, // 23
and worshipped them with gold and new garments made of fine threads, / he should give a chariot at Piṅgalaka, and an elephant at Kāyāvarohaṇa. // 24
Having given a horse at Bilveśvara, and a bull in the north, / and having given a cow furnished with all accessories at Mahākāla— // 25
he who does this thus, O Vyāsa, hear the meritorious fruit for him! // 26
Together with his paternal and maternal lines, he rejoices in heaven / with singing and dancing of apsarases, in aerial chariots that fulfill all desires. // 27
Thus ends the praise of the pilgrimage to the five Īśānas.
He who circumambulates Kuśasthalī with fixed vows / has circumambulated the earth with its seven continents. // 28
That man who beholds Padmāvatī and worships her with lotuses,

6.1.m:
having offered incense and food offerings, goes to the city of Brahmā upon death. // 29
Having worshipped Svarṇaśṛṅgāṭikā, O Vyāsa, with flowers resembling gold / with great devotion, he goes to the abode of Śiva. // 30
He who beholds the goddess Avantinī, renowned in the three worlds, / goes to the city of Indra in an aerial chariot that fulfills all desires. // 31
He who worships the goddess Amarāvatī with lotuses with devotion / rejoices forever in heaven, delighted together with the immortals. // 32
He who beholds the goddess Ujjayanī with devotion and concentrated mind, / endowed with all sovereignty, is glorified in the realm of Rudra. // 33
And he who beholds Viśālā with concentrated mind, with devotion to Rudra, / is freed from the three kinds of sins; there should be no doubt about this. // 34
Thus ends the greatness of the seven Kalpas.
Hear, O Vyāsa, of the great sacred ford worshipped in ancient times by Brahmā, / named Akrūreśvara, where the grandfather attained perfection. // 35
Having performed worship of the deity there, fasting on the eighth day of the dark fortnight, / with conquered senses, pure and self-controlled, one attains the realm of Rudra. // 36
A man remaining in his house in the morning should not speak with anyone; / having beheld the god Akrūreśvara, he obtains the fruit of giving gold. // 37
Thus ends the greatness of Akrūreśvara.
He who beholds Brahmā, pure, bathed, and with conquered senses, / is freed from terrible sin, and goes to the realm of Brahmā upon death. // 38
Brahmā, seated in the lotus posture, meditating on the supreme state, / was addressed by the best of sages, Vasiṣṭha and others, concerning the origin of actions: // 39
The seers said: / The Ādityas, the Maruts, the Sādhyas, and both the Aśvins, / and the ancestors of the worlds who are worshipped on earth by mortals, // 40
the planets, the sun, the stars, the yakṣas, the elephants of the quarters, and the fire and wind— / these gods, and all of us, are recited as your portions. // 41
Why do you meditate, O lord of gods? Declare all this to us! // 42

6.1.m: The two kinds of knowledge whose nature is truth, both the higher and the lower, / are my two forms, eternal and embodied. // The seers said: // O grandfather, how may we know you, the supreme lord, / through whose darśana the highest perfection is attained by us? // Brahmā said: // There is a supreme sacred field of Maheśvara, called Kuśasthalī. / Desiring to perform a sacrifice, I prayed to the god Śrīkaṇṭha, the lord of Pārvatī. // When begged, that god, Parameṣṭhin, said to me: / “This sacred field, a full yojana all around, O Grandfather, // is granted by me to you, O lord, except for the Mahākāla forest.” / There I was barred; hidden in that forest out of anger, / Kapardin said there: “We shall not come near you.” // Then the sacrifice was begun under the protection of Nārāyaṇa. / Yet my sacrifice was known by Śambhu, the god of gods. // Kapardin then came to the sacrificial enclosure to beg for alms. / Then the sacrificers said to him there: “Do not stay here, loathsome one!” // And Kapardin said to them there: “I shall return.” / Having said this and set down his skull-bowl right there on the ground, // Kapardin, the supreme lord, went to the river Śiprā to bathe. / When that Kapardin had gone to the Śiprā, the twice-born said: // “How can the fire-offering be made when a skull is resting in the assembly? / The wise declared of old that purifications are free of skulls.” // That skull was cast aside by an assembly member with his own hand. / When it was thrown, another appeared; when that was thrown, another appeared again.

Sanatkumāra said:

known as Candrāditya, worshipped formerly by Candra and Āditya.
Whoever worships that god, who is venerated by gods and demons,
with perfumes, flowers, incenses, and various food-offerings,
attains the world of Candra, Āditya, and others, fulfilling all desires,
on an aerial chariot bright as the sun, for as long as the moon and the sun endure.
Thus ends the Candrādityamāhātmya.
Sanatkumāra said:

Sanatkumāra said:

6.1.d: द्वितीयापि त्वियं सीता उक्तो रामेण लक्ष्मणः .. 38 ..
6.1.m: with this Sītā as the second.” Thus Lakṣmaṇa was addressed by Rāma.
Seizing the bow, Lakṣmaṇa then stood up, dejected.
The two tormentors of foes reached the enclosure boundary, the limit of the sacred field.
Having crossed beyond the boundary of the sacred field, Rāma said to Lakṣmaṇa:

6.1.s: nivartayasva saumitre samarpaya ca me dhanuḥ ..
6.1.d: निवर्तयस्व सौमित्रे समर्पय च मे धनुः ..
6.1.m: “Turn back, Saumitri, and hand over my bow!”
Hearing Rāma's words, Lakṣmaṇa said to Sītā:

6.1.s: kimarthaṃ hi parityaktaḥ ko'parādhaḥ kṛto mayā ..
6.1.d: किमर्थं हि परित्यक्तः कोऽपराधः कृतो मया ..
6.1.m: “For what reason have I been abandoned? What fault was committed by me?
Abandoned by Rāma, I will surrender my life, without a doubt.”
Then Sītā said to Rāma: “For what reason, O lord,
is Lakṣmaṇa, the hero who increases Sumitrā’s joy, being abandoned by you?”
Rāghava, however, said to Sītā: “I will not abandon Lakṣmaṇa,
a beloved one equal to Lakṣmaṇa, never even in a dream.
Yet, O fair-hipped one, the working of this sacred field was previously heard by me:

6.1.s: asminkṣetre na saubhrātraṃ sarvo hi svārthatatparaḥ .. 45 ..
6.1.d: अस्मिन्क्षेत्रे न सौभ्रात्रं सर्वो हि स्वार्थतत्परः .. 45 ..
6.1.m: In this sacred field there is no brotherly love; indeed, everyone is intent on their own self-interest.
They do not respect one another, having self-interest as their sole motive.

6.1.s: na śṛṇvaṃti pituḥ putrāḥ putrāṇāṃ vā tathā pitā .. 46 ..
6.1.d: न शृण्वंति पितुः पुत्राः पुत्राणां वा तथा पिता .. 46 ..
6.1.m: Sons do not listen to the father, nor likewise does the father listen to the sons;

6.1.s: na ca śiṣyo gurorvākyaṃ gururvā śiṣyakarma ca ..
6.1.d: न च शिष्यो गुरोर्वाक्यं गुरुर्वा शिष्यकर्म च ..
6.1.m: neither does the student listen to the teacher's word, nor the teacher care for the student's deed.
Affection is bound to material interest; no one is dear to anyone else.”

6.1.s: evamuktvā yayau rāmo lakṣmaṇo jānakī tathā ..
6.1.d: एवमुक्त्वा ययौ रामो लक्ष्मणो जानकी तथा ..
6.1.m: Having spoken thus, Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, and Jānakī went on,
the joy of the Raghus having installed a liṅga there named after himself.

6.1.s: rāmatīrthe naraḥ snātvā dṛṣṭvā rāmeśvaraṃ śivam..
6.1.d: रामतीर्थे नरः स्नात्वा दृष्ट्वा रामेश्वरं शिवम्..
6.1.m: A man, having bathed at Rāmatīrtha and seen Rāmeśvara, [who is] Śiva,
is freed from all sins and goes to the world of Śiva.
Thus ends the praise of the greatness of Rāmeśvara.
Sanatkumāra said:
Having bathed at the Saubhāgyaka sacred ford and seen the lord of Saubhāgya,
freed from all sins, one obtains supreme good fortune.
A man, having bathed at Ghṛtatīrtha, should bathe Śiva with clarified butter.
Then, having offered clarified butter into the fire, he is exalted in the world of Rudra.
Having worshipped the goddess Yogīśvarī, who is bowed to by gods and demons,
freed from all sins, one attains supreme yoga.
A man, having bathed at Śaṅkhāvarta, freed from all sins
and endowed with wealth and grain, is born in a pure family.
A man should bathe [the deity] at Sudhodaka on the fourteenth day for the sake of liberation;
having seen Śiva Sudheśvara, he then attains the path of liberation.
Likewise, I shall proclaim another sacred ford, renowned throughout the three worlds,
famed as Kiṃpunā, which frees one from the sin of killing a brahmin.

6.1.s: pūrvaṃ tretāyuge vyāsa sunetro nāma vai dvijaḥ..
6.1.d: पूर्वं त्रेतायुगे व्यास सुनेत्रो नाम वै द्विजः..
6.1.m: Formerly in the Tretā age, O Vyāsa, there was a twice-born man named Sunetra.

6.1.s: tasya putraḥ samu tpanno viśvāvasuriti smṛtaḥ ..56..
6.1.d: तस्य पुत्रः समु त्पन्नो विश्वावसुरिति स्मृतः ..56..
6.1.m: A son was born to him, known as Viśvāvasu.
Due to a curse of Yavakrīta, his own father was killed by him.
Afflicted by the sin of killing a brahmin, O Vyāsa, wandering from sacred ford to sacred ford,

6.1.s: tīrthe kiṃpunake snātvā dhārātīrthe gato dvijaḥ ..
6.1.d: तीर्थे किंपुनके स्नात्वा धारातीर्थे गतो द्विजः ..
6.1.m: having bathed at the Kiṃpuna sacred ford, the twice-born man went to Dhārātīrtha.
Then at Kapiladhārā he contemplated within himself:

6.1.s: kathaṃ me patitā dhārā anṛtā vā śrutistathā ..
6.1.d: कथं मे पतिता धारा अनृता वा श्रुतिस्तथा ..
6.1.m: “How has the stream fallen upon me? Or is the sacred tradition untrue?”
Reflecting thus, he then returned to Avantikā.

6.1.s: atra tīrthe punaḥ snāti yāvadvāṇīṃ tato'śṛṇot ..
6.1.d: अत्र तीर्थे पुनः स्नाति यावद्वाणीं ततोऽशृणोत् ..
6.1.m: While he was bathing again at this sacred ford, he heard a voice:
"Why do you contemplate further, O brahmin, by which you have become the best of the twice-born?

6.1.s: na te'sti brahmahatyā vai tīrthasnānena nāśitā ..
6.1.d: न तेऽस्ति ब्रह्महत्या वै तीर्थस्नानेन नाशिता ..
6.1.m: Indeed, your [sin of] killing a brahmin exists no more; it has been destroyed by bathing at the sacred ford.

6.1.s: gaccha śīghraṃ gṛhaṃ vipra pāpahīno yathāsukham .. 61 ..
6.1.d: गच्छ शीघ्रं गृहं विप्र पापहीनो यथासुखम् .. 61 ..
6.1.m: Go quickly to your home, O vipra, freed from sin, at your ease."
Thus ends the māhātmya of Kimpunā.
Sanatkumāra said:
I shall speak of another excellent [shrine], Pattaneśvara.
Standing there, the Great Lord again looked upon the city.
He is called Pattaneśvara, the Great Lord, God of gods.
The man who, filled with devotion, O Vyāsa,
always worships [him] according to rule with fragrant perfumes, flowers, incenses, and delightful lamps,
his lineage is not cut off as long as the liṅga remains in place;
and by a vehicle drawn by swans, he goes to the world of Śiva.
Likewise, I shall proclaim another sacred ford, renowned across the three worlds,
known as Durdharṣa, which frees one from the sin of killing a brahmin.
In ancient times, O Vyāsa, the Sun established [a sacred ford] named Durdharṣa;
the famous sacred ford, consecrated by the Sun, was on the riverbank.
There is a liṅga, a mass of splendor, worshipped by the gaṇas and gandharvas.
Having bathed there on the seventh or eighth day, on a solstice, or on a Sunday,
having become pure, having fasted for one day,
and having seen the Great Lord situated there on the bank of the Śiprā,

6.1.s: pūjayitvā tu bhāvena yatphalaṃ tacchraṇuṣva me .. 69 ..
6.1.d: पूजयित्वा तु भावेन यत्फलं तच्छ्रणुष्व मे .. 69 ..
6.1.m: and having worshipped [him] with devotion—hear from me the fruit thereof:
having rescued the entire family of his father and mother, he goes to Śiva.

6.1.s: tatra yacchati yo dānaṃ gohemādi viśeṣataḥ .. 5.1.31.70 ..
6.1.d: तत्र यच्छति यो दानं गोहेमादि विशेषतः .. 5.1.31.70 ..
6.1.m: Whoever gives a gift there, especially of cows, gold, and the like,
it remains imperishable in the world as long as the moon and sun endure.
Likewise, I shall proclaim another excellent sacred ford, Gopīndra,

6.1.s: gautamena purā yatra indraḥ śāpādbha gīkṛtaḥ ..
6.1.d: गौतमेन पुरा यत्र इन्द्रः शापाद्भ गीकृतः ..
6.1.m: where formerly Indra was covered in vulvas by the curse of Gautama.
Filled with shame over the vulvas, Śakra entered an excellent forest,
and formerly gratified Śaṃkara there with fierce austerity.
By Śambhu being pleased, O vipra, those vulvas that were on his body
were turned into a thousand eyes by him; therefore it is called Gopīndra.
Having bathed there, equal in prowess to Śakra, he goes to heaven.
Those who die there do not obtain rebirth on the surface of the earth.
Having bathed at the Gaṅgātīrtha, a man obtains abundant religious merit.
On the tenth day of the bright half of Jyeṣṭha, he declares the fruit in the Gaṅgā.
Having bathed in Puṣpakaraṇḍa and having seen Puṣpakaraṇḍaka,
he departs in the Puṣpaka aerial chariot and rejoices in heaven.
A man who bathes at Uttareśvara quickly delivers [his ancestors] from hell;
endowed with his desired pleasures, he goes to heaven without a doubt.
A man, having bathed at Bhūteśvara, should then worship Bhūteśvara
with fragrances, flowers, and the like, and food offerings; upon dying, he goes to the city of Rudra.

6.1.s: śiprāyāṃ tu naraḥ snātvā kailāsaṃ tu namasyati .. 79 ...
6.1.d: शिप्रायां तु नरः स्नात्वा कैलासं तु नमस्यति .. 79 ...
6.1.m: A man who bathes in the Śiprā and bows down to Kailāsa—
just as darkness is struck down by the sun, so his sin perishes.
And whoever sees Ambālikā with the restraint of meditation,

6.1.s: sa muktaḥ sarvapāpebhyaḥ kaṃcukena phaṇī yathā ..
6.1.d: स मुक्तः सर्वपापेभ्यः कंचुकेन फणी यथा ..
6.1.m: he is freed from all sins, just as a serpent [is freed] from its slough.
I shall proclaim Ghaṇṭeśvara, which is worshipped even by the gods,
where, having drunk the water of the well, one obtains incomparable good fortune.
Whoever worships the Lord of gods in proper sequence with perfumes and flowers
dwells in the world of Śiva as long as the fourteen Indras [endure].

6.1.s: puṇyeśvaraṃ tu yaḥ paśyecchuciḥ snāto jiteṃndriyaḥ .. 83 ..
6.1.d: पुण्येश्वरं तु यः पश्येच्छुचिः स्नातो जितेंन्द्रियः .. 83 ..
6.1.m: Whoever, pure, having bathed, with senses conquered, beholds Puṇyeśvara,
he attains the status of Gaṇapati's attendant, which is difficult to attain even for the gods.
A man having bathed at Lampeśvara and fully worshipped the Great Lord

6.1.s: na yāti narakaṃ martyaḥ svargaloke mahīyate..
6.1.d: न याति नरकं मर्त्यः स्वर्गलोके महीयते..
6.1.m: does not go to hell; that mortal is exalted in the heavenly world.
Likewise, I shall proclaim another [deity] difficult to attain even for the gods,
Vināyaka, named Sthavira, who was worshipped in ancient times by Brahmā.
Having bathed there and become pure, whoever worships Vināyaka
with fragrances, incenses, food offerings, and eatable and chewable foods—hear the fruit:
his desired perfection comes to be, and upon dying, he goes to the city of Śiva.
Near the Navanadī, the wise person should worship Pārvatī.
with fragrant perfumes, flowers, and incenses, one obtains peerless good fortune.

6.1.s: kāmodake naraḥ snātvā dṛṣṭvā kāmaṃ ratipriyam ..
6.1.d: कामोदके नरः स्नात्वा दृष्ट्वा कामं रतिप्रियम् ..
6.1.m: Having bathed in Kāmodaka and beheld Kāma, the beloved of Rati,
one obtains in heaven a body coveted by gods and gandharvas.

6.1.s: prayāge tu naraḥ snātvā prayāgeśaṃ tu paśyati ..
6.1.d: प्रयागे तु नरः स्नात्वा प्रयागेशं तु पश्यति ..
6.1.m: A man who bathes at Prayāga and beholds Prayāgeśa,
surpassing all worlds, is glorified in the world of Śiva.

6.1.m:
Sanatkumāra said:
Now I shall proclaim another, the sun god Narāditya,
by whose mere darśana one is freed from all diseases. / 1
I shall describe to you the manner of the installation of Narāditya.
Formerly, when the battle between the one born of blood and the one born of sweat was averted, / 2
the two gods Nara and Nārāyaṇa descended to the surface of the earth.
They were born in Mathurā to the noble Kuntī and Devakī. / 3
Thus the two lived in the world, radiant and attaining supreme prosperity.
For one cause Kṛṣṇa was born, and for another Dhanañjaya. / 4
Indeed, he slew all the Dānavas in battle, beginning with Kaṃsa.
Then Pārtha went to heaven to obtain celestial weapons from Vāsava. / 5
When the hero had acquired the weapons, Indra requested him for a sacrificial fee.
Being praised, the king of the gods indeed asked for that sacrificial fee: / 6
“The fierce Nivātakavacas, who dwell in Hiraṇyapura,
must be slain quickly, Arjuna; this is my guru’s fee.” / 7
Arjuna pledged the slaying of those evil-minded ones.
Mounting the chariot of Indra and taking up his bow with arrows, / 8
Pārtha, having slain them and thus accomplished an exceedingly difficult deed,
brought delight to all the dwellers of heaven. / 9
Then Śakra spoke these words to Arjuna, whose task was accomplished:
“O hero, choose the supreme boon that is pleasing to you, / 10
rarely found in the mortal world, and longed for in your heart, O Pārtha.”
He chose two icons which had been worshipped by Brahmā himself. / 11
By Brahmā, full of affection, they had been bestowed upon Dakṣa;
and by Dakṣa too, they, the dispellers of darkness, were worshipped for more than a yuga. / 12
When a conflict arose between the gods and the asuras,
Śakra was conquered by the Dānavas, his kingdom was seized, and he went to the forest. / 13
Śatakratu, standing on one leg, performed fierce austerity
for a thousand divine years, and Dhiṣaṇa saw him. / 14
Seeing the king of the gods, Bṛhaspati said:
“Leaving heaven, how have you come to this forest, Śakra? / 15
Remaining in the forest alone, you cannot subdue your enemies.
Knowing this, O king of the gods, go quickly to the hermitage of Dakṣa. / 16
Given by Brahmā for worship and made from the Pārijāta tree,
which Viśvakarman fashioned—beg those two from the Prajāpati. / 17
The destruction of your enemies will happen through the grace of those two icons.”
Gladdened by that speech of his guru, the god Śatakratu / 18
went swiftly to where the Prajāpati Dakṣa was.
Bowing low in humility, he asked for the two auspicious icons. / 19

6.1.m:
The two icons, O Vyāsa, were worshipped by Śakra for a hundred autumns.
By their splendor, all the Dānavas met their destruction.
The two icons spoke to Śakra: “Choose an excellent boon.
Know, O Vāsava, that we are supremely pleased by this devotion of yours.”
Then Śakra, with a gracious heart, chose a boon, O best of brahmins:
“Those evil-minded Dānavas who are our adversaries—
may all of them go to destruction; this is the boon I desire.
And I wish to worship you two as long as I remain Indra.”
Saying “So be it,” the two icons went to heaven.
“I indeed ask for that pair of icons as the necessary object of my boon.”
Indra said:
“Well done, Pārtha, again well done! That they should reside in this manner—
these two icons, O Pārtha, by the high-souled Śaṅkara
were worshipped with lovely red lotus petals for a day of Brahmā;
for the protection of the three worlds, they were worshipped formerly by Viṣṇu
with fragrant blue lotuses for a thousand years.

6.1.m:
Then Prajāpati, desiring to perform creation with concentrated mind,
worshipped the two icons with auspicious red lotuses and water lilies.
How indeed will you alone take them to the mortal world, O Pārtha?
Bereft of these two, heaven will become equal to death.”
Arjuna, bowing down before Devendra who was unwilling to give them,
said, “O Lord, I have no need of this boon [if you are unwilling].”
Then Śakra spoke again to Pārtha, O eminent sage:
“O hero, take these two and install them in Kuśasthalī.
On the northern bank of the Śiprā, Keśava [installed] Keśavārka;
where the destroyer of all sins is established,
install them there, where all sins are destroyed.
Then there shall be the festival on the full moon of Āṣāḍha and on Kaumudī.
I shall come there accompanied by hosts of apsarases;
the Maruts shall come, and clouds accompanied by lightning.
When a bank of clouds has arisen and I am raining there,

the people will surely say: ‘Lord Purandara has arrived.’
Bowing to the radiant sun, the omnipresent lord worshipped by Brahmā and others,
I shall return, O Bībhatsu, just as I came.”
Thus, O Vyāsa, having given the pair of icons to Pārtha, Vāsava
sent the son of Pāṇḍu to the earthly realm together with the charioteer.
Nārada, in Dvārakā, in order to summon Kṛṣṇa,
spoke that word of the king of gods, along with the secret, to Keśava,
reciting it to that foremost of men: “Come, Kṛṣṇa, to Kuśasthalī!
For the two icons made of Pārijāta wood, well crafted by Viśvakarman,
have been granted by Indra to you and to the son of Pāṇḍu.”
Hearing those words, Śauri departed for the city of Avantī.
And he descended from the sky and embraced that son of Pāṇḍu.
Pleased, he embraced Phālguna and spoke these words: [5.1.32.40]
“My birth has borne fruit; my delight has been born, O Arjuna.
Since my joy is peerless, let the highest task be accomplished.” [41]

6.1.m:
Having spoken thus, O Vyāsa, the two then reached Kuśasthalī.
Kṛṣṇa, whose desire was fully accomplished, then said to Pārtha: [42]
“Go, Arjuna, to the eastern quarter and install one image.
For in the forenoon there will be an auspicious, delightful astrological moment. [43]
I too am going to the northern river, O sage, for the sake of installation.
At the sound of my conch, install the lord Sun.” [44]
Having gone to the east, O Pārtha, he looked upon an auspicious place.
O Vyāsa, he installed the Lord of Day firmly. [45]
As the Pāṇḍava meditated, “I shall install the divine Arka,”
he spoke to him: “Make a beautiful place!” [46]
He spoke to Pārtha, unbearable with that splendour.
Then Savyasācin, terrified upon seeing that image speaking, [47]
unable indeed to endure its splendour, said these words to the god:
“Where, O god, shall I install you? What place pleases you? [48]
Assume a gentle form and one easy to behold for the creatures, O Lord of Rays!

May the gods dwelling in heaven, the serpents residing in Pātāla, [49]
and the mortals dwelling on earth become purified by your darśana.”
The god said to Arjuna: “Do not fear from seeing me.” [5.1.32.50]
Then, bestowing fearlessness with his right hand in the gesture of fearlessness,
reassuring him, he became peaceful, assuming a gentle form. [51]
By the divine Maker of Light, his own splendour was displayed.
Then Sūrya said: “This very place is my immovable [abode].” [52]
When the astrological moment arrived, the great conch was blown by Hari,
and Sūrya, praised by the immortals, was installed by Nara. [53]
Arjuna said:
Victorious is the Garlanding-Rayed, radiant, whose steeds are untired, the abode of all worlds, the boisterous laughter at the end of the eastern quarter,
by the mere praise of whom the body of men, seized by manifold defilements and faults, becomes free of sin. [54]
What poet would wish to praise at will the Sun, who is praised by seers beginning with Brahmā?

6.1.s:
stoṣyehaṃ tadapi suvistarātsubuddhe kiṃ dīpo jvalati hi nodite śaśāṃke .. 55 ..
śāstrārthakāmanipuṇairmunibhiḥ stutasya kiṃ vastu yanna racitaṃ vividhaiḥ prayogaiḥ ..
dvaipāyanaprabhṛtibhirmunibhiḥ purāṇairāpītasāramiha bhāti jagatsamastam .. 56 ..
kāmaṃ tathāpyahamatīva vicārya bruddhyā bhānostrilokagurupūjitapādayugmam ..
vṛttaiḥ sphuṭārthamadhurākṣarasaṃdhiyuktaistvāṃ vai vicitragatibhiḥ parikīrtayiṣye .. 57 ..
tāvajjagadbhavati niścalameva sarvaṃ tāvatkriyāśca vividhā na ca yāṃti siddhim ..
yāvacca nātha kamalāmalamaṃḍala tvamuttiṣṭhase vyapanayankiraṇaistamāṃsi .. 58 ..
tāvanna bhāṃti śikharāṇi mahīruhāṇāṃ gucchaistu phullavanamīlitalocanāni ..
suptāni bodhayasi ṣaṭcaraṇākulāni yāvanna bhābhiramalābhiranuttamābhiḥ .. 59 ..
6.1.d:
स्तोष्येहं तदपि सुविस्तरात्सुबुद्धे किं दीपो ज्वलति हि नोदिते शशांके .. 55 ..
शास्त्रार्थकामनिपुणैर्मुनिभिः स्तुतस्य किं वस्तु यन्न रचितं विविधैः प्रयोगैः ..
द्वैपायनप्रभृतिभिर्मुनिभिः पुराणैरापीतसारमिह भाति जगत्समस्तम् .. 56 ..
कामं तथाप्यहमतीव विचार्य ब्रुद्ध्या भानोस्त्रिलोकगुरुपूजितपादयुग्मम् ..
वृत्तैः स्फुटार्थमधुराक्षरसंधियुक्तैस्त्वां वै विचित्रगतिभिः परिकीर्तयिष्ये .. 57 ..
तावज्जगद्भवति निश्चलमेव सर्वं तावत्क्रियाश्च विविधा न च यांति सिद्धिम् ..
यावच्च नाथ कमलामलमंडल त्वमुत्तिष्ठसे व्यपनयन्किरणैस्तमांसि .. 58 ..
तावन्न भांति शिखराणि महीरुहाणां गुच्छैस्तु फुल्लवनमीलितलोचनानि ..
सुप्तानि बोधयसि षट्चरणाकुलानि यावन्न भाभिरमलाभिरनुत्तमाभिः .. 59 ..
6.1.m:
Even so, O wise one, I shall praise [you] at great length; does a lamp not indeed burn when the moon has risen? [55]
What praise-matter is there that has not been composed through various applications by seers skilled in desires for scriptural truth?
The entire world here seems to have had its essence drained dry by the ancient seers headed by Dvaipāyana. [56]
Even so, having reflected deeply with my intellect upon both feet of the Sun, worshipped by the teacher of the three worlds,
I shall indeed celebrate you with verses joined with clear meaning and sweet syllables, through varied movements. [57]
For that long the entire world remains utterly motionless, for that long various rites do not attain success,
until you, O Lord with an immaculate orb like a lotus, arise, driving away darkness with your rays. [58]
For that long the crests of trees, with clusters of blossoms, do not shine, their eyes closed in the blooming forest;
until you awaken them from sleep, teeming with six-legged bees, with your pure, unsurpassable splendours. [59]

6.1.s:
udyaṃtamaṃbaratale surasiddhasaṃghāḥ sabrahmadaityamunikinnaranāgayakṣāḥ ..
tvāmarcayaṃti vibudhāḥ praṇataiḥ śirobhiścañcatkirīṭamaṇibhābhiranuttamābhiḥ .. 5.1.32.60 ..
astaṃ gate tvayi jagadbhavati prasuptaṃ bhūyastvayi pratapati pratibodhameti ..
evaṃ sadā varada lokahitārthahetorekastvameva bhagavaṃstimirasya haṃtā .. 61 ..
utsāhaśaktinayaśauryasamanvitānāṃ sevāprayogaracanāvidhitatparāṇām ..
kāryāṇi yanna phaladāni bhavaṃti puṃsāṃ hetustvabhaktiriha nātha veti nūnam ..62 62 ..
yatsaṃyugeṣu rathakuñjarakuntaśaktinārācacakraśaratomarabhīmakhaḍgaiḥ ..
kṣipraṃ narāḥ samupayāṃti vijitya śatrūnsarvaṃ sadā praṇatavatsala veṣṭitaṃ te .. 63 ..
kāṃtāradurgaviṣameṣvapi vartamānā ṛkṣebhasiṃhabahukaṇṭakataskareṣu ..
tṛṣṇānvitāśca bahuśokavimūḍhacittāstvatkīrtanāddhi gatamṛtyu bhayā bhavaṃti .. 64 ..
6.1.d:
उद्यंतमंबरतले सुरसिद्धसंघाः सब्रह्मदैत्यमुनिकिन्नरनागयक्षाः ..
त्वामर्चयंति विबुधाः प्रणतैः शिरोभिश्चञ्चत्किरीटमणिभाभिरनुत्तमाभिः .. 5.1.32.60 ..
अस्तं गते त्वयि जगद्भवति प्रसुप्तं भूयस्त्वयि प्रतपति प्रतिबोधमेति ..
एवं सदा वरद लोकहितार्थहेतोरेकस्त्वमेव भगवंस्तिमिरस्य हंता .. 61 ..
उत्साहशक्तिनयशौर्यसमन्वितानां सेवाप्रयोगरचनाविधितत्पराणाम् ..
कार्याणि यन्न फलदानि भवंति पुंसां हेतुस्त्वभक्तिरिह नाथ वेति नूनम् ..62 62 ..
यत्संयुगेषु रथकुञ्जरकुन्तशक्तिनाराचचक्रशरतोमरभीमखड्गैः ..
क्षिप्रं नराः समुपयांति विजित्य शत्रून्सर्वं सदा प्रणतवत्सल वेष्टितं ते .. 63 ..
कांतारदुर्गविषमेष्वपि वर्तमाना ऋक्षेभसिंहबहुकण्टकतस्करेषु ..
तृष्णान्विताश्च बहुशोकविमूढचित्तास्त्वत्कीर्तनाद्धि गतमृत्यु भया भवंति .. 64 ..
6.1.m:
As you rise in the sky, hosts of gods and perfected beings, along with Brahmā, daityas, seers, kinnaras, nāgas, and yakṣas—
the gods worship you with bowed heads, with the unsurpassable lustre of jewels on their trembling diadems. [5.1.32.60]
When you have set, the world falls asleep; when you shine forth again, it awakes;
thus ever, O boon-giver, for the sake of the world’s welfare, you alone, O Lord, are the destroyer of darkness. [61]
When the undertakings of men endowed with zeal, power, policy, and valour,
intent on the performance of service and proper application, bear no fruit, the cause here, O Lord, is surely lack of devotion to you. [62]
When in battles, with chariots, elephants, lances, javelins, iron arrows, discuses, shafts, javelins, and dreadful swords,
men quickly return having conquered enemies, all that, O you who are affectionate to the suppliant, is always your deed. [63]
Even those dwelling in wildernesses, fortresses, and uneven terrains, among bears, elephants, lions, numerous thorns, and thieves,
seized by thirst and their minds bewildered by immense sorrow, become freed from the fear of death through the recitation of your name. [64]

6.1.s:
tejorāśistvamiha śaraṇaṃ sarvatoduḥkhitānāṃ
tvattulyo'nyo jagati sakale nāsti kaściddayāluḥ ..
tvayyekasminbhavati sakalā bhaktiranviṣyamāṇā
tvāmāsādya prabhavati kuto vyādhiduḥkhaṃ narāṇām.. 65 ..
kaḥ kuṣṭhābhihataḥ kva cāribhiratho ko vyādhibhiḥ pīḍitaḥ
ke paṃgvaṃdhajaḍāḥ kva śīrṇacaraṇaḥ ko vā vipannakriyaḥ ..
ityevaṃ prasamīkṣya deva kṛpayā doṣātparitrāyase
kasyānyasya paropakāraniratā ceṣṭā yathaiṣā tava .. 66 ..
dharmaḥ paratra kila tiṣṭhati sevito'sau
kālāṃtareṇa vibudhā varadā bhavaṃti ..
tvaṃ sevitaḥ praṇatavatsala bhūtikāmaiḥ
sadyaḥ prayacchasi phalaṃ yadabhīpsitaṃ taiḥ .. 67 ..
vibhrāṃtakāṃtahariṇīsadṛśekṣaṇābhiḥ
kāṃtoruhāramaṇikuṇḍalamekhalābhiḥ ..
teṣāṃ bhavaṃti bhavanāni vilāsinībhiryeṣāṃ nṛṇāṃ tvamasi vai varadaḥ prasannaḥ .. 68 ..
6.1.d:
तेजोराशिस्त्वमिह शरणं सर्वतोदुःखितानां
त्वत्तुल्योऽन्यो जगति सकले नास्ति कश्चिद्दयालुः ..
त्वय्येकस्मिन्भवति सकला भक्तिरन्विष्यमाणा
त्वामासाद्य प्रभवति कुतो व्याधिदुःखं नराणाम्.. 65 ..
कः कुष्ठाभिहतः क्व चारिभिरथो को व्याधिभिः पीडितः
के पंग्वंधजडाः क्व शीर्णचरणः को वा विपन्नक्रियः ..
इत्येवं प्रसमीक्ष्य देव कृपया दोषात्परित्रायसे
कस्यान्यस्य परोपकारनिरता चेष्टा यथैषा तव .. 66 ..
धर्मः परत्र किल तिष्ठति सेवितोऽसौ
कालांतरेण विबुधा वरदा भवंति ..
त्वं सेवितः प्रणतवत्सल भूतिकामैः
सद्यः प्रयच्छसि फलं यदभीप्सितं तैः .. 67 ..
विभ्रांतकांतहरिणीसदृशेक्षणाभिः
कांतोरुहारमणिकुण्डलमेखलाभिः ..
तेषां भवंति भवनानि विलासिनीभिर्येषां नृणां त्वमसि वै वरदः प्रसन्नः .. 68 ..
6.1.m:
You are a mass of splendour, the refuge here for the afflicted on every side;
there is none other so compassionate in the entire world.
In you alone all devotion sought after is found;
having reached you, whence can the sorrow of disease arise for men? [65]
Who is struck down by leprosy, where are those afflicted by enemies, and who is tormented by diseases?
Who are the lame, blind, and dumb, where is the one with withered feet, or who is ruined in ritual acts?
Observing thus, O god, out of compassion you deliver [them] from affliction;
whose other effort is thus intent upon helping others as this of yours? [66]
Righteousness, when cultivated, stands ready in the hereafter, they say;
the gods become granters of boons only after a lapse of time.
You, when served by those desirous of prosperity, O you who are affectionate to the suppliant,
instantly bestow the fruit that they desire. [67]
With wanton women whose eyes resemble those of startled lovely does,
and who wear lovely necklaces, jewels, earrings, and girdles,
the mansions of those men abound, to whom you, gracious one, grant boons. [68]

6.1.s:
yaistvaṃ naraiḥ sakṛdapi praṇataḥ kathaṃciddhyāto'thavā bhuvananātha tathāṃtakāle ..
niṣkalmaṣā jagati duṣkṛtino bhavaṃti te nirmalāḥ sukṛtino gatimāpnuvaṃti .. 69 ..
ye tvāṃ kutarkamatibhirna namaṃti bhaktyā romāṃcakaṃcukaśatākulitaiḥ śarīraiḥ ..
te nirdhanāḥ paragṛheṣvavabhūtamannaṃ kṣutkṣāmakaṇṭhavadanāḥ paritarkayaṃti .. 5.1.32.70 ..
udadhijalataraṃgakṣobhalolākṣiyugmaiḥ saphaṇimaṇimayūkhodbhāsitairlelihadbhiḥ ..
praṇipatitaśirobhirnāgamukhyairajasraṃ śrutibhiranupamābhiḥ stūyase puṣkalābhiḥ .. 71 ..
tava suravara gacchato'nusaraṃti tridaśanadīkamalodga tāni vātaiḥ ..
kanakakamalareṇupiṃjaritāni bhramarakulāni pataṃga cāmarāṇi .. 72 ..
tattvadhyānaṃ jalanidhinivahe sthitvā sthitvā caraṇanivahaiḥ ..
ājīvārthaṃ pratapasi bhagavankaste tulyastribhuvanasamaye .. 73 ..
6.1.d:
यैस्त्वं नरैः सकृदपि प्रणतः कथंचिद्ध्यातोऽथवा भुवननाथ तथांतकाले ..
निष्कल्मषा जगति दुष्कृतिनो भवंति ते निर्मलाः सुकृतिनो गतिमाप्नुवंति .. 69 ..
ये त्वां कुतर्कमतिभिर्न नमंति भक्त्या रोमांचकंचुकशताकुलितैः शरीरैः ..
ते निर्धनाः परगृहेष्ववभूतमन्नं क्षुत्क्षामकण्ठवदनाः परितर्कयंति .. 5.1.32.70 ..
उदधिजलतरंगक्षोभलोलाक्षियुग्मैः सफणिमणिमयूखोद्भासितैर्लेलिहद्भिः ..
प्रणिपतितशिरोभिर्नागमुख्यैरजस्रं श्रुतिभिरनुपमाभिः स्तूयसे पुष्कलाभिः .. 71 ..
तव सुरवर गच्छतोऽनुसरंति त्रिदशनदीकमलोद्ग तानि वातैः ..
कनककमलरेणुपिंजरितानि भ्रमरकुलानि पतंग चामराणि .. 72 ..
तत्त्वध्यानं जलनिधिनिवहे स्थित्वा स्थित्वा चरणनिवहैः ..
आजीवार्थं प्रतपसि भगवन्कस्ते तुल्यस्त्रिभुवनसमये .. 73 ..
6.1.m:
By whichever men you are bowed to even once in any way, or meditated upon, O Lord of the World, even at the hour of death,
even wrongdoers become free of stain in the world, and spotless, doers of good deeds, they attain the supreme goal. [69]
Those who, through minds prone to fallacious reasoning, do not bow to you with devotion, / their bodies thrilled with hundreds of bristling hairs,
penniless, with faces and throats emaciated by hunger, / look about wistfully for food discarded in others' homes. (70)
With pairs of eyes darting about from the agitations of ocean waves, / illuminated by the rays of the gems upon their hoods, licking their lips,
with bowed heads, the foremost of serpents unceasingly / praise you with peerless, copious Vedic hymns. (71)
O foremost of gods, as you move across the sky, / swarms of bees rising from the lotuses of the heavenly river, driven by breezes,
yellowed with the pollen of golden lotuses, / follow you, fluttering like fly-whisks, O Sun. (72)
Fixing your deep contemplation upon reality, resting again and again in the mass of waters / with multitudes of your rays,
you blaze forth, O Lord, for the sustenance of life. / Who is equal to you in the order of the three worlds? (73)

6.1.s:
udayādrinitaṃbasaṃsthitasya hyudayeṣvastamayeṣu cāvṛtasya ..
kiraṇāstapanīyasaprabhāste vilasantastaḍito viḍaṃbayaṃti .. 74 ..
yathāyathā vrajati rathastavāṃbare vipāṭayandhanatimiraughasaṃcayān ..
tathātathā kṣubhitamahānilāsṛtaṃ pratīyate muhuriva dundubhiryathā .. 75 ..

kāminīmiva ratiśramālasāṃ tāṃ vibodhayasi padminīṃ karaiḥ .. 76 ..

tvatprabhābhiranurāgaraṃjitaṃ padmarāgamiva śobhate bhṛśam .. 77 ..
sphuracchaśāṃkahāranirmalaṃ khaga tvadaṃkeṣvacaṃcalam ..
vibhātyatīva kāṃtamaṃbaraṃ samaṃ bṛhaccaika pāṭalam.. 78 ..

6.1.d:
उदयाद्रिनितंबसंस्थितस्य ह्युदयेष्वस्तमयेषु चावृतस्य ..
किरणास्तपनीयसप्रभास्ते विलसन्तस्तडितो विडंबयंति .. 74 ..
यथायथा व्रजति रथस्तवांबरे विपाटयन्धनतिमिरौघसंचयान् ..
तथातथा क्षुभितमहानिलासृतं प्रतीयते मुहुरिव दुन्दुभिर्यथा .. 75 ..
चारुपद्मविनिमीलितेक्षणां चक्रवाककलहंसमेखलाम् ..
कामिनीमिव रतिश्रमालसां तां विबोधयसि पद्मिनीं करैः .. 76 ..
नीललोलमतिकान्तमुत्पलं भृंगतुंगचरणाकुलीकृतम् ..
त्वत्प्रभाभिरनुरागरंजितं पद्मरागमिव शोभते भृशम् .. 77 ..
स्फुरच्छशांकहारनिर्मलं खग त्वदंकेष्वचंचलम् ..
विभात्यतीव कांतमंबरं समं बृहच्चैक पाटलम्.. 78 ..
हरिति च तावन्मुहिर्निषेविततमस्यशुभं भवति च यावदैव किरणैस्तव पूजिततरम् ..
6.1.m:
Resting upon the slopes of the mountain of dawn, / and veiled during your rising and your setting,
your rays, flashing with the splendor of molten gold, / resemble brilliant flashes of lightning. (74)
The more your chariot moves across the firmament, / rending asunder the dense accumulations of darkness,
the more it is perceived, stirred by the rushing great wind, / sounding again and again like a war-drum. (75)
Her eyes closed like lovely lotus blooms, / girdled by the cackling ruddy geese and swans,
like an impassioned woman languid from love's fatigue, / that lotus-cluster you awaken with your rays. (76)
The dark-blue, trembling, exceedingly lovely blue water-lily, / stirred by the raised legs of the bees,
colored by red glow through your radiance, / shines intensely like a ruby. (77)
Spotless as a glistening necklace of moons, O bird of the sky, / resting motionless within your laps,
the sky shines exceedingly lovely, / uniformly vast and rose-red. (78)
And in the green quarters of the sky, misfortune from darkness is dispelled again and again, / as long as it is thoroughly adored by your rays.

6.1.s:
ṛṣibhirmunibhirudāradhībhiḥ śāśva tamārgaparairvarada na śakyate tava guṇastutirāśrayitum .. 79 ..

āditya bhāskara divākara saptasapte mārtaṃḍa sūrya haridaśvapate ca bhāno ..

prāgdigvadhūtilakabhāsurakarṇapūra maṃdākinīdayitanātha jagatpradīpa ..
6.1.d:
ऋषिभिर्मुनिभिरुदारधीभिः शाश्व तमार्गपरैर्वरद न शक्यते तव गुणस्तुतिराश्रयितुम् .. 79 ..

By seers, by sages of exalted intellects / devoted to the eternal path, O granter of boons, your praises cannot be fully reached. (79)
You are Viṣṇu, you are the moon, you are the crusher of demons, you are six-faced Kārttikeya, you are the lord of wealth, you are Time, and you are the Creator, you have your refuge in the mountains and Malaya, you are the sacrificial fire,
you are the sacred syllable Oṃ for brahmins, you are the ocean here, you are the arrow and you are Rudra, you are the foremost, you are the rain-cloud, you are observances, restraints, and disciplines, you are the entire world. (80)
O blameless one, O lord of rays, O smiter of the three cities, O burner of love, O destroyer of the terrible pride of demons, protect me!
You have the face of a noble lotus, O lord of the gods, you are the teacher of the gods here, O Lord. / Who in the orb of the three worlds is equal to you in virtues? (81)
O Āditya, O light-maker, O creator of day, O you with seven horses, O Mārtaṇḍa, O Sūrya, O master of the tawny horses, and O Bhānu,
O you whose steeds never tire, O sky-formed one, O you garlanded with rays, / this person takes refuge in you, O protector of the world! (82)

O scorcher of the golden mountain, O captivating jewel of the sky, / O redness on the face of the maiden of twilight, salutations, salutations to you! (83)
O reality of Brahman itself, O auspicious and beneficial one, O protector of the world, / O master of the courtyard of the sky, O praised by sages, O universal form,
O dispeller of the sorrow of the afflicted, O protector of your servants, / be gracious unto me who have come for refuge, O Lord! (84)
Placing folded hands upon my head like a lotus bud, / as you have been praised today by me with devotion here, O god,
by virtue of that, O Lord, turn a gentle countenance toward me; / make my mind ever intent on righteousness, and grant immense prosperity. (85)
Salutations to Savitṛ, the sole eye of the universe, / the cause of the birth, preservation, and dissolution of the universe,
composed of the three Vedas, bearing the nature of the three qualities, / whose self is Viriñci, Nārāyaṇa, and Śaṃkara. (86)
Sūrya said:

I shall gladly grant you a boon, whatever is in your heart. (87)

And especially to the heroic, there is nothing that cannot be given with all heart." (88)

"This indeed is the boon for me, best of the best boons:
Be present right here at all times, O Lord, O god! (89)
And whatever human beings shall praise you with devotion, ever bowing down,
to them may wealth, grain, sons, wives, and other treasures, (90)
and all desires of the heart be given—this indeed is my boon."
Sanatkumāra said:
Āditya, having granted him the boon, spoke these auspicious words: (91)
"Whatever foremost man will praise me with this hymn composed by you,
there shall be no fall from fortune for him; this is my boon." (92)

6.1.m: Vyāsa said: / "O venerable one, the māhātmya of the sacred field has been described properly, / the highest sacred ford among sacred fords, increasing the merit of meritorious things. / How many sacred fords are there here, and likewise how many liṅgas? / Pray tell, by your grace, to me who am now asking." / Sanatkumāra said: / "Sixty thousand crores and sixty hundred crores— / in the forest of Mahākāla, O Vyāsa, there is no end to the number of liṅgas. / Whatever person is born here, whether free from desire or having desire, / in the delightful forest of Mahākāla, is honored in the world of Śiva. / Sacred fords fulfill desires, as do shrines and temples; / bathing in them and becoming purified, one is honored in the world of Śiva. / All sacred fords are meritorious, abodes of perfections on all sides; / know this sacred field, and likewise this highest sacred ford, to be the foremost among them. / Whoever hears this with great devotion goes to the supreme state." / Thus ends the thirty-ninth chapter, named 'Description of the Māhātmya of the Forest of Mahākāla,' in the Avantīkṣetramāhātmya in the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.

6.1.s: devāḥ saṃti sadā tatra tīrthāni vividhāni ca .. 17 ..
6.1.d: देवाः संति सदा तत्र तीर्थानि विविधानि च .. 17 ..
6.1.m: The gods are always there, and diverse tīrthas.

6.1.s: pūrvakalpe sthito'haṃ ca yatra tvaṃ keśavastathā ..

6.1.m: Where in a former kalpa I was situated, and you, as well as Keśava.

6.1.s: tāmeva ca purīṃ draṣṭuṃ sarve lokā hyavaṃtikām .. 18 ..
6.1.d: तामेव च पुरीं द्रष्टुं सर्वे लोका ह्यवंतिकाम् .. 18 ..
6.1.m: And to see that very city, Avantikā, all the worlds,
as well as divine seers, siddhas, yakṣas, kiṃnaras, and dānavas,
came along with Sthāṇu and Vedhas, whose origin is Brahman.
Likewise, excellent women, exceedingly dear to the gods,
flew down by the thousands to behold that most wondrous city.

6.1.s: āgatya ca yadā devaḥ saha devairmaheśvaraḥ ..
6.1.d: आगत्य च यदा देवः सह देवैर्महेश्वरः ..
6.1.m: And when the god Maheśvara, having arrived with the gods,
looked upon that lovely city, he saw it thus surrounded
by palaces endowed with golden pinnacles and adorned with jewels and gems.
For the blessed lord Viśvarūpa, king and sole ruler of the universe,
resides there in a beautiful, divine palace adorned with gems,
served by gods, siddhas, munis, vidyādharas, and uragas."

6.1.s: tato maheśaśca pitāmahaśca sametya taṃ viśvapatiṃ nanaṃdatuḥ ..
6.1.d: ततो महेशश्च पितामहश्च समेत्य तं विश्वपतिं ननंदतुः ..
6.1.m: Then Maheśa and Pitāmaha, having approached that lord of the universe, rejoiced;
honored by him with respect as was fitting along with their followers, he asked the reason for their arrival:

6.1.s: kimāgatau vā tridivānmahītalaṃ sahānugāvāśa yakaśca kathyatām ..
6.1.d: किमागतौ वा त्रिदिवान्महीतलं सहानुगावाश यकश्च कथ्यताम् ..
6.1.m: "Have you two come down from heaven to the surface of the earth with your retinues? Speak your intention."

6.1.s: tatastu tāvūcaturabjajeśvarau bhavāntare yatra ca tatra nau ratiḥ .. 25 ..
6.1.d: ततस्तु तावूचतुरब्जजेश्वरौ भवान्तरे यत्र च तत्र नौ रतिः .. 25 ..
6.1.m: Then those two, the lotus-born [Brahmā] and Īśvara, said: "Where you are, there is our delight in existence after existence.

6.1.s: tvayā vinā naiva surālaye sukhaṃ mahītale vātha rasātale' sti naḥ ..
6.1.d: त्वया विना नैव सुरालये सुखं महीतले वाथ रसातले' स्ति नः ..
6.1.m: Without you, we have no happiness in heaven, nor on the surface of the earth, nor in Rasātala.

6.1.s: kadā tvayā kāṃcanaśekharā purī niveśitā veśmavatī vicitritā .. 26 ..
6.1.d: कदा त्वया कांचनशेखरा पुरी निवेशिता वेश्मवती विचित्रिता .. 26 ..
6.1.m: When was this city with golden pinnacles, endowed with varied mansions, founded by you?"
Hari said:

6.1.s: tvadarthameveśa viśeṣaśālinī sṛṣṭā hi vai sarvaguṇākarā mayā ..
6.1.d: त्वदर्थमेवेश विशेषशालिनी सृष्टा हि वै सर्वगुणाकरा मया ..
6.1.m: "For your sake alone, O Īśa, was this most excellent [city], a mine of all virtues, created by me.

6.1.s: prayaccha viśveśvara cāvayoriha sthānaṃ ca tīrthaṃ pralaye'kṣayaṃ ca .. 27 ..
6.1.d: प्रयच्छ विश्वेश्वर चावयोरिह स्थानं च तीर्थं प्रलयेऽक्षयं च .. 27 ..
6.1.m: [They said:] 'O Lord of the Universe, grant us two here an abode and a tīrtha that is imperishable at the dissolution of the world.'
[Hari said:] 'I grant the desired abode to you two here: O Prajāpati, your station is to the north;

6.1.s: maheśvara tvaṃ vraja dakṣiṇālayaṃ sthānaṃ sudattaṃ yuvayoḥ suśobhanam .. 28 ..
6.1.d: महेश्वर त्वं व्रज दक्षिणालयं स्थानं सुदत्तं युवयोः सुशोभनम् .. 28 ..
6.1.m: O Maheśvara, go to the southern abode; an exquisite abode has been well bestowed on you two.'
Mahākāla, the lord and soul of the universe, is stationed with downward flames,
the Supreme Lord, honored by many thousands of gaṇas.
"This city was created for sport by [me], desiring the welfare of all beings;
today it is given to you two by me, leaving my own mountain.
Because it was called 'Golden-Pinnacled' (Hemaśṛṅgā) by you two,
the city will be renowned in the world as Kanakaśṛṅgā.
Thus 'Kanakaśṛṅgā' is spoken of as its first name."
And where Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara dwell, uttering prayers,
they constantly delight, granting the fruit of every wish to their devotees.

6.1.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe'vantīkṣetramāhātmye kanakaśṛṅgābhidhānavṛttāṃtavarṇanaṃnāma catvāriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 40 .. .. cha ..
6.1.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डेऽवन्तीक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये कनकशृङ्गाभिधानवृत्तांतवर्णनंनाम चत्वारिंशोऽध्यायः .. 40 .. .. छ ..
6.1.m: Thus ends the fortieth chapter, named 'Description of the Account of the Name Kanakaśṛṅgā', in the Avantīkṣetramāhātmya of the fifth Avantīkhaṇḍa, in the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].
Sanatkumāra said:

6.1.s: śṛṇu vyāsa yatheyaṃ tu procyate hi kuśasthalī ..
6.1.d: शृणु व्यास यथेयं तु प्रोच्यते हि कुशस्थली ..
6.1.m: Listen, O Vyāsa, how this Kuśasthalī is spoken of
by the wise knowers of the Veda in the former Tatpuruṣa kalpa.
The universe was created by Vedhas with daityas, dānavas, and rākṣasas,
infatuated with mutual pride and hating one another in battle.
The gods and dānavas were constantly engaged in rivalry in combat;
men [fought] with men, along with siddhas and vidyādharas;
cāraṇas with kiṃnaras—thus intent on hostility,
they waged war constantly with indistinct speech.

6.1.s: sarve caiva ca balino durbalairmanujaiḥ saha ..
6.1.d: सर्वे चैव च बलिनो दुर्बलैर्मनुजैः सह ..
6.1.m: And all the strong [fought] against weak men;

6.1.s: paśavaḥ paśubhiḥ sārdhaṃ pakṣiṇaḥ saha pakṣibhiḥ .. 5 ..
6.1.d: पशवः पशुभिः सार्धं पक्षिणः सह पक्षिभिः .. 5 ..
6.1.m: beasts [fought] with beasts, and birds with birds.
"Seeing this world thus transgressing all bounds,

6.1.s: dṛṣṭvā viśvasya kartāraṃ viṣṇuṃ viśveśvaraṃ param .. 6 ..
6.1.d: दृष्ट्वा विश्वस्य कर्तारं विष्णुं विश्वेश्वरं परम् .. 6 ..
6.1.m: one against another and with others, [I go for refuge] to Viṣṇu, the maker of the universe, the supreme Lord of the universe;
I go for refuge to the god Hari, who takes away the distress of those who seek refuge."

6.1.s: evaṃ manasi saṃdhāya dadhyau dhyānena mādhavam .. 7 ..
6.1.d: एवं मनसि संधाय दध्यौ ध्यानेन माधवम् .. 7 ..
6.1.m: Having thus resolved in his mind, he meditated upon Mādhava in meditation.
Then, having been meditated upon, Hari, the great yogin who bears the universal form
and wields an iron staff, glorious, spoke thus to the Grandfather:
"O Brahmā, I have been properly meditated upon by you through the yoga of meditation. Behold me
approaching, meditated upon in this way, ready to protect the worlds."
Then the Creator, having heard this, relinquished meditation and, beholding him,
stood up with single-minded focus, bowed down, and worshipped Keśava again
with water for the feet, water for sipping, and honey-mixture.
Having worshipped him, the lotus-born [Brahmā] again addressed Acyuta:
Brahmā said:
"O God of gods, O Lord of the world, this universe was created by you;
without you, O Viṣṇu, the world cannot endure at all.

6.1.s: śāstā tvamasya viśvasya viśuddhasya ca nāparaḥ ..
6.1.d: शास्ता त्वमस्य विश्वस्य विशुद्धस्य च नापरः ..
6.1.m: You alone are the ruler of this pure universe, and none other;
this entire world has its being from you, therefore do you govern it.
The gods, Dānavas, Gandharvas, together with Yakṣas, serpents, and Rākṣasas,
whose bodies encompass all, without you, O lotus-eyed one,

6.1.s: parasparaṃ vinighnaṃti tāṃśca tvaṃ rakṣituṃ kṣamaḥ .. 14 ..
6.1.d: परस्परं विनिघ्नंति तांश्च त्वं रक्षितुं क्षमः .. 14 ..
6.1.m: slay one another; and you are capable of protecting them.

6.1.s: tvamasya viśvasya carācarasya sthiteḥ sadā prāṇabhṛdātmarūpiṇī .. 15 ..
6.1.d: त्वमस्य विश्वस्य चराचरस्य स्थितेः सदा प्राणभृदात्मरूपिणी .. 15 ..
6.1.m: You are the embodiment of the Self that sustains the breath for the maintenance of this universe of moving and unmoving beings.

6.1.s: tvayā dhṛtaṃ sarvamidaṃ jagadvai yatastato'si tvamupendrasaṃjñaḥ ..
6.1.d: त्वया धृतं सर्वमिदं जगद्वै यतस्ततोऽसि त्वमुपेन्द्रसंज्ञः ..
6.1.m: Because all this universe is indeed supported by you, therefore you are named Upendra;

6.1.s: praveśanaṃ vyāptamidaṃ svadhāma yattvamucyase viṣṇurato munīṃdraiḥ .. 16 ..
6.1.d: प्रवेशनं व्याप्तमिदं स्वधाम यत्त्वमुच्यसे विष्णुरतो मुनींद्रैः .. 16 ..
6.1.m: because your own abode has entered and pervaded this [world], therefore you are called Viṣṇu by the foremost sages.

6.1.s: nivāsitaṃ viśvamidaṃ tvayādya vāsaśca dhātoriti vāsudevaḥ ..
6.1.d: निवासितं विश्वमिदं त्वयाद्य वासश्च धातोरिति वासुदेवः ..
6.1.m: This universe has now been made an abode by you, and from the root vas ('to dwell') [you are called] Vāsudeva;
this universe follows you; you are the all-pervading Lord, shining forth as the king of the entire universe.

6.1.s: senānurūpaṃ jagadeva yasmādataḥ smṛtastvaṃ kila viśvasenaḥ ..
6.1.d: सेनानुरूपं जगदेव यस्मादतः स्मृतस्त्वं किल विश्वसेनः ..
6.1.m: Because the universe is indeed suitable for your army, therefore you are recalled as Viṣvaksena;
and from furrowing this moving and unmoving world, and from the root kṛ ('to do'), you are therefore Kṛṣṇa.

6.1.s: jitaṃ tvayā deva jagattrayaṃ yajjiteśca dhātostvamato'si jiṣṇuḥ ..
6.1.d: जितं त्वया देव जगत्त्रयं यज्जितेश्च धातोस्त्वमतोऽसि जिष्णुः ..
6.1.m: Because the three worlds have been conquered by you, O God, from the root ji ('to conquer') you are therefore Jiṣṇu;
therefore, O all-pervading Lord, protect forever the world together with all its planets and world-guardians.
You are the primordial king of all this; may your auspicious throne be unequalled!
The conch, coiling to the right, held in your hand, graces the Supreme Person.

6.1.s: sudarśanaṃ nāma tavāsti cakramato hi gītaḥ kavibhi stu cakrī ..
6.1.d: सुदर्शनं नाम तवास्ति चक्रमतो हि गीतः कविभि स्तु चक्री ..
6.1.m: Your discus is named Sudarśana, hence you are praised by the poets as Cakrin;

6.1.s: dhvajo'sti te deva suparṇasevitastathāsuparṇaśca tavāsti vāhanam ..21..
6.1.d: ध्वजोऽस्ति ते देव सुपर्णसेवितस्तथासुपर्णश्च तवास्ति वाहनम् ..21..
6.1.m: your banner, O God, is adorned by Suparṇa, and Suparṇa is also your mount.

6.1.s: turaṃgamāḥ saṃtu tavārisaṃhare tathā hṛṣīkeśa sudantadantinaḥ..
6.1.d: तुरंगमाः संतु तवारिसंहरे तथा हृषीकेश सुदन्तदन्तिनः..
6.1.m: May horses be yours in the destruction of your foes, and likewise tusked elephants with fine tusks, O Hṛṣīkeśa!
Adorned with diadems, coins, armlets, ear-ornaments, bracelets, necklaces, and excellent gold chains,
and with wondrous garments and excellent red garlands, become Bhīmasena.

6.1.s: śriyā kadācicca na mucyate bhavānbhavaṃ ti te nityamanaṃtasaṃpadaḥ .. 23 ..
6.1.d: श्रिया कदाचिच्च न मुच्यते भवान्भवं ति ते नित्यमनंतसंपदः .. 23 ..
6.1.m: You are never parted from Śrī; endless riches are perpetually yours.

6.1.s: tavānugā bhaktirihāstu vai satī mukunda bhakte tvamataḥ prasīda me .. 24 ..
6.1.d: तवानुगा भक्तिरिहास्तु वै सती मुकुन्द भक्ते त्वमतः प्रसीद मे .. 24 ..
6.1.m: May faithful devotion here follow you, O Mukunda; therefore, be gracious to me, your devotee!"
Sanatkumāra said:

6.1.s: sa evamuktastu puro divaukasāṃ vibhuḥ prasannastvidamabravīddharaḥ ..
6.1.d: स एवमुक्तस्तु पुरो दिवौकसां विभुः प्रसन्नस्त्विदमब्रवीद्धरः ..
6.1.m: Being thus addressed before the gods, the gracious all-pervading Lord, the bearer [of the world], said this:

6.1.s: viriṃca me darśaya tasya maṃḍalaṃ tvayā vimuktaṃ ca sadāśivaṃ vibho .. 25 ..
6.1.d: विरिंच मे दर्शय तस्य मंडलं त्वया विमुक्तं च सदाशिवं विभो .. 25 ..
6.1.m: "O Viriñci, show me that region which has been set apart by you, and which is ever-auspicious, O Lord,

6.1.s: sthiraṃ sthi yatra jagatkaromyahaṃ tato viraṃciḥ kuśamuṣṭimādade ..
6.1.d: स्थिरं स्थि यत्र जगत्करोम्यहं ततो विरंचिः कुशमुष्टिमाददे ..
6.1.m: where I may make the universe firm and established." Then Viriñci took a handful of kuśa grass

6.1.s: pavitradeśasya nidarśanāya jagāma puṇyaṃ cyavanāśramaṃ tadā .. 26 ..
6.1.d: पवित्रदेशस्य निदर्शनाय जगाम पुण्यं च्यवनाश्रमं तदा .. 26 ..
6.1.m: to point out the pure site, and went then to the sacred hermitage of Cyavana.
Then, having reached a higher ground, the Grandfather spoke with respect to Keśava:

6.1.s: tvadudbhavaṃ cātra pavitramaṃḍalaṃ tvayā vimuktaṃ ca sadā śivaṃ vibho .. 27 ..
6.1.d: त्वदुद्भवं चात्र पवित्रमंडलं त्वया विमुक्तं च सदा शिवं विभो .. 27 ..
6.1.m: "Here is the pure region sprung from you, set apart by you, and ever-auspicious, O Lord.

6.1.s: tvameva viṣṇurvibudhārcitaḥ sadā smṛto munīṃdraiḥ sa ca viṣṭaraśravāḥ ..
6.1.d: त्वमेव विष्णुर्विबुधार्चितः सदा स्मृतो मुनींद्रैः स च विष्टरश्रवाः ..
6.1.m: You alone are Viṣṇu, ever worshipped by the gods, and celebrated by the foremost sages as Viṣṭaraśravas;

6.1.s: niṣīda viśveśa kuśasthalaṃ yadā tadāśrito mādhavamāsarūpavān .. 28 ..
6.1.d: निषीद विश्वेश कुशस्थलं यदा तदाश्रितो माधवमासरूपवान् .. 28 ..
6.1.m: sit down, O Lord of the universe, upon this kuśa-ground, manifesting the form of the month of Mādhava."

6.1.s: kuśasthalīṃ saṃsthita eva deva itthaṃ vidhātrā puruṣottamaḥ stutaḥ ..
6.1.d: कुशस्थलीं संस्थित एव देव इत्थं विधात्रा पुरुषोत्तमः स्तुतः ..
6.1.m: Thus praised by the Creator, the god Puruṣottama, established in Kuśasthalī,
sat down upon that ground strewn with kuśa grass—Kuśasthalī, frequented by gods and foremost sages,

6.1.s: samaṃtato yojanasaṃ khyayāvṛtāṃ tato vidhātā puruṣottamastathā ..
6.1.d: समंततो योजनसं ख्ययावृतां ततो विधाता पुरुषोत्तमस्तथा ..
6.1.m: which was covered on all sides for the measure of a yojana. Then both of them, the Creator and Puruṣottama,

6.1.s: kuśasthalīti prathitaṃ jagattraye pracakraturnāma ca tāvubhāvapi .. 5.1.41.30 ..
6.1.d: कुशस्थलीति प्रथितं जगत्त्रये प्रचक्रतुर्नाम च तावुभावपि .. 5.1.41.30 ..
6.1.m: made the name 'Kuśasthalī' renowned throughout the three worlds.
There the glorious Lord of the universe, the sovereign of the universe, the all-pervading maker of the universe,
the Soul of the universe, the leader of the entire universe, ruled the universe.

6.1.s: evaṃ kuśasthalī khyātā hemaśṛṅgeti yā purā ..
6.1.d: एवं कुशस्थली ख्याता हेमशृङ्गेति या पुरा ..
6.1.m: Thus Kuśasthalī was known, which previously was called Hemaśṛṅgā;

6.1.s: stīrṇā kuśairyato dhātrā kuśasthalī tataḥ smṛtā .. 32 ..
6.1.d: स्तीर्णा कुशैर्यतो धात्रा कुशस्थली ततः स्मृता .. 32 ..
6.1.m: because it was strewn with kuśa grass by the Creator, it is therefore remembered as Kuśasthalī.

6.1.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvaṃtyakhaṇḍe'vantīkṣetramāhātmye vyāsasanatkumārasaṃvāde kuśasthalīnāmahetukathāvarṇanaṃnāmaikacatvāriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 41 .. ... cha .. ..
6.1.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवंत्यखण्डेऽवन्तीक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये व्याससनत्कुमारसंवादे कुशस्थलीनामहेतुकथावर्णनंनामैकचत्वारिंशोऽध्यायः .. 41 .. ... छ .. ..
6.1.m: Thus ends the forty-first chapter, named 'The Description of the Reason for the Name Kuśasthalī,' in the dialogue between Vyāsa and Sanatkumāra, in the Avanti-kṣetra-māhātmya, in the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, of the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa comprising eighty-one thousand verses.
Sanatkumāra said:

6.1.s: purā caiśānakalpe tu smṛtāvaṃtī yathā purī ..
6.1.d: पुरा चैशानकल्पे तु स्मृतावंती यथा पुरी ..
6.1.m: Listen how formerly in the Aiśāna kalpa the city of Avantī was celebrated;
formerly, when defeated by the army of Daityas, the gods
took refuge on the peak of Meru, which was covered with forests, ravines, and caves.

6.1.s: tatra gatvā dvijaśreṣṭha maṃtraṃ ca cakrurudyatāḥ..2..
6.1.d: तत्र गत्वा द्विजश्रेष्ठ मंत्रं च चक्रुरुद्यताः..2..
6.1.m: Having gone there, O best of brahmins, they resolved and held counsel;
and approaching one another and honoring each other,

6.1.s: jagmuḥ sarve suragaṇā yatra brahmā prajāpatiḥ..3..
6.1.d: जग्मुः सर्वे सुरगणा यत्र ब्रह्मा प्रजापतिः..3..
6.1.m: all the hosts of gods went where Brahmā the Prajāpati was.
They announced to him the whole reason for their coming there.

6.1.s: teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā devānāṃ sa prajeśvaraḥ..4..
6.1.d: तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा देवानां स प्रजेश्वरः..4..
6.1.m: Hearing their words, that lord of creatures, the god,
went together with the gods to the god of gods, Maheśvara.

6.1.s: sa cāpi hyagamattatra vaikuṭhaṃ dhāma yatra vai .. 5 ..
6.1.d: स चापि ह्यगमत्तत्र वैकुठं धाम यत्र वै .. 5 ..
6.1.m: And he too went there to Vaikuṇṭha, the abode where indeed
[Viṣṇu resides,] which constantly grants prosperity and perfection, frequented by sages and cāraṇas,
sung by kinnaras, attended by hosts of apsarases,
by seers such as the Bhārgavas, and the best divine seer, Nārada,
by the foremost of siddhas and gandharvas, and by the Kumāras such as Sanaka,
thronged by groups of prajāpatis and the fourteen Manus,
by the Vasus, the Viśvedevas, and the foremost hosts of the ancestors,
and frequented by people of righteous conduct and meritorious deeds;
divine, adorned with divine palaces and divine trees,
divine, beautified with jewel-gem stairs and lakes,
crowded with swans and kāraṇḍava ducks, splendid with the luster of jewels,
a place free from the six waves [of worldly existence], where birds abide.

6.1.s: tatra gatvā surāḥ sarve vāsu devadidṛkṣayā ..
6.1.d: तत्र गत्वा सुराः सर्वे वासु देवदिदृक्षया ..
6.1.m: Having gone there, all the gods, desiring to see Vāsudeva,
began to make a hymn of praise to the god of gods, the lord of the universe.
The gods said:
Obeisance to the infinite, the vast, obeisance and praise to the Tortoise,
to the terrible one who took the form of the Man-Lion, obeisance to the Boar-formed one,
to the descendant of Raghu, Rāma, to Brahman of boundless power,
to Vāsudeva, the tranquil one, to the lord of the Yadus, obeisance!
Obeisance to Buddha, the pure one, to Kalki, the destroyer of barbarians!
To those engaged in this praise, a bodiless voice spoke:

6.1.s: śṛṇudhvaṃ bhoḥ surāḥ sarve bhūtvā caikāgramānasāḥ .. 15 ..
6.1.d: शृणुध्वं भोः सुराः सर्वे भूत्वा चैकाग्रमानसाः .. 15 ..
6.1.m: Listen, O all you gods, having become single-minded:
In the delightful Mahākālavana, frequented by hosts of brahmin seers,
there is a sacred city that yields the fruit of all desires,
delightful, named Kuśasthalī, frequented by siddhas and gandharvas,

6.1.s: kalpādau kalpamadhye vā yatra saṃnihito haraḥ .. 17 ..
6.1.d: कल्पादौ कल्पमध्ये वा यत्र संनिहितो हरः .. 17 ..
6.1.m: where Hara is present at the beginning of a kalpa or in the middle of a kalpa.

6.1.s: kalpakṣaye kṣayaṃ yāṃti sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca ..
6.1.d: कल्पक्षये क्षयं यांति स्थावराणि चराणि च ..
6.1.m: At the dissolution of a kalpa, all stationary and moving beings meet destruction,
as do all sacred fords and holy shrines,
all rivers, all oceans, lakes, and groves,
medicinal herbs, trees and creepers, mechanisms, mantras, good and bad,

6.1.s: jyotīṃṣi caṃdrasūryau ca sarvaṃ viṣṇumayaṃ jagat ..
6.1.d: ज्योतींषि चंद्रसूर्यौ च सर्वं विष्णुमयं जगत् ..
6.1.m: the luminaries, the moon and the sun—the entire universe consisting of Viṣṇu.

6.1.s: teṣāṃ bījaṃ ca puṇyaṃ ca jīvakarmāśaya tathā .. 5.1.42.20 ..
6.1.d: तेषां बीजं च पुण्यं च जीवकर्माशय तथा .. 5.1.42.20 ..
6.1.m: Taking their seed, and the religious merit, and the latent disposition of the living beings' karma—
taking all that, Lord Śaṃkara remains there.
The Gaṅgā contains all sacred fords; Hari embodies all the gods;
the Veda embodies all sacrifices; compassion contains all righteousness;

6.1.s: revā ca saritāṃ śreṣṭhā bhuvi puṇyakṛtādhikā .. 22 ..
6.1.d: रेवा च सरितां श्रेष्ठा भुवि पुण्यकृताधिका .. 22 ..
6.1.m: and the Revā is the best of rivers, excelling in creating merit on earth.
More beneficent than that, O best of gods, is Kurukṣetra;
ten times greater than that, I hold, is Prayāga, the excellent sacred ford.
Ten times greater than that is Kāśī; ten times greater than Kāśī is Gayā;

6.1.s: tato daśaguṇā proktā kuśasthalī ca puṇyadā .. 24 ..
6.1.d: ततो दशगुणा प्रोक्ता कुशस्थली च पुण्यदा .. 24 ..
6.1.m: and ten times greater than that is declared to be merit-giving Kuśasthalī.
Thousands of eclipses, tens of thousands of vyatīpātas,

6.1.s: amālakṣaṃ tu etasyāḥ kalāṃ nārhaṃti ṣoḍaśīm .. 25 ..
6.1.d: अमालक्षं तु एतस्याः कलां नार्हंति षोडशीम् .. 25 ..
6.1.m: and a hundred thousand new-moon days are not worth a sixteenth part of this.
A gift at the waning of the moon yields a hundred thousandfold; at the two solstices, a thousandfold;

6.1.s: vyatīpāte ca koṭiḥ syādrā kāyāṃ ca hyanaṃtakam .. 26 ..
6.1.d: व्यतीपाते च कोटिः स्याद्रा कायां च ह्यनंतकम् .. 26 ..
6.1.m: at a vyatīpāta it yields ten millionfold, and on the full moon day it is indeed infinite.
Therefore, O gods, this city of Kuśasthalī is truly beneficent.
Whatever little gift is made by men becomes counted infinitely infinite;

6.1.s: tatsarvaṃ bhoḥ suraśreṣṭhāḥ sarvaṃ taccākṣayaṃ bhavet ..
6.1.d: तत्सर्वं भोः सुरश्रेष्ठाः सर्वं तच्चाक्षयं भवेत् ..
6.1.m: all of that, O best of gods, all of that becomes imperishable.

6.1.s: tasmātsarvaprayatnena yūyaṃ yāta hi mā ciram .. 28 ..
6.1.d: तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन यूयं यात हि मा चिरम् .. 28 ..
6.1.m: Therefore, go there with all effort and do not delay.

6.1.s: kṣīṇapuṇyā bhavaṃto vai bādhaṃte tena vaḥ surāḥ ..
6.1.d: क्षीणपुण्या भवंतो वै बाधंते तेन वः सुराः ..
6.1.m: Your merit has dwindled, gods; therefore [the demons] torment you.
This city of Kuśasthalī is in the delightful Mahākālavana.

6.1.s: tatra gatvā bhavaṃto vai snānadānādikaṃ bhuvi ..
6.1.d: तत्र गत्वा भवंतो वै स्नानदानादिकं भुवि ..
6.1.m: Having gone there on earth, you should indeed
perform ablutions, gifts, and the like according to the proper rules; through that merit you will regain heaven.
Having heard those words of that voice in the sky at that time,
bowing down with their heads to it, [the gods] headed by Brahmā and Īśāna [departed].

6.1.s: punarjagmuḥ surāḥ sarve yatra māheśvaraṃ vanam ..
6.1.d: पुनर्जग्मुः सुराः सर्वे यत्र माहेश्वरं वनम् ..
6.1.m: All the gods went again to where the forest of Maheśvara was,
and to that city, O best of the twice-born, which grants the fruits of all desires, / 32
crowded with the four social classes, frequented by seers and gandharvas,
filled with meritorious people, frequented by siddhas and cāraṇas, / 33

6.1.s: daridro na jaḍo mūrkho na rogī na ca matsarī ..
6.1.d: दरिद्रो न जडो मूर्खो न रोगी न च मत्सरी ..
6.1.m: where no poor person, no fool, no dullard, no sick person, and no envious person,
no afflicted person, and no wrongdoer was ever seen anywhere; / 34
generous, tranquil, well-behaved, free from old age and disease,
always devoted to their own duties, of good conduct and fond of guests, / 35
men and devoted wives dwell there;
there were great festivals, beautiful songs, and offerings to gods and ancestors in every house. / 36

6.1.s: īdṛśīṃ ca purīṃ dṛṣṭvā devā harṣaṃ paraṃ gatāḥ ..
6.1.d: ईदृशीं च पुरीं दृष्ट्वा देवा हर्षं परं गताः ..
6.1.m: And seeing such a city, the gods reached the highest joy.
There is a sacred ford there well known by the name Paiśācamocana, / 37
always to be resorted to by meritorious people, frequented by all sacred fords.

6.1.s: tasminsnātvā ca japtvā ca hutvā dattvā ca devatāḥ .. 38 ..
6.1.d: तस्मिन्स्नात्वा च जप्त्वा च हुत्वा दत्त्वा च देवताः .. 38 ..
6.1.m: Having bathed there, muttered prayers, offered oblations, and given gifts, the deities, / 38
having obtained inexhaustible merit, then returned to the abode of the gods.
Having defeated the exceedingly wicked asuras, they attained their respective realms. / 39
Those fortunate ones who perform ritual ablution, gifting, and worship here,
fire-offerings, and libations to the ancestors—all that becomes endless. / 5.1.42.40
Therefore, by every effort, this should always be done by the wise;
and the preservation of gods, sacred fords, medicinal herbs, seeds, and living beings / 41

6.1.s: kalpekalpe ca yasyāṃ vai tenāvaṃtī purī smṛtā ..
6.1.d: कल्पेकल्पे च यस्यां वै तेनावंती पुरी स्मृता ..
6.1.m: [occurs] in it in kalpa after kalpa; therefore it is remembered as the city of Avantī.
From this day forward, this city Kuśasthalī shall indeed be named Avantī. / 42

6.1.s: ityuktvā vai tadā devāḥ svadhāma paramaṃ gatāḥ ..
6.1.d: इत्युक्त्वा वै तदा देवाः स्वधाम परमं गताः ..
6.1.m: Having spoken thus, the gods then went to their supreme abode.
Beginning from that time, O best of the twice-born, Avantī became renowned on earth. / 43

6.1.s: ya etāṃ sukathāṃ divyāṃ puṇyāṃ ca pāpahāriṇīm..
6.1.d: य एतां सुकथां दिव्यां पुण्यां च पापहारिणीम्..
6.1.m: Whoever listens to this divine, meritorious narrative that removes sins,
or causes it to be heard, is indeed freed from all sins. / 44
A childless person obtains a son; an impoverished person obtains wealth.
Gaining merit exceeding a thousand Vājapeya sacrifices

6.1.s: puṇyaṃ labdhvā naro nityaṃ śivaloke mahīyate .. 46 ..
6.1.d: पुण्यं लब्ध्वा नरो नित्यं शिवलोके महीयते .. 46 ..
6.1.m: and a hundred Rājasūyas, a man is perpetually honored in the world of Śiva. / 46

6.1.m: Thus ends the forty-second chapter, titled 'Description of the Narrative of the Name of Avantī' in the Avantīkṣetramāhātmya of the fifth Avantyakhaṇḍa, in the Skandamahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses. / 42

6.1.m:
The person who constantly resides in this [city], O highly fortunate one, / having enjoyed all desired pleasures of the mind, goes to Śiva's realm upon death.
There indeed he dwells eternally for more than a hundred crores of kalpas.
Whoever reads or listens to this holy narrative / is freed from all sins and attains the fruit of [gifting] a thousand cows.
Thus ends the forty-third chapter, named 'The Description of the Name Ujjayinī', in the Māhātmya of the Avantī Field, in the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].

6.1.m:
Sanatkumāra said:
At one time, O Vyāsa, how the city came to be remembered as Ujjayanī—
that I will proclaim; listen with an attentive mind. / 1
A great daitya named Tripura, the lord of all daityas,
performed terrible austerity in order to please Brahmā. / 2
Subduing himself in the heat by serving the fire, in the rainy season by facing the mass of clouds,
and in the cold season in a pool of water, / 3
subsisting on fallen leaves and water, feeding on air, without shelter,
devoted to the observance of the Gāyatrī, abandoning all possessions, / 4
thus for a thousand years he performed austerity that was exceedingly difficult to practice.
When the thousand years were completed, Brahmā, highly pleased, said: / 5
'O best of asuras, choose a desired boon from me;
I shall now grant all that boon to you in the world.' / 6
Thus spoken to by the Creator, the daitya named Tripura
immediately spoke these words to Brahmā of strict vows. / 7
Tripura said:
'If, pleased in mind, O Brahmā, you wish to grant me a boon:
may I always be invulnerable to gods, dānavas, gandharvas,
piśācas, serpents, and rākṣasas; this is the boon I choose.' / 8
Brahmā said:
'So be it, O child! Wander about free from fear of anything.'
Having spoken thus, Brahmā vanished right there at once. / 9
Beginning from that time, the great daitya wrought great slaughter upon the gods,
filled with anger as he remembered the former enmity. / 5.1.43.10
Having established the wandering Three Cities here and there,
all the people devoted to their caste and life-stage settled here. / 11
The evil-minded one brought slaughter upon them through various means.
In that city of wicked habitation, the brahmins versed in the Vedas / 12
did not offer the agnihotra, nor did they ever drink soma;
people nowhere performed any good deed, O sage. / 13
Deprived of the call of 'svāhā', the call of 'svadhā', and the call of 'vaṣaṭ',
no festival was seen anywhere spread across the houses on earth. / 14

6.1.m:
There is no temple of the gods, nor any worship of Śiva; / there is no sacrifice, no gifts, and no worship of cows and brahmins.
There is no person of righteous conduct; compassion is entirely discarded. / Neither a donor nor a benefactor nor an ascetic is to be seen.
Thus, O Vyāsa, in that city this world was practically destroyed. / Brahmins are the root of creatures, and the Vedas are the root of brahmins;
sacrifices rest upon the root of the Vedas, and the gods are rooted in sacrifices. / Therefore, O Vyāsa, everything was laid waste by that evil-souled one.
By him all the hosts of gods were practically destroyed and bereft of power; / defeated by him, they wander upon the earth like mortals.
Having formed an alliance with one another and deliberated with focused minds, / they went to where the blemishless Prajāpati resides.
The gods related the cause of their calamity. / Knowing that, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, rose up at once
and went along with the gods to the supreme forest of Mahākāla, / where the god Śiva ever abides with Umā,
where lies the divine city Avantī, resorted to by all sacred fords. / Having arrived there together with the gods, the self-manifest four-faced one,
after performing ritual ablution, gifting, silent prayer, and oblation in the Rudrasaras lake, / and worshipping Mahākāla, Brahmā spoke [these] words:
Brahmā said:
O God of gods, O Mahādeva, who grants fearlessness to devotees! / Listen, O best of gods, to the supreme affair of the gods.
A lord of the Daityas named Tripura is causing great slaughter among the gods; / that Daitya continuously reviles gods and brahmins.
Having established three vast cities, he roams about, / and the beings residing there are led to destruction by that evil-souled one.
Having done so, all living creatures, moving and unmoving, have been brought to ruin; / the continents, villages, and towns have been desolated,
as well as all the hermitages of the seers and the dwellings of the ascetics. / Having done so, all the gods have been deprived of their kingdom and defeated;

6.1.m:
they wander like mortals because of the evil-souled Tripura. / Having obtained a boon from me, he continually wanders without fear of anything.
Therefore, by every effort, his slaying must be devised.
Having heard that speech of Brahmā, whose mind was resolved, / Mahādeva meditated for a long time and said to Brahmā:
Mahādeva said:
Listen, O best among the gods, headed by Brahmā and Indra! / I shall devise a means for the conquest of this evil-souled Daitya.
Or rather, you who desire your own victory, perform austerity! / Whatever is offered into fire or given in Avantī shall become imperishable.
Having spoken thus, Śiva vanished right there before all the gods. / Going to the abode of the cremation ground, inhabited by bhūtas and pretas,
for the sake of conquering that evil-souled Daitya Tripura, / the lords of the gods worshipped Cāmuṇḍā there
with buffaloes and great sacrificial victims, with offerings of animals and flowers, and with libations, / with various offerings, gifts, incense, lamps, and oblations in fire.
Having worshipped the goddess then, the bull-bannered [Śiva] praised her: / Durgā, the fortunate, the auspicious, who ferries across the impassable world of transmigration,
the magical weapon that destroys Tripura, intent on slaying Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa,
intoxicated with pride from the fat of Daityas, named Raktā, with blood-red teeth, / wearing blood-red garments, steadfast, possessed of red flowers, the virtuous wife,
mounted on a buffalo, dark-complexioned, taking a seat upon a yakṣa, / dressed in a leopard skin, with dried flesh, exceedingly terrifying.
Having worshipped her with a serene mind, he stood fixed in meditation. / Then the venerable, auspicious Caṇḍikā, by whom this world is upheld,
having become cheerful of face, visibly said:
The Goddess said:
O best of gods, choose a boon desired from me! / I shall grant all that was spoken by you, which brings benefit to the worlds.
Hara said:
