6.1.m:
If you are pleased, O Goddess, grant me an excellent boon / by which I may slay the great Daitya Tripura, the thorn to the gods.
The Goddess said:
Conquer him indeed, O Mahādeva! Take the supreme Pāśupata [weapon], / granted by me, O best of gods, which is supreme in destroying Daityas!
And taking the great Pāśupata weapon in hand, Śaṃkara, / Śambhu quickly set out then for the destruction of the Daitya.
Becoming one of great majesty, terrifying to all living beings, / he departed after praising [her] with words, and the gods followed behind.
With a single arrow indeed Rudra struck that great Asura. / Having split that illusion-maker into three through a battle of illusions, Śaṃkara
came back again to this city Avantī, frequented by immortals. / Uttering blessings of victory, the seers, Siddhas, and Cāraṇas,
and the gods then praised him, delighted with the shout of victory. / The apsarases danced there; the Gandharvas sang delightfully.
Then the most auspicious wind blew, conferring happiness on men;
at that time the shout of victory arose in every house of living beings. / The fires that were subdued blazed forth, and the [ominous] sounds born of the directions were calmed.
Then sacrifices accompanied by great festivities and priestly fees commenced; / the gods regained their own respected abode.
Since the Dānava was overcome and fame was established in the three worlds, / therefore by all the best of gods and the seers headed by Sanaka,
the name of Avantī was made Ujjayinī, which destroys sin. / And Avantī was previously spoken of as the bestower of all desires and boons.
From this day forward, O Vyāsa, those who take refuge in the city Ujjayinī, / and whatever men on earth perform ritual ablution, gifting, and the like in it,
no evil deed born of sin remains in their body.
One seeking knowledge [should dwell on] the Lord of the Mountain; one seeking wealth, on the Lord of Wealth; one seeking a son, on the Lord of Sons; one seeking happiness, on the Sun;
one seeking wisdom, on the Lord of Gaṇas; one seeking what is dear, and a person who holds the speech [of the scriptures] as authoritative, should indeed dwell in Ujjayinī.
Sanatkumāra said:
Now, therefore, I shall fully explain how [the city] became Padmāvatī.

In the meantime, Nārada, who appears to the gods, arrived. // 5

Sanatkumāra said:
"Listen, O highly fortunate Vyāsa: this city, indeed named Amarāvatī,
is also declared as Viśālā and is sung of in all the worlds.
So I shall recount what was spoken by Brahmā formerly,
a sacred field more secret than the secret, destroying all sins.
The god wandered alone in the forest together with Umā.
Then came all the bhūtagaṇas, and after that all the suras and asuras,
where Viṣṇu of the ten forms, the goddesses, the mothers of the world,
the Vināyakas, Vetālas, Kūṣmāṇḍas, and Bhairavas and others [gathered],
as well as the liṅgas originating across the kalpas, numbering eighty-four,
the sacred fields, the Kṣetrapālas, and likewise Prosperity and Perfection,
the ancestors, the world guardians, the siddhas, and those who grant perfections,
and the highly fortunate seers, the wives of seers of pure intent,
the kinnaras, divine gandharvas, and excellent apsarases,

endowed with divine intention, delightful with divine sites,
furnished with all celestial qualities, vast, stainless, and auspicious,
with markets, towers, and courtyards filled with buying and selling,
filled with many mansions and houses, adorned with rows of palaces,
constructed with crystal walls, with floors of beryl gems,
excellent with coral pillars, abounding in ornaments of gold,
with thresholds of reddish gems, adorned with doorposts,
rich in doors of Jāmbūnada gold, well fitted with diamond bolts,
whose interiors of houses, courtyards, and gateways had floors resembling precious gems,
very delightful with lattices of tinkling ornaments, hung with strings of pearls.
In every house there were banners set upon golden flagstaffs,
and water-jars encrusted with gems and gold shone in every dwelling.

fragrant with the filaments of lotuses, adorned with water-fountains,
thronged with swans and kāraṇḍava ducks, beautified by flocks of peacocks,
having reservoirs formed by water-fountains, and an abundance of groves and household stepwells.
Here and there peacocks danced; here and there cuckoos called;
the rows of trees had clusters rich with flowers licked by swarms of bees.
Crowded with hosts of men and women, inhabited by the castes and stages of life,
women standing within the palaces shone as they gazed out,
and it gleamed like archways formed by rows of garlands of moons.

6.1.m: Thus, O Vyāsa, the delightful city was settled by [Śiva's] own yogic power,

there was divine Bhogavatī, the supreme abode of Varuṇa,
crowded with fierce nāga maidens and wives of serpents;
Saṃyamanī, the excellent city ruled by the King of Dharma,
filled with people of good conduct who were skilled in what is to be done and what is not to be done;
the charming city of the gods protected by Vāsava,
crowded with hosts of virtuous women, adorned with the loud songs of kinnaras.
In former times, there were many such lovely cities,
vastly extensive in measure and exceedingly radiant.
Here and there doors were made of plantain trees, with auspicious jars containing barley-sprouts;
in places the gandharvas sang, and in places dancers danced;
here and there young twice-born boys recited, studying the Veda;
in places patrons performed sacrifices together with the officiating priests;
in some places they bathed in the concluding ablution, and in some places they gave gifts;
here and there took place the sacred-thread ceremony and the taking of the wedding fire;
in places the consecration of groves, in places the fixing of pilgrimages,
as well as [the dedication] of stepwells, wells, and pools in accordance with rule.
In some places narrators recited narrative discourses;
in some places poets composed verses in that excellent city;
here and there wrestlers wrestled, and in places actors were intent on drama;
the lakes shone with flights of gem-encrusted steps.
Fickle and lively young maidens, sixteen years of age,
were intent on carrying water there, prominent with jars of gems and gold.

6.1.m: By whom was it made? Who is its deity? Or what is recorded as its fruit?" // 2
Sanatkumāra said:

6.1.d: शृणु पुण्यतमे क्षेत्रे सुन्दराख्यं यदा ऽभवत् ..
6.1.m: "Listen to when that which is named Sundara came to be in the most meritorious sacred field,
Allaying all sins, bestowing the fruit of desired objectives, // 3
The mere hearing of which dispels the sin of slaying a brahmin,
[Granting] the merit of the Aśvamedha and others, exceeding a hundred Vājapeyas. // 4

6.1.s: purā kalpakṣaye vyāsa naṣṭakalpā ca medinī ..
6.1.d: पुरा कल्पक्षये व्यास नष्टकल्पा च मेदिनी ..
6.1.m: Formerly, O Vyāsa, at the end of an eon, when the earth was almost destroyed,
Mount Meru was pulverized by fierce winds and rains. // 5
Then, O Vyāsa, the excellent peak of Vaikuṇṭha fell here,
In the awesome, secret, imperishable, and firm Mahākālavana. // 6
The moment that peak fell, a pool certainly came into being,
Having jewel steps and clear water, filled with sands of pearls, // 7
With gold hand-railings, adorned with golden lotuses,
Shaded by wish-granting trees, elevated with wish-fulfilling gems, // 8
Crowded with swans and kāraṇḍava ducks, beautified by cakravāka birds,
Teeming with collections of seeds and medicinal herbs, endowed with all cosmic principles. // 9

6.1.s: kalpakṣaye na kṣīyaṃte yāni tattvāni sarvaśaḥ ..
6.1.d: कल्पक्षये न क्षीयंते यानि तत्त्वानि सर्वशः ..
6.1.m: Those cosmic principles that are not destroyed in every way at the end of an eon

6.1.s: tāni tatra pratiṣṭhaṃti mūrtimaṃti parāṇi ca .. 5.1.53.10 ..
6.1.d: तानि तत्र प्रतिष्ठंति मूर्तिमंति पराणि च .. 5.1.53.10 ..
6.1.m: Abide there, supreme and embodied: // 5.1.53.10
The Vedas, treatises, and Purāṇas, verses, songs, the perishable and imperishable syllables,
The syllable Oṃ, the exclamation vaṣaṭ, the supreme three-footed Gāyatrī, // 11
Kalās, kāṣṭhās, muhūrtas, lavas, truṭis, palas, and ghaṭīs,
Day and night, watches, fortnights, months, and seasons, // 12
And years and yugas dwell in embodied form in that pool.
Gods, yakṣas, nāgas, guhyakas, and kinnaras, // 13
Gandharvas, apsarases, yakṣas, siddhas, and kimpuruṣas,
Afflicted by the fear of the blemish of the eon's end, worshipped it. // 14
Brahmā, Rudra, Kāla, and the guardians of the world of great splendor,
as well as some Siddhas intent on meditation and ascetics of celebrated vows, 15
stay for many yugas, O Vyāsa, until the kalpa comes to an end.
It has the lovely shape of the Sudarśana discus and is filled with waters of nectar; 16
it is endowed with divine trees possessing the qualities of the pārijāta;
it emits diffusing fragrance, scented with the water perfumed by celestial women bathing. 17
In some places peacocks dance; in some places cuckoos sing;
in some places there are cries of peacocks; somewhere it resounds with the rumbling of clouds. 18
It is beautiful (sundara), of beautiful form, and therefore it is called Sundara.
It confers great merit, O Vyāsa, and supreme destruction of all sins, 19

6.1.s: yatra saṃnihito viṣṇuḥ śivaḥ śaktyā yuto vaśī ..
6.1.d: यत्र संनिहितो विष्णुः शिवः शक्त्या युतो वशी ..
6.1.m: where Viṣṇu is present, and Śiva, self-controlled, accompanied by his Śakti.
They worshipped it constantly, at all times, forever. 20

6.1.s: pakṣārdhaṃ pakṣamekaṃ ca sundarakuṇḍe naro vaset ..
6.1.d: पक्षार्धं पक्षमेकं च सुन्दरकुण्डे नरो वसेत् ..
6.1.m: If a man should dwell at Sundarakuṇḍa for half a fortnight or for a fortnight,
his residence in Vaikuṇṭha is assured for a hundred kalpas. 21
Birds, insects, and moths that die there go to the abode of Śiva;

6.1.s: kiṃ punarmānavā loke snānapūtāśca tatra vai .. 22 ..
6.1.d: किं पुनर्मानवा लोके स्नानपूताश्च तत्र वै .. 22 ..
6.1.m: how much more so human beings in the world who are purified by ritual ablution there! 22
Those who give sesame seeds, a cow, elephants, horses, chariots, lands,
female and male servants, gold, and various kinds of jewels, 23
the gift of beds, aerial chariots, and various gifts—

6.1.s: na teṣāṃ dānajaṃ vedmi kīdṛgvyāsa phalaṃ bhavet.. 24 ..
6.1.d: न तेषां दानजं वेद्मि कीदृग्व्यास फलं भवेत्.. 24 ..
6.1.m: I do not know, O Vyāsa, what kind of fruit born of gifts theirs would be! 24

6.1.s: bhūyaḥ śṛṇu paraṃ vyāsa sundarakuṇḍaphalaṃ smṛtam..
6.1.d: भूयः शृणु परं व्यास सुन्दरकुण्डफलं स्मृतम्..
6.1.m: Hear further, O Vyāsa, the supreme fruit recorded of Sundarakuṇḍa:
Once, fallen into sinful wombs on account of abundant sin, 25
a piśāca attained liberation and departed bearing the form of Śiva.
Having bathed at Piśācamocana and having seen the god Maheśvara, 26
one is freed from all sins, even if one is the slayer of a brahmin. 27
Vyāsa said:

6.1.s: ko'sau piśāca iti khyātaḥ kiṃ tena duṣkṛtaṃ kṛtam ..
6.1.d: कोऽसौ पिशाच इति ख्यातः किं तेन दुष्कृतं कृतम् ..
6.1.m: "Who is this who was known as a piśāca? What evil deed was done by him,
by which connection with sin he attained the state of a piśāca? 28

6.1.s: kathaṃ tīrthaprasaṃgo'sya jāto vai dvija sattama ..
6.1.d: कथं तीर्थप्रसंगोऽस्य जातो वै द्विज सत्तम ..
6.1.m: How did his connection with this sacred ford come to be, O best of the twice-born?
I wish to know this from you, O foremost among the knowers of Brahman!" 29
Sanatkumāra said:
"Hear, O Vyāsa, the great narrative, the supreme māhātmya of the sacred ford,
by the mere hearing of which destruction of all sins occurs. 30
There was a brahmin named Devala, a Southerner, the lowest of the twice-born,

6.1.s: sadā pāparato lobhī kūṭasākṣī ca laṃpaṭaḥ .. 31 ..
6.1.d: सदा पापरतो लोभी कूटसाक्षी च लंपटः .. 31 ..
6.1.m: always devoted to sin, greedy, a false witness, and a libertine; 31
a traitor to his guru, a gambler, a rogue, a killer of his guru, a violator of his guru's bed;
a stealer of gold, a drinker of liquor, a killer of brahmins, and treacherous to his master; 32
an eater of forbidden food, devoid of the Veda and the scriptures;
a sinner who had accumulated sins across many births, excluded from all righteousness; 33
a betrayer of trust, arrogant, delighting in the company of thieves, wicked.
That fool went to another country to accomplish the work of thievery. 34
Many creatures were killed on the road by that man of sinful conduct.
That wicked man went to Magadha in the company of evildoers. 35
There, a certain brahmin, self-controlled, who had mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas,
maintaining the sacred fire, established in pure goodness, was always devoted to the duties of a brahmin. 36
His wife was staying in her father's house; having taken that renowned woman,
he set off mounted upon a conveyance and was struck down by that sinner. 37
And his wife, of beautiful hips, endowed with beauty and charm,
a devoted wife, highly fortunate, of firm resolve, with a pure smile, 38
afflicted with sorrow when her husband was killed, distressed by separation from her husband,
having wandered into the terrible forest, the noble woman collected pieces of wood, 39
and mounted the blazing funeral pyre, with a glad heart, along with her husband.

6.1.s: sa ca duṣṭataraḥ sarvaṃ tasya viprasya jīvanam .. 5.1.53.40 ..
6.1.d: स च दुष्टतरः सर्वं तस्य विप्रस्य जीवनम् .. 5.1.53.40 ..
6.1.m: And that most wicked man, having seized all the livelihood of that brahmin, 40
set off on the road, but was seized by the king's servants.

6.1.s: baṃdhayitvā ca taiḥ sarvaistena vittena vai saha ..
6.1.d: बंधयित्वा च तैः सर्वैस्तेन वित्तेन वै सह ..
6.1.m: Having bound him along with all that wealth,
he was brought by all of them to the royal palace and presented before the king. 41

6.1.s: pātito vai gale baddhvā rajjunā vṛkṣakoṭare ..
6.1.d: पातितो वै गले बद्ध्वा रज्जुना वृक्षकोटरे ..
6.1.m: Tied by the neck with a rope, he was cast into the hollow of a tree,
and dragged here and there on the ground by Caṇḍālas and dog-cookers. 42
Through that fruition of his actions, he went to the Raurava hell;
for sixty thousand years he became a worm in feces. 43
Then, by the executors of Yama's commands, he reached another hell:
the dreadful Asipatravana of iron, with heated arrows.
Struck indeed by the servants with clubs and chains,
having gone into Kumbhīpāka, severely tormented, he cried out in the Vaitaraṇī.
Having thus experienced many kinds of pits, ever new, the sinner
then attained the state of a ghost for seventy-five yugas.
Having a huge body, a loud roar, a huge belly, and a needle-sized mouth,
overpowered by hunger and thirst, he resorted to a desert region.
Then, having obtained an even more distressing form, he resorted to a piśāca's body:
crooked, malevolent in disposition, wicked in conduct, sky-clad,
eating leftover, putrid, and stale food contaminated with feces and urine,
eating scraps in cremation grounds, clad in hide, staring wild-eyed.
In a broken well or reservoir, in a dried-up waterless tree,
in an enclosure or moat, in a deserted house, on a riverbank—
dwelling pleased him always at all junctions.
When many yugas had thus passed, he went to Mahākālavana,
where there is a liṅga of Maheśvara and an excellent, beautiful pool.
Merely by having stayed there, he was struck down by a lion.

6.1.s: ghātayitvā ca taṃ pāpaṃ jalārthī kuṃḍamāviśat ..
6.1.d: घातयित्वा च तं पापं जलार्थी कुंडमाविशत् ..
6.1.m: Having killed that sinner, longing for water, [the lion] entered the pool;
and a bone stuck between its fangs fell from its mouth into the water.
By the power of that merit, all [his] sin was destroyed;
and as soon as he died, that liṅga came into the range of his sight.
Abandoning the piśāca body, he, a radiant light, entered that liṅga.
From that time on, O Vyāsa, it is the supreme sacred ford Paiśācamocana.
Thence the god became famous as Piśācamocaneśa.
Sins roar like elephants maddened with rut
only until one reaches the sacred ford Paiśācamocana on the Śiprā.
Having performed ritual ablution in Piśācamocana, purified and concentrated in mind,
and having worshipped the god Piśācamocana according to the rules,
one becomes completely cleansed of all sin, of this there is no doubt.
At Piśācamocana, O Vyāsa, one should cause the great gifts to be made;
he never returns again from the world of Śiva.
This holy story of Piśācamocana, which removes sin—
whoever reads or hears it obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.

6.1.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvantyakhaṇḍe'va ntīkṣetramāhātmye sundarakuṃḍapiśācamocanatīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma tripañcāśattamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 53 ..
6.1.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवन्त्यखण्डेऽव न्तीक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये सुन्दरकुंडपिशाचमोचनतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम त्रिपञ्चाशत्तमोऽध्यायः .. 53 ..
6.1.m: Thus ends the fifty-third chapter, named 'Description of the Glory of Sundarakuṇḍa and Piśācamocana Tīrtha,' in the Avantīkṣetramāhātmya of the fifth section, Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

6.1.m: Vyāsa said: / But further I wish to hear from you, O best among knowers of Brahman: / When did Nīlagaṅgā come to the Śiprākuṇḍa, O Brahman? (1) / Sanatkumāra said: / Listen, Vyāsa, to the great sacred ford that grants the fruit of all sacred fords. / Having bathed in the Nīlagaṅgā, a man should worship Saṃgameśvara; (2) / faults arising from bad company never arise [for him]. / Once, indeed, in the world of Brahmā, the river Gaṅgā, flowing along three paths, (3) / purifying the three worlds, went clad in dark-blue garments, afflicted with sorrow: / "O Lord, what is this sin that was committed by me in the past, (4) / through the fault of vile conduct, by which I have been brought to this state? / Whatever sin belongs to people in all worlds upon earth, (5) / all that settles in me, belonging to all embodied beings. / Overcome with that burden, I am indeed unable to move on the earth, (6) / with a dark-blue appearance, discolored, and excluded from all dharma. / Whatever deed is done, whether auspicious or inauspicious, (7) / creatures casting [it] into me are purified here, utterly free from stain; / they remain in meritorious worlds that grant worldly enjoyment and liberation. (8) / But to us, O Creator, has arisen great distress, the ultimate impurity. / Indeed, there is no happiness, no peace, no sleep, and no relief; (9) / and today there is no eternal place in the world for me, most sinful! / I am flooded with the faults born of bad company, O Teacher of the Universe! (10) / What shall I do? Where shall I go, that peace may come to me? / What austerity, and what gift for me? What sacred ford and what spiritual practice, (11) / by which I, whose limbs are smeared with sin, may again attain my natural state? / Knowing this, O great yogin, do as is proper!" (12) / Brahmā said: / "Listen, O best of rivers, to the cause of the destruction of sin! / In the lovely Mahākālavana, there is indeed this city, Amarāvatī. (13) / There the purifying river, the excellent Śiprā, exists on earth; / by the mere sight of it, destruction of all sins occurs. (14) / Go there, O highly fortunate one, immediately for self-purification!" / Hearing that which was declared by Brahmā, Gaṅgā, the best of rivers, (15) / having recognized that [instruction], reached the auspicious Mahākālavana, / in the southeast portion of Puṣkara, where the god, the son of the Wind, [abides], (16) / and in the northern part of the Vindhya, to the excellent hermitage of Añjanā. / Purified and celibate, she performed austerity with her son, (17) / [a place frequented] by all chaste wives and celibate husbands, / by many divine women, by frolicking young elephants, (18) / with blooming white water-lilies in lakes, resounding with swarms of intoxicated bees, / to be served by non-hostile creatures, resorted to by hosts of brahmin seers, (19) / gladdening the mind, meritorious, pure, destroying sin. / By the mere entrance there, the best of rivers, clad in dark-blue garments, (20) / instantly became clad in white garments, her inauspicious impurity of sin destroyed, / with an appearance resembling the autumn moon, her sins washed away, rich in milk-like waters. (21) / Right there she made her hermitage, the cause of joy to the mind. / Since then, it has been proclaimed in all the worlds as granting merit, (22) / known as 'Nīlagaṅgā', O Vyāsa, a sacred ford that destroys guilt. / Having bathed in this sacred ford, a man should then worship Hanumān; (23) / perfection will be within his reach, there is no doubt. / When the month of Āśvina arrives, during the dark fortnight, collected in mind, (24) / on the new-moon day, he should perform the Mahālaya śrāddha dedicated to the ancestors; / thereby the entire family, along with himself one hundred and one [generations], is saved. (25) / Those ancestors born in the same gotra who dwell in hell, / they all go to a good destination, and theirs are eternal worlds. (26) / Having bathed, devoted to that, he should offer a handful of water with sesame to the ancestors; / imperishable satisfaction arises [for them], and he is honored in heaven. (27) / Having performed the śrāddha with milk-rice dishes, he should feed seven brahmins; / he attains an imperishable śrāddha, and the fruit of a horse-sacrifice is obtained. (28) / Listen to another even more meritorious sacred ford, O Vyāsa; I shall tell it to you, / known as Dugdhakuṇḍa, renowned in the three worlds, (29)

6.1.m: destroying all sins, meritorious, granting all desired boons. / In ancient times, the milk-yielding goddess [Earth], by Pṛthu, the embodiment of dharma, (30) / was milked [of] all sacrificial oblation which gives life to all; / placed in this pool, it was given, hence it is known as Dugdhasaras. (31) / Having bathed in the pool, having drunk milk, and having given a cow rich in milk, / freed from all afflictions and endowed with wealth and grain, (32) / he flourishes at all times, and when dead, he goes to the city of heaven. / Then, having approached Puṣkara, he should perform ablutions, gifting, and so on; (33) / with his soul purified of all sins, he attains the fruit of Puṣkara. (34) / Thus in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of eighty-one thousand [verses], in the fifth section, the Āvantyakhaṇḍa, in the Avanti-kṣetra-māhātmya, the fifty-fourth chapter, named 'Description of the Glory of Nīlagaṅgā'.
Vyāsa said:

6.1.m: Or by whom was he sent formerly to the lovely Mahākālavana? (1)
Sanatkumāra said:
In ancient times, O Vyāsa, this earth was inundated with the waters of the Revā.
Then, thus by all the gods, the excellent sage Agastya, (2)
the highly fortunate one, was worshipped for the sake of protecting the earth.

who removes the burden [of the earth], holy, the auspicious younger sister of Baladeva, (5)
born from the womb of Yaśodā, crusher of the might of Cāṇūra,
having the radiance of lightning, dwelling in the sky, dark, crusher of the black serpent, (6)
mother of Devasena, the sovereign speech of poets,
the Gāyatrī of foremost twice-borns, the excellent Vyāhṛti of meters, (7)

the wish-yielding cow of cattle, the dark creeper beloved of the sweetest season of spring, (8)

the shore longed for by the great ocean, and the royal splendour of kings,

Childless women obtain sons; a maiden obtains an excellent, heroic husband;
all good fortune is attained, bestowing the boon of all desires.
A brahmin becomes learned; a kṣatriya becomes victorious;
a vaiśya becomes rich with manifold profits; and a śūdra experiences happiness.
Reading or even hearing this sacred story,
which grants the boons of all desires, one obtains the fruit of a thousand cows.

where merely by bathing one is freed from great sins.
When the new-moon day falls on a Saturday, one who, composed,
performs a ancestral rite and offers water with sesame seeds dedicated to the ancestors,
and beholds the divine Śanaiścara as an excellent, immovable liṅga,

6.1.m: Formerly, O sinless one, three rivers—the Revā, Carmaṇvatī, and Kṣātā—
arose on earth from Amarakaṇṭaka, purifying the three worlds: (6)
meritorious, having holy waters, charming, purifying, removing sins,
streams purifying all people through bathing and drinking. (7)
Once, in a charming garden in the excellent sacred field of Māndhātṛ,
they were sporting together, delighted, each striving to surpass the others. (8)
Through the occurrence of some offense, a division arose among them.
Having abandoned union with the Revā and cleaved the excellent Vindhya mountain, (9)
that best of rivers went evenly to the delightful Mahākālavana,
where the very holy Śiprā [flows], and this city is indeed Amarāvatī. (10)
There is the best of all tīrthas, commemorated by the name Rudrasaras,
constantly bestowing enjoyment and liberation, attended by hosts of siddhas and seers. (11)
Having arrived there long ago, the Kṣātā resorted to confluence with the Śiprā;

6.1.m: Those who listen to the meritorious, purifying narrative that removes sins,
completely freed from all sins, go to the world of Viṣṇu.

6.1.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pañcama āvaṃtyakhaṇḍe'vantīkṣetramāhātmye gomatītīrthakuṇḍamāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma dviṣaṣṭitamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 62 ..
6.1.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां पञ्चम आवंत्यखण्डेऽवन्तीक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये गोमतीतीर्थकुण्डमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम द्विषष्टितमोऽध्यायः .. 62 ..
6.1.m: Thus ends the sixty-second chapter, titled “Description of the Māhātmya of the Gomatītīrthakuṇḍa,” in the Avantīkṣetramāhātmya of the fifth Avantyakhaṇḍa in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].

having sun-like fangs, the destroyer of Laṅkā, the maker of cries of lamentation, bestower of boons,
the bridge of worldly existence, the great bridge, the builder of the bridge, lord of Ramā,
beloved of Jānakī, full of desire, diademed, adorned with earrings, moving in the sky,
having large lotus eyes, mighty-armed, shaped like a cloud,
moving, flickering, loving, contrary, affectionate to the left-limbed one [Sītā],
dear to women, devoted to women, fond of women, making woman reside on his left side,
the conqueror of enemies, conqueror of desire, conqueror of anger, conqueror of senses,
tranquil, self-controlled, taking pleasure in mercy, steadfastly observing the vow of a single wife,
endowed with sattva, grounded in goodness, the slayer of pride, slayer of wrath, fierce,
surrounded by many rākṣasas, the destroyer of all rākṣasas,
the enemy of Rāvaṇa, the cutter-off of the ten heads [of him who was] vile in battle,
the ruler of the kingdom, the performer of sacrifices, the giver, the enjoyer, rich in austerity,
the sovereign of Ayodhyā, the beloved, Vaikuṇṭha, having an unimpeded form,
observing the vow of truth, steadfast in vows, heroic, practicing austerity, bestower of true fruits,
the witness of all, all-pervading, the taker of all vital breaths, imperishable,
prāṇa, and also apāna, vyāna, udāna, and samāna as well,

6.1.m:
granting all perfections, fulfilling desires, meritorious, embodying Hari and Hara.
Whoever recites [it], rising early in the morning, having become pure and concentrated,
and whatever man constantly listens to this with an unwavering mind
at the three junctions of the day, endowed with faith, is freed from all sins.
He rejoices with sons and grandsons, honored by his wife and servants;
he attains abundant fortune and is freed from all distress;
he attains all desires and obtains immense fame.
A brahmin becomes learned, a kṣatriya becomes victorious,
a vaiśya rich in gaining wealth, and a śūdra attains happiness.
In fierce battle, in dispute, in trade, in servitude to others,
victorious, he wins victory at all times in all undertakings.
Whether once, ten times, a hundred times, or a thousand times,
the man who constantly recites [it] indeed enjoys the fruit in that very manner.
One seeking a son attains sons; one seeking wealth, imperishable wealth;
one seeking liberation attains liberation; one seeking righteousness, an accumulation of righteousness.

6.1.m:
One seeking a maiden attains a maiden difficult to obtain even by the gods;
one seeking knowledge becomes wise; a yogin is united in yoga.
During fierce great portents, famine, conflict with a king,
when a great plague arises, in poverty, when afflicted by misery,
in a forest or wasteland surrounded by a forest fire,
even in a forest beset by lions and tigers, teeming with elephants,
when commanded by an angry king, in an encounter with bandits,
and during terrible lightning strikes, it should indeed always be remembered by men.
In severe planetary afflictions, even when subjected to execution and bondage,
in the great ocean, in a great river, there are no misfortunes for those aboard a ship.
Afflicted by disease, discolored, with hair, nails, and skin lost—
by reciting or even by hearing [it], they acquire divine bodies.
In a grove of tulasī plants, on a lake-island, in a temple of the gods,
at Badrikāśrama, in an auspicious land, at Gaṅgādvāra, in a forest of austerity,
in Madhuvana, at Prayāga, and at Dvārakā, concentrated,
in the accomplished Mahākālavana, restrained, having all their desires fulfilled—

6.1.m:
those who, endowed with devotion and with conquered senses, recite it a hundred times,
become accomplished beings, granting perfections, and wander the surface of the earth.
It is the best means of bringing about friendship among those divided against one another,
an enchantress of enchanters, pure, and destroying sins.
For the destruction of seizing spirits affecting children, it is the best pacification;
and it is the supreme destroyer of the intellect of wicked and sinful people.
A woman whose embryo falls, a barren woman, one whose womb discharges, or one bearing only a single child
constantly gives birth to a son without any difficulty.
Cows give abundant milk, agriculture yields plentiful grain,
servants are devoted to their duty toward their master, and a woman becomes devoted to her husband.
For the destruction of untimely death, and likewise upon seeing a bad dream,
and in every pacification rite, it should always be remembered by men.
Whatever mortal recites [it] daily, being pure, in the presence of Viṣṇu,
alone, with diet restrained, anger conquered, and senses subdued,
mounted upon Garuḍa, clad in yellow garments, four-armed,
having attained his desire in this world, he goes to Viṣṇu's realm. // 28–29

6.1.m:
On the one side are all branches of knowledge; on the one side is all austerity;
on the one side is all righteousness, and likewise on the one side is the name of Viṣṇu. // 30
Whatever twice-born wishes indeed to praise [him] with the thousand names,
he has praised [him] indeed with this single verse; there is no doubt: // 31
“O thousand-eyed one, thousand-footed one, radiant with a thousand faces,
thousand-named one, infinite-eyed one, thousand-armed one, homage be to you!” // 32
Viṣṇu's thousand names indeed, ancient and commended by the Vedas,
should always be recited by devotees, the most auspicious of all auspicious things. // 33
To the gods thus engaged in praise there, O twice-born,
the blessed Lord, the giver of boons worshipped by boon-givers, spoke visibly: // 34
The blessed Lord said:
“O gods, let the boon desired from me be chosen by all;
I shall grant all of it; no hesitation is to be made in this matter.” // 35
The gods said:
“Since you are a granter of boons, O Viṣṇu, give us this boon:
born from Aditi’s womb, become Śakra’s younger brother as well.” // 36

6.1.m:
Having been thus entreated by the gods headed by Brahmā and Śakra,
and saying “So be it,” the blessed Lord vanished right there. // 37
Then, after some time, the blessed Lord, the son of Aditi,
bearing the form of Viṣṇu, the infinite one, became Vāmana due to dwarfhood. // 38
Bali, the son of Virocana, O Vyāsa, with a hundred horse-sacrifices,
sacrificed, O best of the twice-born, desiring to seize the sovereignty of Indra. // 39
Having made Kaśyapa the officiating priest and the best of the Bhṛgus the hotṛ priest,
Brahmā himself, the Grandfather, became [the superintending priest] there. // 40
The blessed Lord Atri, best of sages, became the adhvaryu priest;
Nārada was the udgātṛ priest, and Vasiṣṭha was a member of the assembly. // 41
Whatever lord of sages was prescribed in whatever role, all were there;
Bali, the best of kings, O Vyāsa, became consecrated for sacrifice there. // 42
While the sacrifices were thus proceeding, O best of sages,
“Let it be offered into the fire!”, “Let it be eaten!”, “Let it be given!”, and likewise “Let it be placed!”—
such auspicious words were heard there, O best of the twice-born.
At that time, during the marvelous [rites], Vāmana, having a bright smile, arrived. // 43–44

6.1.m:
Reciting from his mouth the mantras of the four Vedas,
Vāmana, the best of the twice-born, stood at the door, O king of kings. // 45
Everything was reported to the king by the doorkeeper, O Vyāsa.
Then, having arisen, the great king Bali, son of Virocana,
taking all the arghya offering, went out with the members of his assembly. // 46
Having duly worshipped Vāmana, the creator of the worlds,
having brought him into the midst of the assembly and offered the hospitality of a seat, [he said:]
“Whence is your arrival, O brahmin? What desired thing may I give to you?” // 47–48
Vāmana said:
“O king of kings, all creation belongs to Brahmā Parameṣṭhin;
from there I have come, O mighty one, through a desire to see the sacrifice. // 49
Varuṇa’s sacrifice was indeed seen by me previously, O sinless one;
and the sacrifice of the lord of yakṣas was certainly seen by me. // 50
The sacrifice of Dharma too, and of Prajāpati, was [seen] by me, O best one;
the sacrifice of Vāyu, O great king, was seen by me, performed according to rule. // 51
And whatever sacrifices of the royal sages were seen, those too, O you of great vows—

the kind of sacrifice, O great king, that I have seen here of yours,

Bali said:
“Ask, O best of the twice-born! What desired thing shall I grant to you?” // 54
Vāmana said:
“Give me, O king of kings, three paces of the earth
for a dwelling place, if it pleases you today, O best of rulers.” // 55
Bali said:
"What is this that you have asked for, O brahmin? It is very little; it is indeed not much for you.
Elephants, horses, chariots, the earth, and jewels of various kinds,
Male and female slaves, slender-waisted women, and diverse wealth,
Articles of property, two radiant garments—ask for [these], O best of the twice-born!
You are a worthy recipient, accomplished in your aims, one who has mastered the Vedas and their auxiliary branches."
Vāmana said:
"I have no desire whatsoever for anything on earth, O king, O bestower of honor.
Give three paces of land if you have the faith now."

6.1.m:
"Take three paces of land for your dwelling, O bestower of honor!"
Having spoken thus, that royal sage gave the land to the twice-born,
Even though restrained at that time, O Vyāsa, by Bhṛgu, being impelled by fate.
The moment the water was given, Hari immediately strode across the cosmic egg.
With its mountains, forests, and woods, this earth
Became [covered in] two and a half paces then, O Vyāsa; and his wealth was surrendered by Bali.
Having conquered all the host of asuras and given the kingdom to Śatakratu,
Afterwards Viṣṇu, bearing the form of Vāmana, reached Kumudvatī.
In the sacred hermitage of Ṛddhisiddhi, having created a sacred ford sprung from himself,
That best of gods made his dwelling right there, O Vyāsa.
The sacred ford created by Vāmana is called Vāmanakuṇḍa.
In the month of Bhādrapada, in the bright fortnight, the twelfth day conjoined with the Śravaṇā [nakṣatra]
Is proclaimed as Vāmana-dvādaśī, which destroys ten million murders.
When a man, having bathed in this sacred ford and fasted on the eleventh day,
Keeps a night-vigil, he becomes fit for becoming one with Brahman.

6.1.m:
Those who make the great gifts, especially on the twelfth day,
Nothing is hard to obtain for them in the three worlds.
Thus indeed the Vāmana sacred ford was proclaimed in ancient times by the great sage.
It removes all sins, is holy, and grants the boon of all desires;
Everything is indeed obtained through it; no doubt should be entertained here.
Thus ends the sixty-third chapter, entitled 'The Narration of the Greatness of Vāmanakuṇḍa and the Thousand Names of Viṣṇu', in the Avantīkṣetramāhātmya of the fifth Avantyakhaṇḍa in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].

6.1.m:
Sanatkumāra said:
There is an unsurpassed sacred ford there known as Kaṃthaḍeśvara.
A person, having bathed in that sacred ford and beheld the god Maheśvara, // 1
is freed from all sins, becoming pure and restrained in mind.
Accompanied by a hundred aerial chariots, he is glorified in the world of Śiva. // 2
It is the most meritorious sacred ford on earth, the supreme remover of all sins,
where the confluence of the Khagartā is, near Gaṅgeśvara, // 3
meritorious, destroying great sins, and granting the fruit of great merit;
where the Gaṅgā, purifier of the three worlds, falling from the sky, // 4
was instantly caught on his head by Mahādeva Śambhu.
Having bathed in that sacred ford, a person should gaze upon Gaṅgeśa; // 5
obtaining the fruit of bathing in the Gaṅgā, he is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu.
Reaching Vīreśvara, a person should dwell in that sacred ford; // 6
his soul purified of all sins, he would attain the world of heroes.
Another highly meritorious sacred ford is celebrated on earth by great seers, // 7
renowned as Vāmanakuṇḍa, famous throughout the three worlds,
by the mere darśana of which one wards off the sin of killing a brahmin; // 8
attaining a hundred desires, he would later go to the city of Viṣṇu.
Vyāsa said:
At what time in the past did that [sacred ford] called Vāmana arise, O sinless one? // 9
I wish to hear all that from you, O best among knowers of Brahman.
Sanatkumāra said:
Listen, O best of the twice-born, to the supreme, sin-removing tale, // 10
by the mere hearing of which one is freed from all sins.
Formerly, a lord of the Daityas is recounted, devoted to devotion to Viṣṇu, // 11
renowned as Prahrāda, the best of all upholders of dharma.
Dharma was won [by him] through conduct; Lakṣmī was won through truthfulness; // 12
the worlds were upheld through steadfastness; the earth was sustained through patience;
the celestial oceans [were won] through depth; the hosts of enemies through valor; // 13
and guests were won by that great-souled one through modesty;
sacrifice was won through sacrificial fees; the fire through oblations; // 14

6.1.m:
his soul was purified through purity and conduct, and evil was destroyed through austerity;
brahmins were won through gifts, honor, food, clothing, and the like; // 15
birth was conquered through ritual purification; the eternal Self [was won] through self-restraint;
the breath was conquered through breath-control; Hari was won through yogic meditation. // 16
Such was the great yogin, devoted to truth and dharma;
equal to Prahlāda, there never was nor will there ever be a steadfast man. // 17
His grandson of noble conduct was called Bali.
As he ruled righteously, the subjects flourished abundantly. // 18
There was no one short-lived, dull-witted, foolish, diseased, or envious;
no one was childless or devoid of wealth on the surface of the earth. // 19
A great king, a protector of the earth, a sacrificer of abundant fees,
by him was the earth with its seven continents always protected. // 20
Once, as he sat in the center of the assembly on an excellent throne,
while shouts of victory were rising, the Gandharvas sang delightfully; // 21
as instruments were being played, troupes of apsarases danced;
as an auspicious tale was being told by wise men, // 22
bards, panegyrists, siddhas, and learned cāraṇas,
and seers arrived right there, O best of the twice-born. // 23
Sunda, Upasunda, Tuhuṇḍa, and others, fierce like Mahiṣāsura,
Śumbha, Niśumbha, Dhūmrākṣa, and the Kālakeya Dānavas, // 24
and valiant Kālanemi, Daurhṛda, Mūṣaka, Yama,
Nikumbha, Kumbhaviśaṭha, and mighty Andhaka, // 25
Śaṅkha, the dreadful Jalandhara, and Vātāpi of great strength,
Sarvajit, Viśvahantā, Kāmacārin, Halāyudha— // 26
these and many other promoters of Danu's race
attended there upon the flawless King Bali. // 27
Siddhas, nāgas, yakṣas, kinnaras, and kiṃpuruṣas,
sky-roamers, earth-dwellers, boys, and cruel rākṣasas, // 28
these and many others attended upon the king.
There that most divine assembly shone resplendent, O best of the twice-born. // 29

6.1.m: ... like the autumn sky strewn with bright planets. / In the same way, the king Bali sat in his assembly hall and shone, / like Indra in heaven surrounded by the Maruts and the gods. / And one day, Nārada, who appears like a god, / arrived in the middle of the assembly, while all those Dānavas were present. / Seeing that he had arrived, all the sons of Diti rose up. / They all paid homage to the best of Kinnaras, led by Bali. / Having honoured him and offered a seat, the king inquired of his welfare. / Having received hospitality and sat down, the virtuous Nārada spoke; / the best of seers spoke to Bali with a voice deep as a thundercloud: / Nārada said: / Listen, best of the Diti-born, I went to the bull-bannered [god]'s abode. / There the delightful divine assembly was gathered with divine intent. / There the gods, with the Gandharvas and headed by Indra, / were seated, telling holy stories to one another. / There they could not bear the glorious tale of the Daityas told by me: / 'In ancient times the Daitya Hiraṇyakaśipu was a lord of creatures, / a conqueror of the three worlds, a leader by whom this earth was conquered. / Having brought the entire world under control, he enjoyed the earth; / endowed with immense splendour, possessing great strength and prowess, / self-controlled, going everywhere, acting as he pleased, he was struck down by the Man-Lion. / How much strength does Bali possess in the world, that you praise him, O Nārada?' / Thus reproaching me, Indra, the world-gatherer, / raised various sharp disputes, O best of Dānavas. / Therefore, O best of Dānavas, conquer the earth that descended from your ancestors, / and attain universal sovereignty, O lord of the earth! / How much strength do the gods truly possess, O best of Danujas? / They are bent on flight, subdued, and always cowards in battle! / Relying upon my word, become the sovereign of the three worlds! / Hearing Nārada's word, Bali, son of Virocana, then

6.1.m: felt matchless anger to conquer the three worlds, O twice-born. / Having consulted with all the Asuras, the lord of all the Daitya folk / waged fierce battle with the mighty Indra. / And having defeated all the gods, he subjugated them along with Indra. / The Asura Bali, son of Virocana, became the ruler of all the worlds. / The gods, deprived of their authority, cast down from their kingdom, defeated, / wander the earth just like mortals on that account. / After some time had passed, the gods took refuge with Brahmā: / 'O Brahmā, scorcher of foes, we have been cast out of heaven by Bali! / What shall we do? Where shall we go? What means shall we adopt?' / Brahmā said: / Listen, O best of deities, to your supreme means! / Go, O best of immortals, to the delightful city of Padmāvatī! / There is an excellent and sacred ford named Uttaramānasa, / where the famous bestower of the eight perfections grants great perfections to men; / and the nine treasures also reside there, O best [of beings]. / In the southern part of that very [place] is the supreme Viṣṇutīrtha. / Having bathed there, a man should behold Siddheśvarī, who bestows true success; / dedicated to prosperity and success, he is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu. / On the tenth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Āśvina, / one should worship Gaṇeśvara in the region of the Śamī tree with the eight perfections. / He becomes victorious in all the worlds; there is no doubt about this. / A man should constantly worship Gaṇeśa, stationed at the foot of the Śamī tree, / bestower of the boons of prosperity and success, granter of all desires. / Obtaining the boon of all desires, he will be blessed with sons and wealth. / Therefore, with all effort, one should go to the Mahākāla forest; / go without delay to where the Viṣṇusaras sacred ford is situated. / O best of deities, perform the worship / of Viṣṇu of matchless splendour; he will be your protector from all fears, O best of immortals! / Having heard this speech of the celebrated Brahmā,

6.1.m: those gods, intent on fulfilling their purpose, reached the Mahākāla forest. / Having come here and purified themselves with rites such as bathing and gift-giving, / the perfected beings, devoted to Viṣṇu's bhakti, engaged in worship. / Then all those gods, headed by Śakra, / respectfully inquired of Brahmā about the rite of worshipping the god. / The gods said: / O Brahmā, in what manner does supreme bhakti to Viṣṇu arise? / We wish to hear all that from you, O best among the knowers of Brahman! / Brahmā said: / Listen, O best of deities, to the supreme devotion to Viṣṇu! / One should meditate on the four-armed god wearing white garments, with the colour of the moon, / with a serene face, for the pacification of all obstacles. / Gain belongs to them, victory belongs to them; whence could there be defeat for them / in whose heart resides Janārdana, dark as a blue lotus? / For the achievement of desired goals, he is worshipped even by the gods. / Homage to that lord of the hosts, the remover of all obstacles! / At the beginning of the kalpa, desiring to create, I was impelled by Viṣṇu; / yet, although absorbed in meditating on Viṣṇu, I was not able to produce beings. / Meanwhile, the great sage Mārkaṇḍeya, / lord of all perfections, self-controlled, long-lived, having conquered his senses, / was suddenly seen by me; then going forward, I approached him. / Then, both of us with beaming eyes, having honoured one another / and inquired after each other's supreme well-being, while seated comfortably, O best of immortals— / then that great sage Mārkaṇḍeya was asked by me: / 'Blessed one, in what manner will my offspring be free from affliction? / I wish to hear all that, O venerable one, praised by sages!' / The venerable Mārkaṇḍeya said: / Supreme devotion to Viṣṇu is eternal, the destroyer of all distress and sorrow, / the remover of all sins, auspicious, the granter of all happiness. / This supreme lore of Brahman must not be given to just anyone: / to an ungrateful person, to a non-disciple, to an atheist, or to a deceiver.

Om. Of this mantra of the hymn of the thousand names of glorious Viṣṇu, Mārkaṇḍeya is the seer, Viṣṇu is the deity, anuṣṭubh is the metre, and the application in recitation is for the attainment of all desires.
Now the meditation verse:
I bow to the child cowherd, dark as a water-bearing cloud, who displays a noble character, who held up a mountain in the palm of his hand, delightful with flute-music, / the protector of the people and families of Vraja, fond of sporting with lovely women, adorned with a garland of fresh tulasī. // 75
Om. The Universe, Viṣṇu, Hṛṣīkeśa, the Soul of All, the Producer of All, / Omnipresent, Lord of the Night, the Resting Place of the Abodes of All Beings; // 76
The Beginningless and Endless, the God, All-Knowing, Source of All, / All-Pervading, Upholder of the World, Bearer of All Powers, Sinless; // 77
Sanatkumāra said:
"Now, after this, I shall declare Vīreśvara; listen!
Having bathed in that sacred ford, a man will attain the world of heroes.
An eminent sacred ford of the serpents, bestowing the boon of all desires,
That sacred ford named Kālabhairava is remembered as supreme,
By the mere darśana of which one passes beyond all sorrow."
Vyāsa said:
"At what time was the sacred ford named Kālabhairava renowned,
O best of the foremost sages? Tell this in full detail."
Sanatkumāra said:
"In ancient times this Bhairava was a yogin who frightened the yoginīs.
Then, the hosts of yoginīs were the malicious spirits created by the wheel of Time.
Among them, the supremely excellent yoginī renowned as Kālī
Constantly protected this stainless Bhairava like a son.
By him were dispelled these faults and portents, O best of men,
Which were renowned on earth as threefold, the supreme creators of all obstacles.
Then the malicious spirits of Time were destroyed by that Supreme Self:

and also the greatness of that best of sacred fords, O best of the virtuous. // 1
Yet I wish to hear further from you, O best among the knowers of Brahman;
at what time was it told? Tell this in detail. // 2
Sanatkumāra said:
Listen, O brahmin; I will tell in your presence the supreme,

6.1.m: most holy narrative originating at the Nāgatīrtha, which removes sins on earth, // 3
by merely hearing which a man becomes freed from curses.
Formerly, O scorcher of foes, the Nāgas fell from their position due to their mother's curse. // 4
They were being burned by Janamejaya, and were delivered indeed by Āstīka.
They then asked the son of Jaratkāru, O best of the twice-born. // 5
The Nāgas said:
O brahmin, by your grace we have been delivered from the fire
at this sacrifice of Janamejaya, in the presence of the king of gods. // 6
Seeking our welfare, O scorcher of foes, [tell us] for the sake of an abode,
in which place, O brahmin, our residence may always be free from fear. // 7

Sanatkumāra said:

6.1.m: "Hear, dear child! Upon the face of the earth is the most celestial river, the Śiprā;
on its bank is an excellent sacred ford known as Karkarāja, / 2
by whose mere sight the destruction of great sins comes about.

the three seasons [of that course] are declared to be smoky-rayed. / 4
Those who die there return [to rebirth], even yogins, O scorcher of foes!

6.1.s: cāturmāsye harau supte ye narā vratavarjitāḥ ..5..

Mārkaṇḍeya said:

this universe of moving and unmoving things, the whole world, O Lord of the world! / 8

that I wish to hear from you, O best of the knowers of Brahman!" / 9

For Hari dwells residing in the body of one who has performed ritual ablution,

For the destruction of all sins and for the pleasing of the gods,

6.1.m: One should not bathe at night or at twilight, except during an eclipse;
one should not bathe with hot water, [for] at night purification does not arise.
Purification has been ordained in all rites by the sight of the sun;
during the Cāturmāsya especially, purification through water will come to pass.
If the body lacks strength, however, one is purified by an ash bath,
by a mantra bath, O prince of brahmins, or by water from Viṣṇu's feet.

6.1.m:
Sanatkumāra said:
To the south of Meru and north of Dugdhakuṇḍa,
there is Ṛṣabha, an excellent mountain frequented by gods and gandharvas, / 1
where lovely celestial maidens continually disport, O brahmin.
There exists [a lake] named Ramyasaras, which grants all desires. / 2
Having bathed in that sacred ford, a person surely becomes fortunate;
he plays constantly with the gods, becoming exceedingly renowned on earth. / 3
The eighth day of the bright half of Bhādrapada, conjoined with the Anurādhā asterism—
having arrived here on that day, performing rites such as ritual ablution and giving gifts, / 4
whoever does so constantly, O Vyāsa, their realms are eternal.
To the north-east of Meru is a divine, exceedingly splendid sacred ford / 5
renowned as Bindusaras, granting the boon of all desires.
The holy Gaṅgā, Sarasvatī, Śarayū, and Payasvinī— / 6
these excellent rivers have gone there, O son of Satyavatī.
Whatever siddhas, sādhyas, and ascetics observing vows / 7
constantly paid homage to that sacred ford;
having bathed in that sacred ford, a person surely attains all goals. / 8
And the fourth day in the bright half of Bhādrapada that is proclaimed,
it is declared to be always perfected, where the lord of the gaṇas was born. / 9
Renowned as Manaḥkāmeśvara, granting the boon of all desires,
having bathed in his sacred ford and seen the divine Ganeśvara,
a person attains a hundred desires and becomes one who moves at will. / 10
Vyāsa said:
In this auspicious field, O brahmin, the excellent Mahākāla forest, / 11
how many sacred fords and temples of deities are there?
Whichever are renowned, tell us those in detail. / 12
Sanatkumāra said:
Listen, O Vyāsa, best of seers, to the supreme story that removes sin.
Whatever sacred fords and liṅgas are in Avantī, O great sage, / 13
not even the self-manifest four-faced [Brahmā] would be able to describe them
fully in sixty thousand years. / 14

6.1.m:
Just as drops flow from clouds in rain,
and the count of grasses on the earth, or sands on the ground— / 15
no one is able to state the count of lights in the sky;
likewise, O rich in austerity, there is no counting the tīrthas and liṅgas in Avantī. / 16
Both in the intermediate space and on earth, this entire city has become a tīrtha,
with step-wells, wells, tanks and such, springs and fountains, / 17
rivers, lakes, and ponds—it is indeed a tīrtha throughout.
Nonetheless, hear from me in connection with the pilgrimage of the gods; / 18
I shall tell you whichever are the foremost,
knowing which you will forever be freed from previously committed auspicious and inauspicious [deeds]. / 19
Having risen in the morning, always pure, composed in mind,
endowed with the remembrance of Viṣṇu, performing all morning duties and rituals, / 20
supplied with all fragrances, sesamum seeds, unbroken rice, and the like,
having bathed in the lake of Rudra, dear one, he should likewise perform the vow. / 21
Particularly in the months of Kārttika and Mārgaśīrṣa, and in Vaiśākha and Āṣāḍha,
and on Śivarātri, the pilgrimage of the gods is praised. / 22
At whichever god's tīrtha, in the presence of whichever god,
there the ritual ablution should be performed, and the worship of the deity. / 23
He who performs it according to the rule obtains all the fruit;
therefore, with every effort, one should perform the pilgrimage of the gods. / 24
Vyāsa said:
O brahmin, in what manner should a man perform the pilgrimage of the gods?
I desire to hear all that in detail, O rich in austerity. / 25
Sanatkumāra said:
Hear, O Vyāsa, the supreme secret; I shall tell it as I heard it—
the dialogue of Umā and Maheśvara regarding the rites of pilgrimage to the gods and the like. / 26
Umā said:
O god, O Maheśvara, let the power of this sacred field be told!
Whatever tīrthas there are, and whatever liṅgas there are—
tell me them from the beginning, O vast lord, O best of speakers! / 27
Īśvara said:

6.1.m:
Hear with care, O goddess, the power that destroys sin. / 28
It is the primeval sacred field, O great goddess, always exceedingly dear to me,
where there is the most holy Śiprā, the divine Navanadī, my beloved, / 29
and the confluence of the Nīlagaṅgā, and likewise the river Gandhavatī;
these four rivers are dear to me in Kumudvatī, O lady of good vows. / 30
There are eighty-four Īśvaras, and there are eight Bhairavas,
eleven Rudras, and twelve Ādityas are remembered. / 31
There are six Vināyakas here, and twenty-four goddesses,
since I have come, O auspicious one, to this best Mahākālavana. / 32
All the gods, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and others, are stationed right here, O auspicious one;
this sacred field, one yojana in extent, is pervaded by the gods, O goddess. / 33
Ten Viṣṇus are proclaimed; hear from me their names:
Vāsudeva, Ananta, Balarāma, Janārdana, / 34
Nārāyaṇa, Hṛṣīkeśa, the boar Dharaṇīdhara,
Viṣṇu in the form of Vāmana, Śeṣaśāyī, and the abode of Śrī. / 35
These ten manifestations of Viṣṇu are declared supreme, removing all sins. / 36
Umā said:
O Lord, I desire to hear in succession about the gods—
the lords of the gods who dwell in the charming Mahākālavana: / 37
the Vināyakas, the Bhairavas, the goddesses, the sons of the wind who are there,
the Rudras, the Ādityas, and others; tell me their names. / 38
Īśvara said:
Ṛddhida, Siddhida, Kāmada the lord of gaṇas,
Vighnahā, Pramodin, and Caturthīvratakapriya— / 39
these six are proclaimed the supreme destroyers of obstacles.
Umā, Caṇḍīśvarī, Gaurī, granting abundance and success to men, / 40
Vaṭayakṣiṇī, Vīrabhadrā: these are the eight Mothers.
Mahāmāyā, famous Satī, and Kapālamātṛkā, / 41
Ambikā, Śītalā, Ekānaṃśā, bestower of perfections, / 42
Brahmāṇī, Pārvatī, Yoginī, endowed with yoga,
Kaumārī, Bhagavatī, and the six Kṛttikās, / 43

the famous Carpaṭamātṛkās, and the Vaṭamātṛkās,
likewise the renowned Sarasvatī, and Mahālakṣmī is remembered; / 44
then sixty-four Yoginī-Mothers are remembered.
Kālikā, Mahākālī, Cāmuṇḍā, Brahmacāriṇī, / 45
Vaiṣṇavī is named, Vārāhī, Vindhyavāsinī,
Ambā, and Ambālikā: these are the supreme twenty-four [goddesses]. / 46
Hanumān, Brahmacārin, and Kumāra, the mighty one—
these four sons of the wind have been declared to you by me. / 47
Daṇḍapāṇi, Vikrānta, Mahābhairava, Sita, Asita,
Baṭuka, Bālaka, Nandin, and another, the fifty-sixth, / 48
the renowned Kālabhairava, and eighth, Kṣetrapāla—
these eight Bhairavas are known as supreme removers of great sins.
Kapardin, Kapālin, Kalānātha, Vṛṣāsana, / 49
Tryambaka, Śūlapāṇi, Cīravāsas, Digambara,
Girīśa, Kāmacārin, Sarva, Sarvāṅgabhūṣaṇa— / 50
these eleven Rudras are declared the destroyers of enemy factions.
Aruṇa, Sūrya, Vedāṅga, Bhānu, Indra, Ravi, Aṃśumān, / 51
Suvarṇaretas, Ahaḥkartṛ, Mitra, the eternal Viṣṇu—
these twelve Ādityas are supreme, removing all diseases. / 52
O daughter of the Himālaya, hear as I tell you the names
of the eighty-four liṅgas headed by Agastyeśvara: / 53
Agastyeśvara is named, Guheśvara after that;
next is proclaimed Ḍhuṇḍheśvara, and Ḍamarukeśvara, O passionate lady; / 54
then Śambhu Anādikalpeśvara, supreme Svarṇajāleśvara;
the divine Triviṣṭapeśvara, the one named Kapāleśvara; / 55
Śambhu Karkoṭakeśvara, Siddhīśvara after that;
Rudra Svargadvāreśvara, and another, Lokapāleśvara; / 56
then renowned Kāmeśvara, and after that Kuṭumbeśvara;
Indradyumneśvara is known, and after that Īśāneśa; / 57

6.1.m: renowned as Bilvakeśvara, stationed at the western gate; / and Dardureśvara is declared to be at the northern gate. / These and many other purifying lords of the three worlds known as liṅgas / have been declared in the delightful Mahākālavana. / Sixty thousand crores and sixty hundred crores: / in the Mahākālavana, O Vyāsa, there is no counting of the liṅgas; / yet they have been proclaimed by me here according to importance. / Whatever sacred ford belongs to whichever deity is proclaimed by that [deity's] name; / having bathed and given that gift, one obtains the fruit of that sacred ford. / Likewise, O sinless one, the meritorious nine planets were proclaimed long ago; / hear their holy names and their sacred fords: / known as Narāditya, and after that Someśvara; / Maṅgaleśvara is declared, and after that Budheśvara; / Bṛhaspatīśvara is taught, and likewise Śiva Śukreśvara; / the great god Sthāvareśvara is proclaimed by the lords of sages; / Rāhu and Ketu are proclaimed, and their sacred fords, O best of men. / Having bathed in those sacred fords, a person is freed from all sins. / The planets bestow kingship, and the planets take away kingship; / by the planets indeed all the three worlds with the moving and unmoving are pervaded. / Having bathed in a planet-ford, a person should perform the worship of the planets; / the affliction of the planets certainly never troubles him. / Thus, O Vyāsa, have the deities and the sacred fords been declared by me; / the pilgrimage is exceedingly meritorious, supreme, holy, and sin-destroying. / In severe afflictions caused by planets, in poverty, and in terrible distress, / the pilgrimage to the gods is proclaimed for their deliverance. / Those best of men who constantly perform the inner circumambulation of the sacred field, / for them nothing is hard to obtain in the three worlds; / the sonless obtains a son, the destitute acquires wealth.

Vyāsa said:
O Lord, the embodiment of divinity, all has been recounted by you:
the māhātmya of the sacred ford of Avantī, pure and equal to the Veda.
Yet I wish to hear further from you, O best of the knowers of Brahman!
In the delightful Mahākālavana in Avantī upon the earth, O most virtuous one,
how many sacred fords exist here, O you of noble vows?

O Lord, I wish to hear about the auspicious Mahākālavana.

Listen, O best of seers! Whatever sacred fords exist

6.1.m: in the auspicious Mahākālavana, I shall declare them, O you of noble vows.
Whatever sacred fords there are on the earth, Puṣkara and the others,
all of them exist in the supreme Mahākālavana.
Countless thousands, crores upon crores, O most virtuous one,
plunge into the lake of Rudra; therefore it is called Koṭitīrtha.
Kinnaras shower a rain of mist-droplets on the mountain,
and in winter they are seen at the tīrtha named Paiśācamocana.

6.1.m: as to how many sacred fords and how many liṅgas there are.
Even so, I will relate them according to their prominence, O most virtuous one.
As many days as there are in a year, O best of the twice-born,
that many famous [tīrthas] are to be reached, O scorcher of foes.
When a year is completed, the pilgrimage to Avantī is accomplished.
He who performs it according to rule becomes Śambhu himself.
Whatever fruit is attained by living in Kāśī for a thousand manvantaras,
that fruit is attained in Avantī in five days in the month of Vaiśākha.
The pilgrimage to Avantī should be performed with diligence by one seeking liberation.
Especially in the month of Mādhava, one should take the bath in Avantī.

6.1.s: yo hi vaiśākhamāsādya avaṃtyāṃ vyāsa mānavaḥ .. 16 ..
6.1.d: यो हि वैशाखमासाद्य अवंत्यां व्यास मानवः .. 16 ..
6.1.m: A person who, having arrived at the month of Vaiśākha in Avantī, O Vyāsa,
having observed the vow for a year, has bathed at each sacred ford according to rule,
and offered all the gifts, obtains the complete fruit entirely.
Having enjoyed vast pleasures, he is glorified in the world of Śiva.
This māhātmya enhances devotion to Śiva, brings fame, and increases spiritual merit.

6.1.m: 14. The greatness of the Rājasthalatīrtha situated in the middle region of the four oceans; there, the declaration of the fruit in the form of obtaining a son through ritual ablution in the four oceans by sage Dālbhya when questioned by King Sudyumna's wife named Sudarśanā; Sudyumna's journey to Gandhamādana to worship Śiva by Dālbhya's word; his journey to Avantī by Śiva's word; the vision of the four oceans in embodied form through the worship of the four oceans; the four oceans' granting of a boon to the king; the establishment of the tīrtha in that very place; description of the greatness of the four oceans. 15 2

6.1.m: 15. Description of the greatness of the Śaṅkaravāpītīrtha; Śiva's installation of his own liṅga under that name after performing worship of the sun; description of the greatness of Śaṅkarāditya. 16 1

16. Description of the power and greatness of the Nīlagandhavatī; description of the attainment of the fruit of great merit by performing the śrāddha and so forth, as well as by ritual ablution, giving, and so forth there. 16 2

6.1.d: 17 सनत्कुमारव्याससंवादप्रसङ्गेन दशाश्वमेधतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णने मन्वादिभिः स्नानेन दशाश्वमेधफलं सम्पादितमित्यादि सदृष्टान्तवर्णनम्.... ....17 1
6.1.m: 17. Description, illustrated with examples, that the fruit of ten horse sacrifices was obtained through ritual ablution by Manu and others, in the description of the greatness of the Daśāśvamedhatīrtha in the context of the dialogue between Sanatkumāra and Vyāsa. 17 1

6.1.d: 18 एकानंशादेव्युत्पत्तिवर्णने तारकासुरराक्षसपीडितेन ब्रह्मणा निशादेव्याः स्मरणम्, तया तारकविनाशार्थं ब्रह्मण उपायकथनम् तत्रैव ब्रह्मणा तस्याः स्थापनम्, एकानंशादेवीतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्. ....... 17 1
6.1.m: 18. In the description of the origin of the goddess Ekānaṃśā: Brahmā, tormented by the rākṣasa Tārakāsura, remembers the goddess of night; her explanation of a means to Brahmā for the destruction of Tāraka; her installation by Brahmā in that very place; description of the greatness of the tīrtha of the goddess Ekānaṃśā. 17 1

6.1.s: 19 śivapārvatyorakṣakrīḍāsamaye tatra sthale caṇḍapracaṇḍadaityayorāgamanam, pārvatyā tayoḥ parābhavakaraṇama, harasiddhiriti śaṅkareṇa pārvatyā nāmakaraṇam, harasiddhitīrthamāhātmyavarṇanam.. ...... .. ....... 18 1
6.1.d: 19 शिवपार्वत्योरक्षक्रीडासमये तत्र स्थले चण्डप्रचण्डदैत्ययोरागमनम्, पार्वत्या तयोः पराभवकरणम, हरसिद्धिरिति शङ्करेण पार्वत्या नामकरणम्, हरसिद्धितीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्.. ...... .. ....... 18 1
6.1.m: 19. The arrival of the two daityas Caṇḍa and Pracaṇḍa at that spot during Śiva and Pārvatī's dice game; Pārvatī's defeat of the two; Śaṃkara's naming of Pārvatī as Harasiddhi; description of the greatness of the Harasiddhitīrtha. 18 1

6.1.s:
20 vaṭayakṣiṇīmāhātmyavarṇanam, piśācakatīrthamāhātmyam, śiprāguṃpheśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanama, agastyeśvaramāhātmyavarṇanam, ḍhuṇḍheśvaramāhātmyavarṇanam, ḍamarukeśvaramāhātmyavarṇanam, anādikalpeśvaramāhātmyavarṇanam, siddheśvaravīrabhadracaṃḍikāmāhā-

kapāleśvaramāhātmyavarṇanam, svargadvāratīrthayātrāmāhātmyavarṇanam..... 18 2

कपालेश्वरमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्, स्वर्गद्वारतीर्थयात्रामाहात्म्यवर्णनम्..... 18 2
6.1.m: 20. Description of the greatness of the Vaṭayakṣiṇī; greatness of the Piśācakatīrtha; description of the greatness of the Śiprāguṃpheśvaratīrtha; description of the greatness of Agastyeśvara; description of the greatness of Ḍhuṇḍheśvara; description of the greatness of Ḍamarukeśvara; description of the greatness of Anādikalpeśvara; description of the greatness of Siddheśvara, Vīrabhadra, and Caṇḍikā; description of the greatness of the Svarṇajāleśvaratīrtha; description of the greatness of Mahāmāyā; description of the greatness of Kapāleśvara; description of the greatness of the pilgrimage to the Svargadvāratīrtha. 18 2

6.1.s: 21 hanumatkeśvaramāhātmyavarṇane rāvaṇavadhānantaraṃ rāmādīnāmayodhyāyāṃ gamanam, tatra rājyābhiṣekavarṇanam, ligaṃ yācituṃ hanumatā laṃkāṃ gatvā vibhīṣaṇājñayā liṃgaṃ gṛhītvā'vantyāmāgamanama, sarastīre liṃgaṃ saṃsthāpya hanumataḥ snānakaraṇam, snānānte liṅgasyā'calanaṃ dṛṣṭvā śivājñayā tatraiva tasya liṅgasya sthāpanam, hanumatkeśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanam. 19 1
6.1.d: 21 हनुमत्केश्वरमाहात्म्यवर्णने रावणवधानन्तरं रामादीनामयोध्यायां गमनम्, तत्र राज्याभिषेकवर्णनम्, लिगं याचितुं हनुमता लंकां गत्वा विभीषणाज्ञया लिंगं गृहीत्वाऽवन्त्यामागमनम, सरस्तीरे लिंगं संस्थाप्य हनुमतः स्नानकरणम्, स्नानान्ते लिङ्गस्याऽचलनं दृष्ट्वा शिवाज्ञया तत्रैव तस्य लिङ्गस्य स्थापनम्, हनुमत्केश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्. 19 1
6.1.m: 21. In the description of the greatness of Hanumatkeśvara: Rāma and the others go to Ayodhyā after the slaying of Rāvaṇa; description of the royal consecration there; Hanumān's going to Laṅkā to ask for a liṅga and coming to Avantī after taking the liṅga by Vibhīṣaṇa's command; Hanumān's taking a ritual ablution after setting down the liṅga on the shore of the lake; seeing the immobility of the liṅga at the end of the ritual ablution and installing that liṅga in that very place by Śiva's command; description of the greatness of the Hanumatkeśvaratīrtha. 19 1
22. Description of the greatness of Yameśvara; description of the greatness of the Rudrasaras. 19 2
23. Description of the pilgrimage to Mahākāla; description of the greatness of the pilgrimage. 19 2

6.1.s:
24 sumatināmakabrāhmaṇasya kaiśikapatnyāṃ jātasyāgniśarmaṇaḥ kumārasyā'bhyāsatyāgavarṇanam, agniśarmakṛtaduṣṭasaṃgativarṇanam, nityaprāṇihiṃsanaśīlatvātsaptarṣīnāgatāndṛṣṭvā'gniśarmaṇā tadvadhopāyakaraṇam, atrivacanādgṛhaṃ gatvā tasya pāpabhāgitvena svaparivāraṃ prati praśnakaraṇam, tatastairgṛhasthitaiḥ pitrādibhiḥ pāpaphalabhogasyāsvīkaraṇaṃ śrutvā'gniśarmaṇā paścāttāpaṃ kṛtvā maharṣīnprati śaraṇaṃ gatvā prārthanākaraṇam,
tato'trimaharṣidattamantrasyopāsanātpāpaniṣkṛtivarṇanam, tataḥ kālāṃtareṇa valmīkasambhavādvālmīkiriti maharṣibhistasyābhidhānakaraṇam, tena vālmīkinā kuśasthalīṃ gatvā śivamārādhya svanāmnā liṃgasthāpanam, vālmīkīśvaramāhātmyavarṇanam 20 2
6.1.d:
24 सुमतिनामकब्राह्मणस्य कैशिकपत्न्यां जातस्याग्निशर्मणः कुमारस्याऽभ्यासत्यागवर्णनम्, अग्निशर्मकृतदुष्टसंगतिवर्णनम्, नित्यप्राणिहिंसनशीलत्वात्सप्तर्षीनागतान्दृष्ट्वाऽग्निशर्मणा तद्वधोपायकरणम्, अत्रिवचनाद्गृहं गत्वा तस्य पापभागित्वेन स्वपरिवारं प्रति प्रश्नकरणम्, ततस्तैर्गृहस्थितैः पित्रादिभिः पापफलभोगस्यास्वीकरणं श्रुत्वाऽग्निशर्मणा पश्चात्तापं कृत्वा महर्षीन्प्रति शरणं गत्वा प्रार्थनाकरणम्,
ततोऽत्रिमहर्षिदत्तमन्त्रस्योपासनात्पापनिष्कृतिवर्णनम्, ततः कालांतरेण वल्मीकसम्भवाद्वाल्मीकिरिति महर्षिभिस्तस्याभिधानकरणम्, तेन वाल्मीकिना कुशस्थलीं गत्वा शिवमाराध्य स्वनाम्ना लिंगस्थापनम्, वाल्मीकीश्वरमाहात्म्यवर्णनम् 20 2
6.1.m: 24. Description of the boy Agniśarman, born to the brahmin named Sumati through his wife Kaiśikī, abandoning his studies; description of the bad company kept by Agniśarman; because of his habitual harming of living beings, his devising a means to slay the seven seers upon seeing them arrive; his going home by the word of Atri and questioning his family regarding their sharing in his sin; then, upon hearing the refusal of his father and others living at home to experience the fruit of the sin, Agniśarman's repentance and seeking refuge and making a supplication to the great seers; then the description of his expiation from sin through worship with the mantra given by the great seer Atri; then, after a passage of time, the great seers giving him the name Vālmīki because of his emergence from an ant-hill; after that Vālmīki went to Kuśasthalī, worshipped Śiva, and installed a liṅga under his own name; description of the greatness of Vālmīkīśvara. 20 2
25. Description of the greatness of the tīrthas Śukreśvara, Bhīmeśvara, Gargeśvara, Kāmeśvara, Cūḍāmaṇīśvara, Caṇḍīśvara, and others. 21 2

Description of the greatness of Kālavana together with its beauty; description of the greatness of the deities beginning with Piṅgaleśa situated in all directions around Kālavana; description of the greatness of the seven kalpas; greatness of the pilgrimage to the five Īśānas; greatness of Akrūreśvara; description of the greatness of Brahmakuṇḍa; description of the greatness of the Mandākinītīrtha. 21 2

6.1.d: 27 अंकपादाख्यस्थानमाहात्म्यवर्णने बलरामकृष्णयोर्जन्मकर्मनिरूपणम्, सांदीपनये गुरुदक्षिणां दातुं प्रवृत्तयोस्तयो रामकृष्णयोः समुद्रस्थं शंखासुरं हत्वा यमलोके गमनम्, तत्र यमस्य पराजयं कृत्वा सांदीपनिपुत्रं गृहीत्वा तयोर्गुरुसमीप आगमनम्, अवंत्यामङ्कपादाख्ये लिंगस्थापनम्, मूर्तिपञ्चकमाहात्म्यवर्णनम, ... 24 1
6.1.m: 27 Description of the māhātmya of the place called Aṅkapāda: account of the birth and deeds of Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa; when those two, Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, set out to offer the preceptor's fee to Sāndīpani, their killing of the demon Śaṅkha residing in the ocean and going to the realm of Yama; there defeating Yama, taking Sāndīpani's son, and their returning to their guru; installation of a liṅga at the place named Aṅkapāda in Avantī; description of the māhātmya of the five mūrtis ... 24 1

6.1.s: 28 candrādityamāhātmyam, karabheśvaramāhātmyam, gaṇeśamāhātmyam, kusumeśvarajayeśvarayormāhātmyavarṇanam, śivadvāramāhātmyavarṇanam, mārkaṇḍeyeśvaramāhātmyavarṇanam, brahme- śvaramāhātmyama, brahmāṇīkuṇḍamāhātmyam, yakṣavāpīmāhātmyam, paśupatirudrapura rūpakuṃḍakedārakuṃḍakarīkuṃḍājāgaṃdhacakratīrthādimāhātmyavarṇanam, somavatīliṃgaso meśvaraliṃgamāhātmyavarṇanam ... ....26 2

6.1.m: 28 Māhātmya of Candrāditya; māhātmya of Karabheśvara; māhātmya of Gaṇeśa; description of the māhātmya of Kusumeśvara and Jayeśvara; description of the māhātmya of Śivadvāra; description of the māhātmya of Mārkaṇḍeyeśvara; māhātmya of Brahmeśvara; māhātmya of Brahmāṇīkuṇḍa; māhātmya of Yakṣavāpī; description of the māhātmya of Paśupati, Rudrapura, Rūpakuṇḍa, Kedārakuṇḍa, Karīkuṇḍa, Ajāgandha, Cakratīrtha, and others; description of the māhātmya of the Somavatīliṅga and Someśvaraliṅga ... 26 2

6.1.d: 29 अनरकतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनम, तत्प्रसंगेन नरकवर्णनं नरकयातनादिकानां च वर्णनम्, नरकाप्राप्तिसाधनकथनं च. ............. 29 1
6.1.m: 29 Description of the māhātmya of the Anarakatīrtha; in that context, description of hell, tortures of hell, and so forth; and statement of the means to avoid hell ... 29 1

30 In the Anarakatīrtha, statement of the māhātmya of offering lamps; statement of the ritual rules for worship there; statement of the attainment of increase in virility, splendour, and so forth by offering lamps ... 29 2

6.1.s: 31 kedāreśvaratīrthamāhātmyavarṇanam – jaṭātīrtha śuṃgatīrthendratīrtha caṃdreśvarakuṇḍeśvaragopatīrtha cipiṭātīrthānaṃdeśvara rāmeśvarāditīrtha māhātmyavarṇanama, tatra rāmeṇa piturdaśarathasya śrāddhakarmakaraṇam, saubhāgyatīrtha ghṛtatīrtha yogaśvarīdevīśaṃkhāvartasudhodakasudheśvara kiṃpunatīrtha pattaneśvara durdharṣasthaviravināyaka kāmodakāditīrtha māhātmyavarṇanam 32 1
6.1.d: 31 केदारेश्वरतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनम् – जटातीर्थ शुंगतीर्थेन्द्रतीर्थ चंद्रेश्वरकुण्डेश्वरगोपतीर्थ चिपिटातीर्थानंदेश्वर रामेश्वरादितीर्थ माहात्म्यवर्णनम, तत्र रामेण पितुर्दशरथस्य श्राद्धकर्मकरणम्, सौभाग्यतीर्थ घृततीर्थ योगश्वरीदेवीशंखावर्तसुधोदकसुधेश्वर किंपुनतीर्थ पत्तनेश्वर दुर्धर्षस्थविरविनायक कामोदकादितीर्थ माहात्म्यवर्णनम् 32 1

6.1.m: 43 In Ujjayinī, the demon Tripura performing austerity directed towards Brahmā; Brahmā granting a boon to him; Indra and the other gods afflicted by the demon Tripura going before Śiva; Śiva granting them safety; Indra and the others worshipping Cāmuṇḍā in Avantī by Śiva's command; Śiva defeating the Daitya at Cāmuṇḍā's word; description of the renown of that city under the name Ujjayinī because the Dānava Tripura was conquered there; description of the Ujjayinīmāhātmya ... 45

6.1.s: 49 kapāladhāriṇaḥ śivasya vaikuṇṭhe bhikṣārthaṃ gamanam, bhikṣādānasamaye viṣṇoraṃgulyāṃ śivena śūlena prahāre kṛte vipṇoraṃgulito'sṛkpravāhanirgamanam, tasyaiva pravāhasya nadīrūpeṇa pariṇatasya śiprānāmnā prasiddhikathanam, bāṇāsurakṛṣṇayuddhavarṇanam, tatra śivaviṣṇvoryuddhe mithostrapreṣaṇam, śaivajvaravaiṣṇavajvarayormadhye śaivajvarasya parābhavavarṇanam, tasya sthānasya jvaraghnīti nāmnā prasiddhivarṇanama, jvaraghnītīrthamāhātmyavarṇanam. -....... ... ......... 51 1
6.1.d: 49 कपालधारिणः शिवस्य वैकुण्ठे भिक्षार्थं गमनम्, भिक्षादानसमये विष्णोरंगुल्यां शिवेन शूलेन प्रहारे कृते विप्णोरंगुलितोऽसृक्प्रवाहनिर्गमनम्, तस्यैव प्रवाहस्य नदीरूपेण परिणतस्य शिप्रानाम्ना प्रसिद्धिकथनम्, बाणासुरकृष्णयुद्धवर्णनम्, तत्र शिवविष्ण्वोर्युद्धे मिथोस्त्रप्रेषणम्, शैवज्वरवैष्णवज्वरयोर्मध्ये शैवज्वरस्य पराभववर्णनम्, तस्य स्थानस्य ज्वरघ्नीति नाम्ना प्रसिद्धिवर्णनम, ज्वरघ्नीतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्. -....... ... ......... 51 1
6.1.m: 49 Śiva the skull-bearer going to Vaikuṇṭha for alms; when a blow was struck with a trident by Śiva on Viṣṇu's finger at the time of giving alms, an outflow of a stream of blood from Viṣṇu's finger; statement of the renown of that very stream transformed into the form of a river under the name Śiprā; description of the war between the demon Bāṇa and Kṛṣṇa; the mutual hurling of weapons in the battle between Śiva and Viṣṇu there; description of the defeat of the Śaiva fever between the Śaiva fever and the Vaiṣṇava fever; description of that place's fame under the name Jvaraghnī; description of the māhātmya of the Jvaraghnītīrtha ... 51 1

6.1.m: 50. In the context of describing the Pāpanāśinī sacred ford: King Damana, who acted unrighteously, goes to the forest for hunting; tying his horse to a banyan tree at night, the king falls asleep right there; then a snake falls onto the king's head; the messengers of Yama arrive before him as he suffers from snakebite; then, when the king goes to the world of Yama, at the time of his torment by Yama, flesh from his body eaten by crows falls into the Śiprā; through that merit, Damana goes to the world of Śiva; description of the māhātmya of the Śiprā in the dialogue between Yama and the messengers of Yama. 52.1

6.1.m: 51. Śiva's journey to the world of the serpents for alms; due to not obtaining alms, his drinking of all the nectar situated in the twenty-one pools there, whereupon the frightened serpents praise Vāsuki; all the serpents go to the Śiprā and offer praise to Śiva; pleased by this, the Lord establishes a pool named Amṛtodbhava there; description of the māhātmya of Amṛtodbhavā. 53.1
